summary: Ingrid Hilmer works in literature education and sustainability education, focusing on how children's fiction can be used to teach about sustainable development. Her publications analyse Norwegian children's novels, including Arne Svingen's En himmel full av skyer, through literary analysis and didactic discussion, looking at wicked problems and at children's agency in environmental and climate issues. The work relates to school teaching and to how pupils may come to understand sustainability challenges through reading literature.

name: Ingunn Eikeland
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Ingunn Eikeland studies how schools respond to student diversity, with a focus on differentiation and adapted education. Her work includes a configurative review of 28 international papers that maps different ways differentiation is framed, and a study of school leaders' views on pupil diversity. The research applies to school organization, education policy and inclusive teaching practice.

name: Irina Diaz de Leon
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Irina Diaz de Leon studies eating disorders and disordered eating in athletes, including how coaches recognise symptoms. Her work translates and validates a questionnaire into Norwegian, using factor analysis on survey data from over 300 coaches to examine which symptoms they observe and how this relates to coaching experience. She also appears to work on workplace physical activity interventions and their effects on health-related quality of life.

name: James Jacob Thomson
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: James Jacob Thomson studies English academic and pupil writing, with a focus on how writers use metadiscourse features such as signposts to mark relations between parts of a text. His work uses corpus methods, including concordancing of essays from Swedish, Norwegian and British upper secondary schools, combined with teacher interviews. The publications also touch on assessment practices and on phraseology in academic language, with applications in writing instruction and language teaching.

name: Janne Fauskanger
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Janne Fauskanger studies mathematics teacher education and professional development, with a focus on problem-solving tasks, core teaching practices, and teachers' beliefs and narratives. Her work uses mixed-methods and qualitative designs, including logbooks, focus groups, discussion analysis, conceptual analysis of teaching tasks, and observation-instrument validation with Delphi and generalizability methods. Application areas include Norwegian primary and lower secondary schools, preservice teacher preparation, technology integration (TPACK), and research-practice partnerships.

name: Kari Vestbø
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Kari Vestbø appears in the available record with a single 2024 publication, written in Norwegian, whose title translates roughly as "What you read in the curriculum can sometimes be hard to picture." The title points to an interest in education, particularly how students understand and visualise course material. No abstract or methods were provided, so the research approach and application domains cannot be described in more detail.

name: Kari-Anne Svensen Malmo
department: Department of Education and Sports Science

name: Karsten Øvretveit
department: Department of Education and Sports Science

name: Ketil Fred Hansen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Ketil Fred Hansen studies politics, security and military institutions in Central Africa and the Sahel, with a main focus on Chad. His work examines the armed forces of Chad, Cameroon and the Central African Republic, the 2021 constitutional coup after Idriss Déby's death, and security in the Lake Chad area. He also writes on postcolonial critique and the decolonisation of academia in Norway, using analysis of curriculum content and public debate.

name: Kimble Lee Walsh-Knarvik
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Kimble Lee Walsh-Knarvik studies how immigrant perspectives and lived experiences are included or left out of social studies teaching in Norwegian upper secondary schools. The work uses a community-based participatory approach, developing and describing a classroom workshop with university researchers, teachers, pupils and a local museum. It focuses on inclusive, strength-based pedagogy that challenges dominant deficit views of immigration, with relevance for educators across the Nordic region.

name: Kitty Marie Garborg
department: Department of Education and Sports Science

name: Kjersti Melhus
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Kjersti Melhus works on primary school mathematics education in Norway, as shown by textbooks and teacher guides for grades 3 and 4 (Matematikk series, 2022–2024). She also has a publication on the equals sign, a topic in early mathematics learning. Her work focuses on teaching materials and classroom support for young pupils and their teachers.

name: Kristine Marie Olsen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Kristine Marie Olsen researches science education and teacher education, with a focus on play-based science teaching in primary school and on interdisciplinary learning that links home economics with STEAM subjects. Her work includes a collaborative partnership project between a school and a teacher education institution, framed as a community of inquiry, and an Erasmus+ project producing a handbook of 20 learning activities on everyday sustainability. A further publication addresses how young children can gain insight into interactions in nature using bumblebees as a study subject.

name: Lars Rune Waage
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Lars Rune Waage works in children's literature research, with a focus on close reading of recent Norwegian picture books, book series and works by authors and illustrators. The publication is an anthology that combines research articles with essays by writers and illustrators, intended to show approaches to analysing children's literature. It is aimed at researchers, students, teachers, librarians and others who work to encourage children's reading enjoyment.

name: Magne Ivar Drangeid
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Magne Ivar Drangeid studies literature and literature teaching, combining ecocritical readings of travel writing, nature writing and poetry (including Olav H. Hauge) with classroom-based work in teacher education. His projects use place-based writing, literary mapping, poetic and narrative inquiry and dialogic teaching, often on outdoor hikes, to examine how student teachers notice and respond to their environment through the idea of affordance-ability. He also writes essays on higher education pedagogy, such as the value of the lecture, from a post-critical perspective, and on sustainability education.

name: Magne Ove Rogne
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Magne Ove Rogne studies Norwegian as a school and teacher-education subject, using historical and comparative analysis of curricula from the 1970s to the present. His work examines how language and cultural diversity, cross-curricular themes and the structure of the current curriculum (L20) are treated, drawing on paradigm theory for first-language subjects. He also analyses Norwegian-subject teaching materials, including digital reading and the treatment of artificial intelligence, through text theory and close-reading content analysis.

name: Marianne Sandvik Tveitnes
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Marianne Sandvik Tveitnes studies inclusive education and special needs education in Norway, looking at teachers' professional knowledge, the work of educational-psychological services, and the mentoring of newly qualified teachers. Her work uses large-scale surveys with structural equation modelling alongside interviews, focus groups and thematic or content analysis. She also writes on inclusion in working life for people with cognitive support needs, children's participation, interprofessional collaboration, and partnerships and case-based approaches in teacher education.

name: Marie Smith-Solbakken
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Marie Smith-Solbakken studies how people and communities experienced and dealt with the 1980 Alexander L. Kielland disaster in the North Sea, including local responses in the Førresfjorden community and the later handling of the aftermath. Her work draws on retrospective interviews and written sources, using microhistorical and polyphonic methods. She also writes about the use of archival sources in teacher education to support deeper learning.

name: Marieke Gerdien Bruin
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Marieke Gerdien Bruin studies inclusion, participation and social justice in education, with a focus on vocational education and training (VET) for young people at risk of social exclusion, as well as primary schools and municipal arts and music schools in Norway. Her work relies mainly on qualitative interviews analysed thematically, cross-national comparison with the Baltic countries, and co-creative intervention studies with teachers, and it draws on recognition theory, sociocultural theory and social capital. She also examines how education policy places responsibility on parents, and she writes on qualitative research methods and transparency in academic writing.

name: Merete Hagen Helland
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Merete Hagen Helland studies the school subject Food and Health and school meals in Norwegian primary schools. Her work uses interviews, focus groups, content and thematic analysis, and meal photography with statistical comparison to examine how the subject is taught and prioritized, how students experience it, and how lunch type and family affluence relate to meal quality. She also develops and studies interdisciplinary teaching approaches, including STEAM activities and peer teaching with outdoor life, in teacher education.

name: Mette Irene Hvalby
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Mette Irene Hvalby studies teacher education in Norway, focusing on how students' professional suitability is assessed, supervised and developed, and on mentoring of pre-service and newly qualified teachers. Her work uses qualitative methods such as focus groups, in-depth interviews and thematic analysis, alongside surveys and mixed-methods designs, including evaluations of simulation to build critical thinking. Application areas include practicum supervision, teacher induction and well-being, inclusive education, and the use of artificial intelligence in student guidance.

name: Milica Savic
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Milica Savic studies second language pragmatics with young learners of English, especially how children in Norway and Cyprus understand and judge politeness, requests and speech acts. Her work relies on group interviews, task-based discussions and other participant-centred methods, analysed thematically and across age groups. She also researches critical visual literacy and multimodal texts in English language teaching and teacher education, including redesign tasks used with secondary school learners and pre-service teachers.

name: Milla Saara Anneli Saarinen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Milla Saara Anneli Saarinen studies the psychosocial development of young athletes, including how achievement goals, perceived performance and athletic identity relate to self-esteem among student-athletes in Norwegian lower secondary sport schools, using survey data and regression-based conditional process analysis. She also works on higher education teaching in sport and exercise science, examining how technology-enhanced learning and artificial intelligence can be designed to include dual-career athletes, international students and neurodivergent learners. Her work links motivation theory and pedagogical frameworks to practice in youth sport and university education.

name: Miriam Byberg
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Miriam Byberg studies training load management and athlete monitoring in elite women's football. Her work uses online surveys of players, coaches and performance staff in Norwegian Premier League clubs to describe how monitoring data are collected, analysed and used, and to identify practical barriers and facilitators. Her publications also address how female footballers are trained compared with approaches designed for male players.

name: Morten Ugelid Søyland
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Morten Ugelid Søyland studies mathematics education and teacher education in Norway, with a focus on assessment and student prior knowledge. His work includes a quantitative study of how pre-service teachers' basic mathematical knowledge relates to their university mathematics results, and interview research on how experienced teachers understand the practical element of the new oral-practical exam in mathematics and science. He has also contributed to national seminars on learning, assessment and examination in mathematics for primary and lower secondary teacher education.

name: Nils Olav Østrem
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Nils Olav Østrem studies Norwegian emigration history and local history in Rogaland and the Haugalandet region, with particular attention to emigrant letters, women emigrants, and early migration to America. His work, including an analysis of emotional expression in Norwegian-American immigrant letters from 1838 to 1848, draws on archival sources and is also presented through biographical sketches, local yearbook articles, source presentations and public lectures. Other topics include the tenant-farmer (husmann) system, church and religious figures, and the social history of Vindafjord and nearby communities.

name: Nina Helgevold
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Nina Helgevold studies teacher professional development and teacher education, with a strong focus on Lesson Study in Norway, Malawi and online or hybrid settings. Her work uses case studies, interviews, surveys, focus groups and content analysis to examine what sustains Lesson Study in schools, how student voice is included, and how teachers' views of mathematics teaching change. She also researches digital problem-based cases for student teachers, school-university partnerships on play-based science teaching, and classroom management in technology-rich primary classrooms.

name: Nina Lazarevic
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Nina Lazarevic studies English language teaching and teacher education, with a focus on materials design, including materials created by pre-service teachers and by young learners to support writing development. Her work also covers grammar teaching in in-service professional development, CLIL teachers' attitudes in Serbia, and intercultural learning and communicative competence on international campuses in the US and Norway. Methods in the publications include qualitative interviews, thematic and content analysis, and mixed-methods designs, applied in primary, secondary and teacher education settings.

name: Nina Sømme Kvarstein
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Nina Sømme Kvarstein studies physical education and teacher learning in school settings. Her publications look at how pupils describe lessons they find problematic in physical education, and at how facilitators shape teachers' exploratory discussion about embodied learning during the Kyouzai Kenkyuu phase of lesson study. Her work centres on pupil experience and on collaborative professional development for teachers.

name: Ole-Vinjar Egeland
department: Department of Education and Sports Science

name: Paolo Haaland Scarbocci
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Paolo Haaland Scarbocci works on education and digital media, with a focus on videogames as literary experiences and their use in teaching and teacher education. His publications also cover coding and algorithmic thinking in Minecraft Education Edition, student participation in schools, and the balance between handwriting and keyboard use in the classroom. The work is oriented toward school and teacher-training practice, mainly in a Norwegian context.

name: Pauline Book
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Pauline Book studies how pupils, especially multilingual learners in primary and middle school, create meaning in science through writing, drawing, dialogue and multimodal representations. Her work uses qualitative case studies, content analysis, social semiotic frameworks and literature reviews to examine wonder, identity texts, agency and resource-oriented teaching. She also investigates interdisciplinary collaboration among teacher educators for education for sustainable development in Norwegian teacher education.

name: Pia Susanne Wall
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Pia Susanne Wall works on arts-based and participatory approaches to sustainability and change in higher education, using utopian future workshops to reimagine and physically transform underused campus spaces. Her work draws on American pragmatist thinking and examines how collaboration among diverse stakeholders and links between research and practice can support organizational and cultural change. She also takes part in art-subject collaborations with teacher educators in visual arts and music, involving exhibitions and exploratory processes in teacher education.

name: Radel James Eumague Gacumo
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Radel James Eumague Gacumo studies early childhood literacy, focusing on how gender, equity and inclusion are shaped through picturebooks, digital books, and animated films. The work uses critical sensory multimodal literacy, queer theory and close multimodal reading, together with case studies, interviews, a scoping review and an experimental study of children's engagement with scent-enhanced digital books in Norwegian kindergartens. Further publications address queer media and drag in the Philippines, inclusion in Norway's cultural sector, and collaborative autoethnography with Asian queer researchers.

name: Raymond Bjuland
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Raymond Bjuland studies mathematics teaching and teacher professional development, focusing on problem-solving tasks, the work of monitoring students' mathematical thinking, teacher noticing, and teachers' professional identities and narratives. His methods include discourse and commognitive analysis, conceptual analysis of tasks of teaching, thematic analysis and quantitative text analysis, applied to lesson study, research-practice partnerships and thinking classrooms in Norwegian schools. He also examines pre-service teacher knowledge in low-resource Malawian primary classrooms and the structure of multiplication tasks in Norwegian textbooks.

name: Reidar Mosvold
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Reidar Mosvold studies mathematics teaching and teacher learning, with a focus on teacher questioning, talk moves, monitoring of student thinking, and problem-solving tasks in Norwegian schools. His work draws on classroom video, co-planning and co-enactment sessions, logbooks, interviews and observation instruments, and also uses conceptual analysis, mixed methods, and computational text analysis. Application areas include professional development programmes, research-practice partnerships, initial teacher education, technology integration, and the assessment of teaching quality.

name: Sander Vossgård Eriksen Mathisrud
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Sander Vossgård Eriksen Mathisrud studies how partnership is understood and used in Norwegian education, with a focus on education policy and teacher education. His work appears to analyse policy and steering documents to examine how partnership moves from an ideal to a tool of governance, including links to competence development. He has also produced work on writing exercises, dialogue and presenting texts in progress.

name: Sanna Pauliina Törmälä-Tranberg
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Sanna Pauliina Törmälä-Tranberg studies music teacher education in Norway, focusing on how far programmes prepare student teachers for inclusive music education in diverse classrooms. Her work analyses curriculum documents and course plans and considers students' practical experience of inclusion. A further publication looks at voice as a shared space for connection, pointing to an interest in vocal and relational aspects of music-making.

name: Sara Sedberg
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Sara Sedberg's work, as shown by a 2026 round table titled "Creating with GenAI: Agency and Representation", relates to generative AI in creative practice. The title points to interest in questions of creative agency and how people and ideas are represented when GenAI tools are used. Only a title is available, so her specific methods and application domains cannot be described in more detail.

name: Sebastian Schanche Sandgren
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Sebastian Schanche Sandgren studies eating disorders, disordered eating and muscle dysmorphia among athletes and people who do resistance training, mainly in Norway. His work uses surveys with factor analysis and regression, interviews and focus groups analysed thematically, a systematic review, and feasibility testing of interventions built with intervention mapping. Application areas include questionnaire development for coaches and sport professionals, support and self-help resources for athletes, weight management in combat sports, and athlete monitoring in women's football.

name: Shaher Ahmmad Ibrahim Shalfawi
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Shaher Ahmmad Ibrahim Shalfawi studies physical activity, training load and injury prevention in children, student athletes and elite soccer players, mainly in Norway. His work uses randomised controlled trials, longitudinal and cross-sectional questionnaire studies, and accelerometer measurement to examine training distress, perceived exertion, injury prevalence, team communication and physical performance. Application areas include kindergarten play, sports academy high schools, and team sport coaching and athlete management.

name: Silje Eikanger Kvalø
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Silje Eikanger Kvalø works on education research spanning higher education programme development, teacher learning and physically active learning in schools. Her publications address the design of a new study programme in extended education pedagogy for after-school care, the use of situated learning theory, and teacher talk about embodied learning in a lesson-study-style setting. She also evaluates a school-based physical activity programme, looking at its effects, participants' experiences and how it was implemented.

name: Silje Henriette Amalia Normand
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Silje Henriette Amalia Normand researches teacher education, English language teaching and migration, with a focus on diversity, democratic citizenship and inclusion. Her work combines qualitative interviews, survey-based project findings and arts-based methods such as drama tableaux and critical literacy practices. She applies these in schools, teacher education and migrant labour-market contexts, including credential recognition and skills pathways for migrant teachers and workers in Norway.

name: Sindre Mikal Dyrstad
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Sindre Mikal Dyrstad studies physical activity and exercise as tools for health promotion across settings, including opioid agonist therapy clinics, schools, workplaces and Healthy Life Centres. His work combines randomized and pilot trials, systematic reviews, cross-sectional and observational studies, and interviews, with outcomes such as fitness, psychological distress, quality of life and motivation. He also examines school-based physically active learning, teacher implementation and student motivation in education, and writes popular articles on active lifestyles.

name: Sofija Christensen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Sofija Christensen researches literature didactics, with a focus on dialogic literature teaching and how student teachers discuss literary excerpts such as a passage from Orwell's 1984 in book talks. She also analyzes bilingual Sámi–Norwegian picture books as fables, drawing on picturebook research and ecocritical fable theory to explore their use in Sámi pedagogy and language and literature education. A further strand examines motivation, emotions, identity and learning outcomes among international students learning Norwegian as a second language.

name: Sofija Svendsen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Sofija Svendsen studies children's literature, focusing on bilingual Sámi-Norwegian picture books and their use in literature education. Her work applies picturebook research, multilingual picturebook studies and ecocritical fable theory to interpret animal stories that raise questions of identity and belonging. She links this textual analysis to Sámi pedagogy and to teaching Norwegian and Sámi language and literature.

name: Tanu Biswas
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Tanu Biswas works on childism, a critical approach that challenges adult-centred and colonial assumptions about children, applying it to education, philosophy of childhood and climate justice. Her work uses conceptual and philosophical analysis, textbook critique, ethnographic study of children's play and slow post-qualitative research with children, and also covers children's climate activism and school strikes. Application areas include teacher education in Norway, children's participation rights, intergenerational sustainability and the development of an adultcentrism measurement scale.

name: Tarja Irene Tikkanen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Tarja Irene Tikkanen studies skills formation, vocational education and training, and workplace learning, with a focus on groups at risk of exclusion such as vulnerable youth and migrant workers. Her work combines comparative policy and document analysis, surveys, qualitative interviews and machine learning, covering the Baltic countries and Norway as well as wider cross-country comparisons. Application areas include dropout prevention and school-to-work transition in VET, credential recognition and skill mismatch among migrants, teacher professional development and digital competence, and gaming in schools.

name: Thomas Bjørnsen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Thomas Bjørnsen studies strength and conditioning and sports science, covering resistance training methods, jump and power testing, blood flow restriction exercise and athlete monitoring. His work uses randomized crossover and intervention trials, EMG, force-plate and motion-capture measurement, simulation modelling, and systematic reviews with meta-analyses. The applications include supplements such as citrulline malate and caffeine, placebo effects, and training and match-load monitoring in football, ice hockey, handball, TeamGym, kayak and swimming.

name: Tord Austdal
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Tord Austdal studies the skills, labour market experiences and mobility pathways of migrant workers in Norway as part of a Horizon Europe project on skill partnerships and migration. The work combines survey data with qualitative accounts and policy analysis to examine skill mismatch, overqualification, credential recognition, discrimination and perceived fairness at work. It also covers integration policy and sectoral labour demand, with a focus on workers from outside the EU.

name: Tore Dreyer
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Tore Dreyer studies mathematics education in Norway, with a focus on how school textbooks present content to teachers and pupils. One publication analyses how quadrilaterals are defined across Norwegian primary and lower secondary textbooks, checking whether definitions are correct and consistent between textbook series. Another publication concerns a method for practising dialogue-based teaching, pointing to an interest in teaching practice and teacher training.

name: Vegard Moen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Vegard Moen studies teaching, learning and organisation in education, with a focus on Norwegian higher education, teacher education and schools. His work uses comparative case studies, institutional course and examination data, surveys, interviews and focus groups to examine learning management system rollout, class size and grading, and problem-based casework for student teachers. He also researches inclusive practice, school leadership and collaboration between schools and the educational and psychological counselling service, and the support of vulnerable youth in vocational education.

name: Vibeke Klovning
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Vibeke Klovning researches how pragmatics in a second language can be taught to young learners of English as a foreign language, with a focus on primary-school pupils in Norway. Her work looks at instructional approaches such as picture books, collaborative classroom activities and metapragmatic reflection, and at how teaching affects learners' use of request strategies. The studies are classroom-based and relevant to early English language teaching and teacher education.

name: Vidar Kjetilstad
department: Department of Education and Sports Science

name: Wenche Olivia Sigurdsen
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Wenche Olivia Sigurdsen studies teaching, learning and assessment in school physical education, with a focus on how teachers use pedagogical models and how effort is understood and assessed in lessons. Her work combines action research, classroom observation, 360-degree video, stimulated recall interviews and teacher narratives with thematic analysis, and includes a systematic scoping review of research on teaching approaches. The studies are set in Norwegian secondary schools and address student-centered teaching, curriculum demands and the practical constraints teachers face.

name: Åge Vigane
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Åge Vigane studies outdoor education and friluftsliv in higher education and teacher education, using mainly qualitative methods such as questionnaires, interviews and thematic analysis, along with a small randomized pilot study. His work covers resilience, environmental awareness, intercultural learning, interdisciplinary peer teaching and the development of outdoor leadership skills through feedback. His publications also include practical course and training material on first aid, life-saving, resuscitation, safety and self-rescue, as well as ball-based outdoor activities and teacher education.

name: Åsmund Hennig
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Åsmund Hennig studies literature education in Norwegian schools and teacher education, focusing on how pupils and student teachers talk about and respond to literary texts. His work analyses recorded classroom and student conversations, including literature circles and discussions of short stories and fiction about moral dilemmas, to understand dialogic teaching and literary competence. It also considers student teachers' reading experiences and the didactic implications for planning literature lessons.

name: Åsmund Lillevik Gjære
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Åsmund Lillevik Gjære studies how primary school mathematics teachers put a reform-oriented approach, Developmental Education in Mathematics (based on Zankov's and Vygotsky's ideas), into practice in Norway. Using qualitative case studies, classroom video, and focus group interviews, the work examines challenging tasks, teacher questioning, teaching dilemmas and depth of implementation. It also covers teacher professional development, and includes practice-oriented writing on mathematics teaching, classroom dialogue and thinking classrooms.

name: Øystein Nybøe
department: Department of Education and Sports Science
summary: Øystein Nybøe studies teacher-student interactions in Norwegian primary school classrooms, using Honneth's recognition theory to understand how relationships, belonging and inclusive communities develop. His work draws on interviews with teachers and students, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis, and looks at qualities such as care, trust, respect and appreciation as ways of creating space for student participation. He also shares this research with school leaders and practitioners through talks and professional-oriented publications on recognition and relationships in schools.

name: Ann Kristin Kolstø-Johansen
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Ann Kristin Kolstø-Johansen studies classroom teaching quality in upper secondary education, focusing on whether a widely used classroom observation instrument works in Norwegian schools. Her work uses video-recorded lessons scored by certified raters and applies two-level statistical models to nested data from academic and vocational classrooms to examine the instrument's structure and reliability. The findings also relate teaching quality dimensions to study track and teacher characteristics.

name: Beate Mellemsether
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Beate Mellemsether studies inclusive education in secondary schools, focusing on minority students and students with special educational needs. Using qualitative case studies, focus groups, interviews, classroom observation and student surveys, the work examines bullying within and across cultural groups, teacher instructional and emotional support, and teacher attitudes. The findings are applied to school practice, teacher training and policy in culturally diverse Norwegian and other educational settings.

name: Birgit Rodvelt
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Birgit Rodvelt researches early literacy in children, covering reading assessment, handwriting and text writing. The publications address how teachers' judgments compare with results from screening tests, how writing tools are used in schools, what affects pupils' motivation to write, and how writing fluency relates to letter connection. Her work also touches on play and learning in kindergarten, with a focus on educational practice in early schooling.

name: Bjørn Olav Skjæveland
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)

name: Bo Bernhard Randulff
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Bo Bernhard Randulff has a 2024 publication titled "LES FOR MEG: Å se alt som blir rett" (Norwegian for roughly "Read for me: seeing everything that becomes right"). Only the title is available, with no abstract or other publications, so the specific research areas, methods and application domains cannot be determined from the material provided. A fuller description would require additional publication details.

name: Dagmar Strohmeier
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Dagmar Strohmeier studies bullying, cyberbullying, ethnic victimization and teacher bullying among children and adolescents, along with school-based prevention programs and how bullying is measured across countries. Her work also covers immigrant adolescents' school achievement, aspirations and well-being, and adolescents' digital career aspirations and pro-environmental behavior. She mainly uses longitudinal and multilevel survey designs, cross-lagged panel models, structural equation modeling, person-oriented and social network analyses, and a cluster randomized evaluation, within a socio-ecological framework.

name: Eija Kristiina Pakarinen
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Eija Kristiina Pakarinen studies classroom interactions, teacher well-being and early learning in Finnish and Norwegian schools and early childhood settings. Her work combines classroom video observation (CLASS), eye-tracking, think-aloud interviews, questionnaires, mobile-app emotion reports, and statistical approaches such as multilevel modelling, latent profile analysis and longitudinal path models. Application areas include teacher resilience and burnout, educational dialogue, teacher–student relationships, literacy and numeracy development, inclusive education, and family and school experiences during COVID-19.

name: Elisabeth Emilie Sefranek Rongved
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Elisabeth Emilie Sefranek Rongved works on classroom research in schools, with a focus on how pupils read and how teachers teach reading. The publications, which appear to be written for a general or professional audience, cover tablet use and pupil collaboration, dialogue in teaching, ways teachers foster reading motivation, and the role of school leadership support in reading outcomes. The titles point to an emphasis on teaching practice and the school environment in reading instruction.

name: Elisabeth Stray Gausel
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Elisabeth Stray Gausel studies how children experience smell and how odors can be used in learning and play. Her work includes a participatory case study in a Norwegian children's museum, where abstract scents were built into a storytelling exhibition through an academia-industry collaboration and framed by a social theory of learning. She has also produced practical guidance for adults on exploring everyday smells and weather-related scents with children.

name: Erlend Aano
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Erlend Aano is listed with a 2024 publication titled "Innføringsseminar (Read to me) for ledere i Lindesnes kommune", an introductory seminar for managers in the municipality of Lindesnes in Norway. The title suggests work on introducing the Read to me initiative to local government leaders, but no abstract is available, so methods and specific application details cannot be described from this single record.

name: Hallvor Lyngstad
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Hallvor Lyngstad works on professional development and professional guidance (veiledning) in education, with a focus on partnerships between institutions. His publications address collaborative models for developing professional practice and the status and future opportunities of regional guidance networks, including forums for local supervisors in Rogaland. The work appears oriented toward practice and cooperation between education providers and the field.

name: Helene Urdland Karlsen
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Helene Urdland Karlsen works on digitalisation in early childhood education and care (kindergartens), with a focus on Scandinavian research. Her publication is a knowledge review that combines a long-term research database, a quality-assessed set of recent studies and newly published work from 2024–2025 to map themes, methods and gaps. It covers how digital tools relate to children's play and learning, staff competence, ethics, participation and the organisational conditions in kindergartens.

name: Ina Midttveit
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)

name: Janine Anne Campbell
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Janine Anne Campbell researches early childhood education and care, focusing on shared book reading, multisensory and olfaction-enhanced digital books, and children's engagement, vocabulary and comprehension. Her methods include experiments with young children, national parent surveys, scoping and narrative reviews, scale development and validation, and a Delphi study to build evidence indicators for educational technology. Application areas include kindergarten and school practice, early identification of high academic potential, child well-being, and quality standards for EdTech.

name: Kristin Vestrheim Cranner
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)

name: Leif Tore Sædberg
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Leif Tore Sædberg works on the digitalisation of early childhood education and care in Norwegian kindergartens. His publication, a short piece for the public, argues that knowledge is limited about how growing use of digital tools affects the youngest children. The work is framed around kindergarten practice and the need for more research in this area.

name: Mads Olsen
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Mads Olsen's work, as shown by a 2025 feasibility study, focuses on quality in kindergartens (early childhood education and care) and how it relates to children's everyday well-being. The study appears to examine whether and how this relationship can be investigated in practice, pointing to an applied, exploratory approach relevant to the early years education sector. Only one publication is available, so the range of methods and wider research areas cannot be described in more detail.

name: Maria Gilje Strand
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)

name: Martyna Bell
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Martyna Bell studies how parents, teachers, students and other adults cooperate to prevent and respond to cyberbullying in schools, mainly in Norway. Her work combines a systematic scoping review, semi-structured interviews analysed with reflexive thematic analysis, and Q methodology to capture parents' and students' perspectives. She also carries out comparative document analysis of national digitalization strategies in Norway and Poland, and writes on social media age limits.

name: Melissa Bond
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Melissa Bond studies educational technology in school and higher education, with a focus on artificial intelligence, learning analytics, student engagement, and programming, robotics and computational thinking. Her main method is secondary research, including systematic reviews, mapping reviews, meta-reviews and bibliometric or authorship analyses, alongside collective writing, surveys and work on automating evidence synthesis. Her publications also address generative AI in teaching, openness in education, and support for doctoral students who are mothers.

name: Roderick Thomas Duncan Dale
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Roderick Thomas Duncan Dale studies how medieval Norse culture and literature are portrayed in modern media, with a publication on the depiction of berserkir (Norse warrior figures) in the video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. The work examines how the game reshapes historical and literary sources into a fictional, pseudo-Norse version of these figures. His research connects medievalism, Old Norse studies and game analysis.

name: Selina Eckhoff Hamadi
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Selina Eckhoff Hamadi studies school attendance problems, including school refusal, truancy and absenteeism, in primary and lower secondary education, with a focus on Norway and the Nordic region. Her work combines systematic scoping review, qualitative interviews and focus groups with youths and professionals analysed through reflexive thematic analysis, and quantitative latent profile analysis of adolescent survey data on school climate. The research addresses how attendance problems develop and persist, how professionals' attitudes and collaboration shape support, and the role of early, coordinated and alternative provision in schools and support services.

name: Tim Olsen Levang
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Tim Olsen Levang's listed work consists of two 2023 items: one titled "Det var en gang et orgel" (Norwegian for "Once upon a time there was an organ") and one titled "AILIT Trailer". The titles suggest an interest in music or organ-related topics and in media or trailer production, but no abstracts are available, so methods and application domains cannot be described in more detail.

name: Torunn Helene Lindstad Fredriksen
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)

name: Trine Mathiesen Gilje
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Trine Mathiesen Gilje is a researcher whose listed work, a 2022 publication titled in Norwegian as a systematic knowledge summary for the education sector, concerns research synthesis in education. The title points to systematic review methods used to collect and consolidate existing evidence for the education sector. Only a title and year are available, so more specific topics, populations and findings cannot be described.

name: Trond Egil Toft
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)

name: Trond Hadland
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Trond Hadland appears in the publications as a contributor to Norwegian research on children's reading comprehension, specifically a short report on the PIRLS 2021 international reading study of ten-year-olds in Norway. The record also lists a 2024 appendix-type document ("Vedlegg"), but no content is given, so its subject cannot be described. The available work points to large-scale international assessment data used to describe reading achievement in primary school.

name: Øyvind Munthe
department: Faculty of Arts and Education (department not stated)
summary: Øyvind Munthe co-authored a technical report analysing the situation for kindergarten teachers in Norway, using national register data from Statistics Norway and higher education statistics. The work examines recruitment to and completion of kindergarten teacher education, as well as employment, retention, further education, retirement and generational differences among graduates. The findings concern workforce stability in the early childhood education sector.

name: Andréa Aparecida Goncalves Nes
summary: Andréa Aparecida Goncalves Nes studies nursing education and palliative care, with a focus on digital tools, simulation-based learning and clinical practice placements. Her work combines qualitative interviews and focus groups, scoping and mixed-studies reviews, and psychometric validation of instruments for nursing students and mentors in Norway and Brazil. Application areas include guidance and assessment of students with the TOPP-N app, postgraduate palliative care training, and telehealth and ethics in home-based palliative care.

name: Angelena Ursula Moore
summary: Angelena Ursula Moore studies how working while unwell (presenteeism) affects nurses and the safety of patient care in emergency and primary care settings. Her work uses qualitative methods, drawing on interviews with nurses at out-of-hours primary care facilities in Norway to examine work ethics, workplace stress and coping strategies. The findings relate to occupational health, healthcare quality and patient safety in acute care.

name: Anne Gunn Dovland Vassbø
summary: Anne Gunn Dovland Vassbø studies education for nursing students and healthcare personnel, with a focus on ethical competence, reflection and simulation-based learning. Her work combines qualitative methods such as focus group interviews, thematic analysis and hermeneutic reading of caring theory to develop educational models, including a caring-perception model for virtual reality. Application areas include clinical placements in nursing, peer-to-peer and collaborative simulation, and educational needs for AI adoption among healthcare leaders.

name: Anne Marie Gausel
summary: Anne Marie Gausel studies pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain and low back pain, combining interviews with women, questionnaire cohort data and statistical modelling of pain courses and their links to weight gain, physical activity, disability and quality of life. She also researches how chiropractors in Norway view and use evidence-based practice and maintenance care, using national surveys. Her work applies to women's health, musculoskeletal care and clinical practice in chiropractic.

name: Arild Eskeland
summary: Arild Eskeland studies anaesthesia and postoperative pain management, with a focus on how opioid dosing is organised during surgery. The publication shown is a retrospective observational analysis of patient records, using multiple regression, that compares when oxycodone is given during propofol and remifentanil target-controlled infusion and how much further opioid patients need after laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The work applies to clinical anaesthesia practice and analgesic protocols in hospital surgical care.

name: Bente Dahl
summary: Bente Dahl conducts qualitative research in midwifery and perinatal care, focusing on how women, partners and midwives experience childbirth and reproductive health events such as postpartum haemorrhage, fetal death, induction of labour, medical abortion and alcohol use in pregnancy. Her methods include phenomenological interviews, systematic text condensation, meta-ethnography, and mapping and umbrella reviews. The work addresses maternity care quality, communication and information needs, rural birth access, and support for groups such as bereaved lesbian mothers and male partners.

name: Bente Kristin Høgmo
summary: Bente Kristin Høgmo studies public health nursing and postnatal care for new families, with a focus on how parents, fathers and nurses experience municipal child and family health services. Her work uses qualitative methods, including phenomenological interviews, focus groups with reflexive thematic analysis, and meta-ethnographic syntheses of existing studies. It also covers groups who may be underserved, such as LGBTQ+ parents and resettled refugee youth, and the role of home visits, with implications for nursing practice, education and health policy.

name: Birgitta Haga Gripsrud
summary: Birgitta Haga Gripsrud studies care and relational ethics in healthcare and nursing, including how technology, policy and education shape professionals' ideals and practice of care. Her work uses qualitative methods such as focus groups, ethnographic fieldwork, narrative interviews and depth-hermeneutic interpretation, along with scoping reviews and policy document analysis. Application areas include nursing homes, end-of-life and death communication, multicultural workplaces, digital health, breast cancer and academic writing and career development.

name: Camilla Ann-Louise Koskinen
summary: Camilla Ann-Louise Koskinen works in caring science, studying how people experience health, suffering, loss and dignity in situations such as long-term illness, major life changes, parental or paternal alienation and leaving a high-cost religious group. Her work also covers how nursing students become caring nurses and how ethical competence can be developed through reflection, role-play simulation and virtual reality. Methods include hermeneutic approaches, in-depth interviews with thematic analysis, qualitative systematic reviews and meta-ethnography, conceptual and theory development, and cross-sectional surveys with cluster analysis and structural equation modelling of health and social care educators' competence.

name: Christina Tølbøl Frøiland
summary: Christina Tølbøl Frøiland conducts qualitative research on clinical nursing education and on care for older adults, including cancer survivors. Her work on nursing homes uses participant observation, interviews, focus groups and co-creative workshops to study how registered nurses mentor students and how digital educational resources can support mentors and nurse educators. She has also interviewed oncology staff in Norwegian long-term follow-up clinics about the quality and safety of late-effects care for older patients.

name: Eileen Oftedal
summary: Eileen Oftedal studies personality disorders and emotion-related difficulties in people treated in specialist mental health services, including emotional dysregulation, aggression, self-harm, alexithymia and personality functioning. Her work mostly uses longitudinal, observational analyses of Norwegian quality registry data with linear mixed models, compares mentalization-based and non-manualized psychotherapy, and evaluates the psychometric properties of emotion regulation measures using factor analysis. She has also carried out a qualitative interview study of therapeutic writing within a group cognitive behavioural programme for binge eating disorder.

name: Ellen Ramvi
summary: Ellen Ramvi studies how technology, organisational conditions and relationships shape care in Norwegian health and care services, drawing on care ethics and relational ethics. Her work uses qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, ethnographic fieldwork, visual matrix workshops and scoping reviews, with psychoanalytically informed interpretation in some studies. Application areas include general practice, nursing homes, midwifery and nursing education, covering digital health, welfare technology, death and emotions in long-term care, multicultural workplaces and ethical competence training.

name: Eva Christina Furskog-Risa
summary: Eva Christina Furskog-Risa studies midwifery education and practice, with a strong focus on simulation-based education for nursing and midwifery students in Tanzania and Malawi, including training in postpartum hemorrhage management. Her work uses qualitative interviews and focus groups, surveys, mixed-methods designs, quasi-experimental studies and a meta-synthesis, as well as cross-national comparisons of European and Nordic-Baltic midwifery. Other topics include women's experiences of pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain and contraceptive counselling, midwives' views on normal birth, and interdisciplinary care for vulnerable pregnant women in Norway.

name: Grethe Heidi Bjerga
summary: Grethe Heidi Bjerga conducts qualitative caring science research on clinical supervision, nursing education and ethical competence in healthcare. Her studies use focus group interviews, reflective student notes and dialogue groups, analysed with thematic and content analysis and hermeneutic application research, to examine how nurses and nursing students are supervised, how ethical practice is sustained, and how person-centred cancer care is enabled or limited. She also contributes to books and chapters on supervision, the formation of nurses and nursing care for suffering patients.

name: Gry Ciekals Wallgren
summary: Gry Ciekals Wallgren conducts qualitative caring science research on men's health, exploring how men experience loss, suffering, meaning and ethical values after major life changes such as paternal alienation, using in-depth interviews with hermeneutic and thematic analysis. She also studies how doctors and nurses in Norwegian hospitals recognize and acknowledge the approaching end of life in cancer patients, using interviews and content analysis to examine the roles of experience, collaboration, continuity and organizational structures. Her work informs palliative care practice and understanding of health and wellbeing in men facing life transitions.

name: Gun Ingela Jobe
summary: Gun Ingela Jobe studies person-centred care for older adults, with a focus on dementia care in nursing homes and on collaborative care planning in health and social care. Her work uses qualitative methods such as focus group interviews with content analysis, along with a philosophical synthesis of earlier empirical studies drawing on Paul Ricoeur's ethics. Topics include how assistant nurses create and use life story documentation, and how personhood and power asymmetry shape care planning.

name: Hanna Skog
summary: Hanna Skog works on qualitative, psychosocial research using biographical narrative methods, particularly the Biographic Narrative Interpretive Method (BNIM). Her publications address in-depth hermeneutic interpretation in group settings and the use of a reflexivity track to make the interviewer's role visible in interviews. Her doctoral material examines how cancer patients experience care through their biographical narratives.

name: Hege Bjøkne Wathne
summary: Hege Bjøkne Wathne studies nurse-assisted eHealth and remote patient monitoring that supports self-management in people with long-term illnesses, mainly heart failure and colorectal cancer, after hospital discharge. Her work uses qualitative interviews, observation, mixed methods analysis of usage data, an integrative literature review, and feasibility and randomised trial protocols to examine design needs, acceptability, usability, recruitment and the work nurses do in these services. The research is set in Norwegian hospital and primary care settings and centres on the relationship between patients and nurse navigators.

name: Henriette Thune
summary: Henriette Thune studies how health risk information about pandemics is communicated to the public, using COVID-19 in Norway as the main case. Her work combines qualitative methods (expert and public interviews, thematic analysis, mental models) with a randomized controlled experiment testing how video features such as source and call to action affect trust, comprehension, intentions and behavior. It also looks at collaboration between health experts and creative communicators to design evidence-based video communication for the public and decision makers.

name: Ida Helene Mykkeltveit
summary: Ida Helene Mykkeltveit researches health professional education, especially how clinical supervisors of specialist nursing and midwifery students are trained. Her qualitative studies use focus groups, written reflections and thematic analysis to evaluate a blended supervision course that combines e-learning with simulation-based practice of communication and relational skills. She has also carried out an observational study of surgical hand hygiene adherence among operating theatre nurses and surgeons, and has written about master's-level operating theatre nursing education.

name: Inger Johanne Bergerød
summary: Inger Johanne Bergerød studies resilience, quality and patient safety in health and welfare services, with a focus on elderly care, cancer care, and the involvement of next of kin and informal caregivers. Her work uses systematic and scoping reviews, qualitative interviews, consensus and co-creation methods, and a mixed-methods intervention protocol for leaders in older adult care. She also examines how regulatory inspection and supervision of hospitals, child welfare and social services drive improvement work.

name: Janet Bakken
summary: Janet Bakken studies end-of-life and palliative care, using qualitative methods such as interviews, content analysis and meta-ethnography to explore how dying patients experience facing death and how doctors and nurses recognise and acknowledge the end of life in hospitals. Her work also covers the development and evaluation of a web-based palliative care pathway in Western Norway. In nursing education, she examines guided reflection and the Fundamentals of Care framework in student supervision during clinical placements.

name: Janne Gabrielle Hunsbeth
summary: Janne Gabrielle Hunsbeth works in midwifery education and practice, with publications on student-led simulation, peer-to-peer learning with a neonatal resuscitation simulator in Tanzania, and communication skills training through simulation and group reflection. Her work also covers international student mobility in a midwifery master program, community midwifery in Norway, and the debate over gender-neutral professional titles. In addition, she has written a narrative portrayal of a humanitarian health worker dealing with trauma, war and maternal mortality.

name: Kari Kaldestad
summary: Kari Kaldestad conducts caring science research grounded in Katie Eriksson's caritative theory, studying dignity, suffering, health and ethical values in nursing and healthcare. Her work uses qualitative methods, including hermeneutic approaches, in-depth and focus-group interviews and thematic analysis, with groups such as men going through life transitions, fathers experiencing paternal alienation, older women receiving municipal care, and nurses at a low-threshold substance use centre. She also studies multi-professional ethical competence and leadership in clinical practice, and has contributed to developing a master's-level supervision education programme.

name: Kari Vevatne
summary: Kari Vevatne works on care ethics, gerontology and professional guidance (supervision), drawing mainly on philosophical and humanistic perspectives from thinkers such as Kierkegaard, Gilligan, de Beauvoir, Honneth and Bakhtin. Her publications examine ethical questions in elderly care and in loving acts of care, as well as recognition and dialogue in guidance relationships. She has also studied experiences of post-incident reviews after coercive measures in mental health services, covering personal, professional and ethical perspectives.

name: Kine Gjesdal
summary: Kine Gjesdal studies chronic pain management in primary care, including the design and testing of personalized, multidisciplinary group-based interventions delivered through municipal health services. Her work uses co-development, feasibility and longitudinal cohort designs with questionnaire outcomes such as health literacy, quality of life, sleep and medication use. She also contributes to national registry-linkage research in Norway describing people with chronic pain and long-term opioid users, covering diagnoses, prescribing and socioeconomic factors.

name: Kirsten Lode
summary: Kirsten Lode researches cancer care and nursing, combining clinical studies of breast cancer relapse monitoring using circulating tumor DNA and liquid biopsies with nursing research on patient experience. Her work uses qualitative interviews, cross-sectional surveys, mixed-methods designs and document analysis to examine recovery after colorectal cancer surgery in people aged 80 and over, psychological distress and coping during prostate cancer diagnosis, and patient safety in hospitals. She also writes and studies nursing education and practice, including the Fundamentals of Care framework, its Norwegian adaptation, student supervision and textbooks.

name: Kjetil Moen
summary: Kjetil Moen studies existential and ethical aspects of health care, including how patients experience facing death at the end of life and how professionals are affected by coercion and relationally demanding work in mental health care. His methods include qualitative narrative studies, a meta-ethnography of interview research, and a pedagogical intervention using virtual reflection groups to build ethical competence among nurses. His work also covers hospital chaplaincy and the psychiatrist's encounter with death, and is aimed at palliative care, mental health services and clinical education.

name: Kristina Sundt Eriksen
summary: Kristina Sundt Eriksen studies recovery and follow-up care for older people with cancer, especially adults aged 80 and over after curative colorectal cancer surgery. Her work uses qualitative interviews, cross-sectional surveys and multiphase mixed-methods designs to examine coping, social support, symptoms and healthcare services. She also works on nurse-led comprehensive geriatric assessment using Delphi methods, and on health technology for older cancer patients with cognitive impairment.

name: Kristine Rørtveit
summary: Kristine Rørtveit conducts qualitative research in nursing and mental health care, using interviews, systematic text condensation, phenomenological approaches and evidence syntheses such as meta-ethnography. Her work covers patient experiences of end-of-life care, depression, binge eating disorder and suicidal behaviour, as well as the experiences of nursing students, emergency primary care staff and school pupils. She also studies how frontline leaders implement clinical guidelines in Norwegian mental health services and writes on relationships, shame, dignity and nursing practice.

name: Linda Nyholm
summary: Linda Nyholm researches caring science and health technology, with a focus on social and humanoid robots in pharmacy counselling and the care of older persons. Her work mostly uses qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, thematic analysis, co-design and role-play, alongside scoping reviews and cross-sectional surveys. She also studies nursing and health topics including organ donation, life transitions and loss, religious disaffiliation, professional voice use and the work vitality of older health professionals.

name: Linda Susanne Estman
summary: Linda Susanne Estman studies caring science and nursing, with a focus on digital health, social robots and sustainability in healthcare. Her work uses mainly qualitative interviews analysed by reflexive thematic analysis, alongside theoretical and methodological papers drawing on hermeneutic philosophy and caring ethics. Application areas include telehomecare, robot-assisted medication counselling in pharmacies, home care and older persons' services, intensive care and organ donation ethics, and ethics education in virtual reality.

name: Line Johanne Øvrebø
summary: Line Johanne Øvrebø studies how the clinical competence of postgraduate critical care (intensive care) nursing students is assessed during placements in Norway. Her work combines an integrative literature review with qualitative interviews, focus groups and document analysis involving students, preceptors and nursing teachers. It examines assessment tools and criteria, the dual roles of assessors, and the learning environment, with a focus on nursing education and collaboration between universities and hospitals.

name: Malene Søiland
summary: Malene Søiland studies how registered nurses practice leadership in everyday work in home healthcare, particularly nurses without formal leadership roles. Her work uses qualitative methods, including individual interviews with nurses in Norwegian municipalities, a hermeneutical approach and thematic analysis, and also addresses how such leadership practices can be explored methodologically. Related topics include nursing activities and accountability, time constraints in care delivery, and salutogenic perspectives on participation in home-based health services.

name: Malin Maria Dramdal
summary: Malin Maria Dramdal works on education for operating room nursing, focusing on an educational podcast called Steril sone that prepares master's students and supports their coursework. The work describes the podcast's development and uses student evaluations after the introduction week to see whether it helped them understand the nurse role and stay committed to the programme. Her output consists mainly of conference and seminar presentations, with the aim of reducing early dropout and improving the learning experience.

name: Margareth Kristoffersen
summary: Margareth Kristoffersen studies why registered nurses stay in the nursing profession, focusing on professional identity, self-realization, solidarity among colleagues and the demands of nurse–patient relationships. Her work combines phenomenological and moral philosophy and theories such as salutogenesis, transformational leadership and reality shock with interview-based empirical examples. These are applied to settings in Norway including home healthcare, nursing homes, mental health wards, school nursing and the transition of newly graduated nurses, with implications for nurse retention and leadership.

name: Maria Handeland
summary: Maria Handeland studies nursing education, with a focus on how students learn during clinical placements. Her qualitative work, using focus group interviews and thematic analysis, examines students' experiences of reflection groups and how nurse educators are supported by a digital educational resource in nursing home placements. Her publications also touch on simulation as a way to learn professional and caring nursing practice.

name: Marta Høyland Lavik
summary: Marta Høyland Lavik studies grief, death and dying, and care relationships, mainly in Norwegian healthcare settings such as neonatal units, nursing homes and midwifery. Her work uses qualitative methods including focus groups, narrative interviews, ethnographic fieldwork, reflexive thematic analysis and psychoanalytically informed depth-hermeneutic interpretation. It covers bereaved parents' use of memory objects, nursing home staff's emotional experiences and communication about death, tensions and racism in multicultural care workplaces, and midwives' reflections on technology, alongside work in religion and African feminist biblical hermeneutics.

name: Miguel German Borda Borda
summary: Miguel German Borda Borda studies aging and dementia, with a focus on frailty, muscle function and cognitive decline, neuropsychiatric symptoms and care of older adults in Latin America, Europe and elsewhere. His work uses randomized trials, cohort and cross-sectional analyses, systematic, scoping and narrative reviews, surveys and conceptual frameworks. Application areas include biomarkers of inflammation and cardiometabolic health, geriatric assessment, dementia diagnosis in memory clinics, anti-amyloid treatment decisions, palliative care and patient involvement in research.

name: Monica Hetlesæther Fosmark
summary: Monica Hetlesæther Fosmark studies perioperative nursing, with a focus on how operating room nurses position patients for robotic-assisted surgery. Her work uses a descriptive qualitative design, drawing on individual interviews with nurses at a university hospital and analysing them through qualitative content analysis. The research addresses patient safety, prevention of positioning injuries, nurse responsibility and teamwork in the operating room.

name: Sebastian Rehnman
summary: Sebastian Rehnman is a philosopher whose work examines how philosophical analysis can clarify practices of care and self-understanding, including psychotherapy, journaling and confidential conversation. He uses conceptual and reflective methods, drawing on his own experience and on critiques of empirical research, to address questions about human nature, health and well-being. His publications also cover the philosophy of religion and philosophical theology, including the thought of Jonathan Edwards, and the use of poetry in philosophical inquiry.

name: Signe Østrem
summary: Signe Østrem studies self-care in people with heart failure, with a focus on nurse-assisted remote patient monitoring after hospital discharge. Her work uses longitudinal qualitative interviews analysed with content analysis, set alongside a randomised controlled trial of a digital intervention. It applies to transitional care from hospital to home and to the design of digital health support within nursing practice.

name: Silje Espejord
summary: Silje Espejord studies midwifery care in Norwegian primary health services, focusing on how community midwives identify and support pregnant women in vulnerable life situations and how they work with other professions. Her work relies on national cross-sectional online surveys analysed with descriptive and associational statistics, and examines factors such as experience and Early Start training. She also writes on midwifery education, including student-driven simulation, communication skills and group reflection, and on professional titles in midwifery.

name: Sissel Steinberg Sørheim
summary: Sissel Steinberg Sørheim works on supervision and clinical placement learning in nursing education, with attention to professional formation, ethics and the power dynamics of the supervisory relationship. Her work includes a qualitative interview study of nursing students' experiences of goal-setting conversations at the start of placements, and educational development projects using art-based learning in a master's course on professional supervision. She has also presented a collaboration between the university and municipalities that tested weekly supervision based on Fundamentals of Care in municipal health services, and has contributed to international simulation courses for nursing students.

name: Siv Tove Aunan
summary: Siv Tove Aunan studies how women with breast cancer prepare to return to work while still in treatment, using individual interviews and qualitative content analysis. Her work looks at survivors' sense of hope and personal value, and at how workplace contact, continuity of care, and information from healthcare providers shape their experience. The findings are aimed at helping healthcare professionals give individualized guidance on sick leave, legal rights, and support services.

name: Synnøve Mari Eidsvik Folkvord
summary: Synnøve Mari Eidsvik Folkvord studies midwifery education, with a focus on simulation-based learning, student-led simulation (SimBegin), clinical placement and supervision of students. Her work uses qualitative designs such as focus groups, written reflections and narratives analysed thematically, along with systematic reviews, to examine learning, self-efficacy, facilitator skills and patient safety. Application areas include midwifery and nursing curricula, supervisor training courses, communication training and respectful maternity care.

name: Torhild Borlaug
summary: Torhild Borlaug studies midwifery practice and midwifery education, using qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups and thematic analysis. Her work covers how midwives in Nordic and Baltic hospitals view and promote normal birth, and how student-led simulation (including SimBegin and NeoNatalieLive), newborn resuscitation training with an intact cord, and communication and compassion teaching are used in training. She also addresses student mobility in a master's programme and professional titles in Norway.

name: Turid Anita Jaastad
summary: Turid Anita Jaastad studies how nursing students develop into professional, caring nurses, working within a caring science perspective. Her work uses qualitative methods, including thematic and content analysis of students' written reflections, and a qualitative systematic review with thematic synthesis. The studies are set in Norwegian nursing education and cover reflection grounded in caring theory, role-play simulation, and guided group reflection on practice stories in clinical placements.

name: Venke Irene Ueland
summary: Venke Irene Ueland studies caring science, with a focus on how nursing students develop into caring nurses and on spiritual and existential care in clinical practice. Her work uses qualitative methods such as content analysis, focus groups, interviews, phenomenological-hermeneutic analysis and systematic review with thematic synthesis, and also includes development and psychometric testing of a spiritual care competency self-assessment tool for students. Application areas include nursing and midwifery education, cancer and end-of-life care in hospitals, person-centred care, obesity care and cardiac rehabilitation.

name: Aksel Paulsen
summary: Aksel Paulsen studies orthopedic care and outcomes, focusing on fractures (ankle, hip, humeral shaft), hip and knee arthroplasty, and primary care pain management. His work uses patient-reported outcome measures, validation and measurement-property studies, systematic reviews, qualitative interviews, randomized trial protocols, cohort studies and quality improvement projects. Other publications cover preoperative X-ray calibration for hip replacement planning, 3D printing for fracture planning, and digital patient-led follow-up after ankle and wrist fractures.

name: Aleksandra Latinovic
summary: Aleksandra Latinovic works on the involvement of family members and other next of kin in health care, with a focus on nursing education at the University of Stavanger. Her publication describes a Norwegian-language relatives' day for bachelor's nursing students, with themes of relatives as a resource, collaboration and the burden on caregivers. The work applies to nursing education and to cooperation between health services and patients' families.

name: Allaug Ulevåg Oksum
summary: Allaug Ulevåg Oksum researches public health nursing, with one strand on how students' learning outcomes are assessed during clinical placements and another on how school health nurses are emotionally affected by their encounters with children and young people. The work uses qualitative methods, including focus group interviews with students, practice supervisors and teachers, and has led to the development and presentation of a new assessment form for placement practice. Her publications also address nursing education, including a master's program in public health nursing, and the effects of efficiency demands on care-oriented education.

name: Ane Kristine Bendixen
summary: Ane Kristine Bendixen studies the legal frameworks governing municipal housing, health and care services for people with severe co-occurring substance use and mental health disorders in Norway. Her work combines doctrinal legal analysis, qualitative interviews with municipal and county governor staff, and conceptual analysis drawing on health, social and legal science, covering topics such as conditions attached to housing, self-determination, coercion, human rights and decision-making support. She also addresses legal application skills in nursing, social work and child welfare education.

name: Anette Sola Foss
summary: Anette Sola Foss conducts qualitative research in public health nursing, focusing on how public health nurses communicate with parents when they are concerned about a child's upbringing environment. Her work uses individual interviews and content analysis to examine relational and ethical aspects of practice, including the role of organizational support. She also studies nurses' aspirations to pursue a master's degree in public health nursing, drawing on preliminary qualitative findings.

name: Anne Marie Lunde Husebø
summary: Anne Marie Lunde Husebø studies nurse-assisted digital health, especially remote patient monitoring and eHealth for self-management after hospital discharge in people with heart failure, colorectal cancer and other long-term illnesses.
