His work combines registry-based cohort analyses of trauma dispatch, prehospital time, remoteness and functional outcome with qualitative interviews of ambulance staff, physicians and stroke patients. It also includes a team training intervention study on medication errors, consensus-built quality indicators for airway management, and reviews of resilience and major-incident preparedness.

name: Teklay Tesfay Kidanemariam
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Teklay Tesfay Kidanemariam studies health services research in Norway, focusing on resilience and mental well-being among health care professionals in home care and on the use of complementary and alternative medicine in hospitals. The work uses qualitative methods such as focus group interviews with thematic analysis, as well as mixed-methods designs combining national surveys, statistical analysis and process evaluation. Findings address team culture, leadership support, work organization and the safe, consistent delivery of care services, and the researcher also takes part in resilience engineering and resilient health care communities.

name: Thor Ole Gulsrud
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Thor Ole Gulsrud's publications span digital image analysis for aquaculture disease monitoring and public-facing discussion of artificial intelligence in education and health. One study developed an automated whole-slide image method, using immunohistochemistry-stained tissue, to quantify and map Vibrio aestuarianus infection in Pacific oysters, comparing results against qPCR measurements. Other works address guidance for academic staff and students on using AI, opportunities and challenges of AI in healthcare, and broader health service topics.

name: Tone Knutsen Brandeggen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Tone Knutsen Brandeggen studies nursing education, with a focus on how nursing students learn clinical skills and judgment in both simulated and real practice settings. Her work mainly uses qualitative methods such as focus group interviews, content analysis and thematic analysis to examine digital tools (a skills training app, virtual simulation software, digital storytelling) and reflective supervision approaches. It also covers the training of clinical supervisors through meta-supervision groups, the Fundamentals of Care framework, and supervision and assessment of students in nursing home placements.

name: Tor Paaske Utheim
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Tor Paaske Utheim studies ocular surface disease, especially dry eye, meibomian gland dysfunction, atopic keratoconjunctivitis and thyroid eye disease, using clinical cohorts, questionnaires, and tear fluid analysis by multiplex cytokine assays, proteomics, glycoproteomics and metabolomics to identify biomarkers. His work also covers rare eye disorders such as congenital aniridia, tear-based markers of mild cognitive impairment, and population retinal screening through tele-ophthalmology. A further strand evaluates dental education, comparing curriculum integration, digital and hands-on teaching of anatomy and histogenetics, and knowledge retention among dental students and hygienists.

name: Torunn Beate Johannessen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Torunn Beate Johannessen studies patient safety, welfare technology and digital home follow-up for older adults in municipal health and care services, mainly through qualitative methods such as focus groups, interviews and content analysis. She also researches simulation-based learning and collaborative simulation in clinical placements within health professional education, and has written on independent safety investigation, risk management and dementia care competence. Her work links nursing education for older-adult care with practice-based collaboration between universities and health services.

name: Torunn Strømme
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Torunn Strømme studies how quality improvement and patient safety interventions are implemented in Norwegian nursing homes and home care services, and how nursing students learn clinical skills. Her work relies mainly on qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, participant observation and grounded theory, including multiple case studies of leadership and competence programmes. Topics include barriers and enablers to implementation, knowledge boundaries, recognition of deterioration in frail older patients, and the use of an interactive app in nursing education.

name: Vegard Asgeir Forsaa
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Vegard Asgeir Forsaa studies retinal detachment and macular hole surgery, using multicenter registry cohorts with propensity matching, prospective imaging studies and a randomized trial. His work compares surgical techniques and tamponade agents, follows anatomical and visual recovery with optical coherence tomography and infrared imaging, and examines the incidence of detachment. He also investigates how repeated anti-VEGF intravitreal injections with povidone-iodine affect the ocular surface and tear cytokines, and has evaluated wet-lab training for open-globe injury management.

name: Verena Juliane Schall
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology

name: Veslemøy Guise
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Veslemøy Guise studies resilience and adaptive capacity in healthcare, looking at how individuals, teams, organizations and leaders enable high-quality, safe care across hospitals, nursing homes, home care and older adult care. Her work uses qualitative designs, systematic and narrative reviews, mixed-methods and co-design protocols, and framework development, including stakeholder involvement of patients, families and informal caregivers. Application areas include elderly care workforce well-being, family-centered care for children with cerebral palsy, digital technology in a diabetes transition clinic, and the role of champions in quality improvement.

name: Victoria Vatsvåg
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Victoria Vatsvåg studies medical education in point-of-care ultrasound, focusing on whether teaching delivered remotely through videoconferencing can match in-person instruction. Her work compares student groups in a prehospital critical care program using pre- and post-course tests of knowledge, image interpretation, scanning technique and clinical decision-making. The findings relate to telemedicine and training in settings with physical distancing or long distances.

name: Vilde Marie Thomseth
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Vilde Marie Thomseth conducts clinical ophthalmology research on retinal detachment and on the effects of repeated intravitreal injections on the ocular surface. Her work includes population-based epidemiology of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in Western Norway, prospective imaging studies using en face OCT, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy, infrared homography and swept-source OCT, and controlled studies of tear film, meibomian glands and tear cytokines in patients treated with anti-VEGF for neovascular age-related macular degeneration. Applications are in postoperative visual recovery and retinal displacement after detachment repair, and in the ocular surface health of patients receiving serial injections with povidone-iodine antisepsis.

name: Wolfgang George Cornelius Voelckel
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Wolfgang George Cornelius Voelckel studies prehospital emergency and trauma medicine in Austria, with a focus on out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (including traumatic and paediatric cases), physician-staffed ground and helicopter emergency services, and the staffing and triage of emergency calls. His work uses retrospective cohort analyses, nationwide audits, Delphi consensus processes and literature reviews, and also covers spinal cord injury epidemiology and drug therapies for haemorrhagic shock and severe traumatic brain injury.

name: Andrea Gotuholt Lunde
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Andrea Gotuholt Lunde works on improving mental health services for young people from indigenous and ethnic minority backgrounds. Her listed work centres on participatory approaches, bringing together youth with minority backgrounds and project partners through gatherings, and on sharing this work with health authorities and child and family agencies. The focus is on user involvement in shaping mental health service provision in Norway.

name: Arne Endresen
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)

name: Cathrine Sneberg
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Cathrine Sneberg's publications relate to patient safety and resilience in healthcare, as shown by an annual report from the SHARE centre for resilience in healthcare and a Norwegian-language piece on participation in national work to improve how serious incidents in health services are handled. Her work appears to sit in the organisational and policy side of healthcare quality, covering centre-level reporting and national efforts on incident management. The titles point to a Norwegian health system setting.

name: Eigil Kloster Osmundsen
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Eigil Kloster Osmundsen is associated with work on patient safety, as shown by a 2023 Norwegian-language publication covering the marking of World Patient Safety Day and a national conference for patients' relatives. The listing points to an interest in involving family members and carers in healthcare quality and safety, though it gives no detail on research methods. The application area is health services, with an emphasis on patient and next-of-kin perspectives.

name: Knut Sommerseth Lie
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Knut Sommerseth Lie's work, as shown by this publication, concerns interdisciplinary mapping of health needs among older adults living at home. It uses a case of an elderly woman recovering from a hip fracture to examine how systematic, holistic assessment could support independence and reduce the risk of functional decline. The application area is municipal health and care services for ageing people.

name: Kristoffer Woldseth Moldekleiv
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)

name: Bastien Ricquebourg
summary: Bastien Ricquebourg is a percussionist who performs with the Stavanger Symphony Orchestra, with the listed work showing him playing marimba, vibraphone and woodblocks. In 2025 he took part in the premiere of John Erik Kaada's chamber ensemble piece "Rational Music For An Irrational World", staged for Stavanger's 900-year anniversary. The piece combines acoustic instruments, organ, electronics and processed church recordings played through a surround sound system, and he is also associated with a 2023 concert titled "Klassisk onsdag 2".

name: Bettina Smith
summary: Bettina Smith is a classical singer and music researcher whose work centres on women composers and gender in music, mainly through the European Voices of Women project. Her activities combine performative research, concerts of art song, early music, French repertoire and contemporary works for voice with organ, harpsichord or piano, and master classes and panel presentations. She also contributes historical case studies, such as one on the Norwegian composer Anne Marie Ørbeck, and project reports on education and cultural transfer in the cultural sector.

name: Bjarte Engeset
summary: Bjarte Engeset is a conductor whose listed work consists of concerts with Norwegian military bands, symphony orchestras and brass bands, including programmes built around Ravel, Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition and Tchaikovsky's Pathétique. He also leads conducting masterclasses and forums for emerging conductors, and has worked on concerts featuring young talents. His activity centres on orchestral and wind band performance and conductor training in Norway and Denmark.

name: Esa Olavi Lilja
summary: Esa Olavi Lilja researches music theory and aural skills, covering both the analysis of harmony in popular and rock repertoire and the assessment of prospective students in higher music education. His work includes style-focused analysis of chords, modes, function and texture in early heavy metal, and comparative and test-based studies of entrance exams in Norway and Scandinavia. He also writes on how music theory concepts and analysis systems are taught, including methods that link improvisation with ear training.

name: Fernando Cruz Robledillo
summary: Fernando Cruz Robledillo works in music performance and conducting, with research outputs on conducting technique and digital approaches to it, including beat prediction in classical conducting. He also appears widely in concerts in the Stavanger region, covering classical, Latin American and jazz-and-classical programs, film music with a symphony orchestra, and venues such as churches, a concert hall and a hospital. His activities include conducting weeks and festival performances.

name: Friederike Wildschütz
summary: Friederike Wildschütz is a pianist and associate professor at the University of Stavanger whose work centres on classical vocal performance, opera and art song. Her publications are concert and recital programmes, including opera cafés, themed song evenings and an interdisciplinary doctoral concert that combines song with dance, theatre and projections. She also takes part in teaching and outreach, including master classes in the Erasmus+ project Voices of Women and public events at the university.

name: Ghislain Marie Gourvennec
summary: Ghislain Marie Gourvennec is a performing musician whose 2023 output consists of organ recitals and concert series, along with festival appearances and seasonal concerts. The titles also show work in baroque ensemble music, including programmes with Stavanger barokk, and in choral and large-scale vocal repertoire such as the B minor Mass and a Requiem by Kreek. His activity centres on live public performance in Norway and France, with programmes for audiences of all ages.

name: Halvor Kristiansson Hosar
summary: Halvor Kristiansson Hosar studies 18th-century and early 19th-century music, especially the symphonic and sacred repertoires of composers such as Johann Baptist Wanhal and Dittersdorf. His work combines catalog and collection analysis, critical editions, and corpus-based study of terminology to reassess institutional music history, keyboard pedagogy and the historiography of the symphony, including in Norway. Application areas include music archives, monastery collections, editorial practice and music historiography.

name: Hans Petter Tangen
summary: Hans Petter Tangen is listed with a 2024 item titled "Mesterklasse på Kongshaug Musikkgymnas" (Master class at Kongshaug Music Upper Secondary School). The title points to a master class at a music-focused secondary school, which suggests involvement in music teaching or performance instruction. No abstract or methods are provided, so the specific instrument, genre and approach cannot be determined from this record.

name: Håkon Vestly
summary: Håkon Vestly is a performing musician whose listed work consists of concerts, including a 2023 performance in Visby Cathedral on Gotland of Messiaen's Quartet for the End of Time with the ensemble Trio Anima. He has also taken part in a public event for a seniors' university about the values in the life and writing of the author Anne-Cath. Vestly. His output is centred on live classical chamber music and cultural outreach rather than conventional research methods.

name: Igor Vyacheslavovich Eliseev
summary: Igor Vyacheslavovich Eliseev is a performing musician whose listed work consists of concerts, including a 2024 concert with the Norwegian double bass club. In 2022 he took part in concerts with Stavanger Domkor and the Stavanger Cathedral Ensemble in churches across Rogaland, performing Steve Dobrogosz's Mass alongside works by Thomas Torstrup, Philip Glass and Ola Gjeilo under conductor Oddgeir Kjetilstad. His activity centres on live ensemble performance of choral and contemporary sacred music and double bass repertoire.

name: Ilmari Tauno Mikael Hopkins
summary: Ilmari Tauno Mikael Hopkins is a performing musician whose work consists of concert and recital appearances in Rogaland, Norway. These include a themed opera and art-song programme at Stavanger Konserthus on motherhood, a performance of Jakob Glans' First Symphony, and church concerts with Stavanger Domkor and the Stavanger Katedralensemble. The repertoire spans opera, lied, choral and contemporary sacred music by composers such as Verdi, Puccini, Schumann, Dobrogosz, Glass and Gjeilo.

name: Kristian Thunestvedt Evjen
summary: Kristian Thunestvedt Evjen is a musician whose listed work centres on performance and conducting, including concerts, choir programmes and staged music productions such as The Medium, Hans og Grete and The Snowman. His output also includes research-linked interpretation of the piano music of Finn Mortensen in an international context, and programmes featuring composers such as Olivier Messiaen. The work is presented through public concerts and productions in Norway, covering classical, opera and children's repertoire.

name: Lise Karin Meling
summary: Lise Karin Meling is a musicologist who studies women composers and musical life in Britain and Norway, using historical and archival methods such as analysis of keyboard works, subscription lists, periodicals and an amateur's music collection. She also researches music education and gender balance through questionnaire studies and the ERASMUS+ Voices of Women project, and writes on canon critique and decolonizing higher education. Her work applies to music history teaching, cultural dissemination and the cultural sector.

name: Milan Rabrenovic
summary: Milan Rabrenovic is a performing musician whose listed outputs are concerts, festival appearances and staged productions in Norway between 2022 and 2025. These include chamber music series in Sand, opera café events in Sandnes, a yoga concert at a chamber music festival, an organ festival, and a children's opera at Utstein Kloster. The work centres on live classical performance and public music events.

name: Morten Schjelderup Wensberg
summary: Morten Schjelderup Wensberg works in music performance and conducting, with publications listing concerts given at Stavanger Konserthus, Sandens kirke and Sandnes kirke in 2024. His output also includes contributions to professional forums and conferences on the development of conducting in the Nordic region, including the Nordic Conductors' Forum in Oslo and the 2023 conducting conference. The work combines practical concert presentation with exchange on conducting practice and education.

name: Olaf Eggestad
summary: Olaf Eggestad works in music history and musicology, with a focus on Norwegian piano culture, music pedagogy and local music life. His publications include a study of the pianist and professor Robert Riefling's aesthetic outlook and teaching, an interview-based survey of recent classical and jazz history in Stavanger, and introductory talks on the composer Johannes Brahms. He has also written about the life and character of the diplomat Dag Hammarskjöld, showing an interest in biography and cultural context.

name: Per Kristian Norbotn Svensen
summary: Per Kristian Norbotn Svensen works in brass music performance and research, with a focus on the trombone. His publications include a historical survey of Scandinavian trombone repertoire, with particular attention to Danish works, and kindergarten concerts given with the Bjergsted Blåseensemble wind ensemble in 2025, which show an outreach role in music for young children.

name: Åsta Willumsen Sirnes
summary: Åsta Willumsen Sirnes is a choral conductor and arranger whose listed work consists of musical productions rather than research articles. The publications show her conducting a recording of a choir arrangement of a wedding march by Thomas Torstrup performed by the Stavanger student choir, for which she co-wrote the text, and her involvement in a university Christmas concert, both in 2025.

name: Øyvind Grong
summary: Øyvind Grong is a bassist, tuba player and vocalist who performs in Arne Skage's blues band, appearing at blues clubs, festivals and venues across Norway, including Svalbard. The listed work centres on live concerts and a single release in blues, roots and New Orleans-influenced music, with slide guitar and second-line styles. One biographical note also records earlier work with symphony orchestras and with other bands.

name: Andreas Christopher Aabel Bjørneboe
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production

name: Ane Iselin Brogeland
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Ane Iselin Brogeland is a dance artist and artistic researcher whose work explores grief as a shared, relational experience through improvisational dance, performance and collaborative practice. Her publications include choreographed works and reflective texts that treat artistic practice as a psychosocial space for gathering around loss. She also creates contemporary dance performances for very young audiences and kindergartens, using fairy tales as a starting point.

name: Anita Kaasbøll
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Anita Kaasbøll is a vocal performer whose work centres on improvisation, live electronics and contemporary vocal music. The listed outputs are concerts, tours, festival appearances and commissioned premieres, mostly with the vocal ensemble Trondheim Voices and in collaboration with musicians, a chamber orchestra and dancers. She has also contributed to improvisation activity within a research school.

name: Birgitte Bauer-Nilsen
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Birgitte Bauer-Nilsen works in dance and performing arts, creating interactive performative installations for museums and stage works that address climate change. Her publications also cover art activism, collaboration between performing arts and museums, and teaching sustainability and green transition in art education. Other outputs include a dance trilogy on climate change, an opera production, artist talks, and work on animist pedagogies and rituals.

name: Brynjar Åbel Bandlien
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Brynjar Åbel Bandlien's listed work centres on queer life, Pride and dance, shown through commentary, performances and panel discussions. The publications connect contemporary dance with lived experience, the pandemic and futures, and include a public response to the 2022 Oslo shootings. The output is mainly in Norwegian and takes the form of media pieces, stage works and event contributions rather than conventional research articles.

name: Dominique Jose Albert Brackeva
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Dominique Jose Albert Brackeva is a performing musician whose work centres on new and improvised music, shown mainly through concerts with the Stavanger-based ensemble Kitchen Orchestra, including collaborations with guest artists and a family concert for children and adults. The publications also list performances with Fint Fransk Orkester at venues and festivals across Norway, as well as jazz ensemble and vocal ensemble concerts involving students and staff at the university. The work combines artistic practice with educational and professional development in live music settings.

name: Henning Rød Haugland
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Henning Rød Haugland is a musician whose listed work covers live performance and recording in Norway. His publications include a CD release by Fint Fransk Orkester, a Stavanger-based ensemble performing original songs and reinterpretations in the French chanson tradition with cabaret, string-swing and hip hop elements, and a concert titled "Salmespor" at the Norwegian Organ Festival, which suggests work with hymn and church music.

name: Kari Marie Manum
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Kari Marie Manum writes on the philosophy of education and music education, working through essayistic, lyrical and vignette-based writing rather than empirical studies. Her publications examine pedagogical relations as encounter, musicking, counterfactual thinking, academic freedom and authoritarianism in universities, and critiques of degrowth and progress-oriented logics in education. Related work addresses democracy and inclusion in school music, and meaning and sustainability in music.

name: Kari Olene Oma Rønnes
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Kari Olene Oma Rønnes works on music and arts education, with a focus on singing, project-based teaching and participatory learning communities. Her publications examine early-years teaching in small multi-grade schools through a development project with arts students, drawing on body phenomenology and the idea of musicking, and also address the mandate and values of the municipal culture school under new education legislation. Other work looks at democratic participation in a medieval-themed practice community project and at exploratory learning processes involving pupils and students.

name: Kristoffer Berre Alberts
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Kristoffer Berre Alberts is a saxophonist and composer whose work combines jazz, improvised music and contemporary composition with artistic research. His output includes new commissioned works, collaborative dance, film and music projects, concerts and album releases with ensembles such as Kitchen Orchestra and Zanussi 3, alongside a book chapter examining how art relates to smart city policy, using Stavanger as a reference point. His work is tied to Stavanger's cultural life, including works made for the city's anniversary celebrations.

name: Mari Flønes
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Mari Flønes researches dance education in Norwegian primary schools, treating choreography, research and teaching as a single entangled practice she calls edu-choreography. Her practice-led work uses a/r/tography, performative inquiry and diffractive analysis, drawing on agential realism and post-qualitative theory, and is based on creative dance projects with pupils and teachers. She also examines research ethics when children are involved, collaboration between artists and teachers, and diversity and inclusion in dance and cultural-school education.

name: Mark William Drews
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Mark William Drews works in music performance, music production and audio recording. His listed outputs are mainly concerts with the Stavanger Storband big band and brass ensembles at regional events, along with a study of environmental sustainability in music production and recording education at the University of Stavanger. He has also judged a student studio recording competition at an Audio Engineering Society conference.

name: Per Zanussi
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Per Zanussi is a double bassist working in jazz and improvised music, shown through album releases and concert activity with groups such as Zanussi 3, Eyolf Dale Trio, Trespass Trio, Wunderkammer and Daydream. His work centres on live performance at clubs and festivals in Norway, Germany, France, Sweden, Finland and Poland, including Kongsberg Jazzfestival. He also takes part in collaborations with visiting international musicians and in workshop and teaching activity at the International Jazz Platform in Lodz.

name: Petru Popa
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Petru Popa is a performing musician whose work centres on live jazz and pop concerts, including seasonal Christmas tours with vocalist Inger Lise Hope. The publications document performances in churches, cultural centres and concert venues across Norway, mixing jazz standards, original songs and rearranged traditional carols. He has also taken part in jazz series with quartets and in a student-organised benefit art event.

name: Petter Frost Fadnes
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Petter Frost Fadnes is a saxophonist and researcher who works on improvised and contemporary music through practice-based and artistic research, including ensemble projects, performances, compositions and workshops. His publications also use critical and case-study approaches to look at hybrid and diasporic music-making, the role of the arts in smart city policy, post-industrial urban soundscapes, and decolonial approaches to teaching music history in higher education.

name: Siri Dybwik
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Siri Dybwik is a choreographer and artistic director of the dance company dybwikdans and the Elefantteateret, working on contemporary dance and performing arts for babies and young children. Her artistic development work includes interactive concert performances, fairy-tale-based productions, outdoor participatory dance projects and workshops, drawing on posthumanist philosophy, material-based staging and improvisation. The projects also address philosophical wonder, ethics and norm-critical themes with young audiences, citizenship and community involvement, and have been shown in Norway and internationally.

name: Stein Inge Brækhus
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Stein Inge Brækhus is a drummer and percussionist whose listed work consists of live concerts and recordings across jazz, blues, soul, Americana and Norwegian pop and folk-influenced music. His contributions include performing in jazz club and festival settings in Norway, playing on a Sámi vinyl album built on improvisation, and drumming, co-producing and mixing singles for the band The Last Hurrah. He works in ensembles ranging from vocal jazz and organ-based bop to roots and rock bands.

name: Svein Olav Herstad
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Svein Olav Herstad is a jazz keyboardist who plays Hammond B3 organ and performs in the Norwegian quartet Organ Jam, alongside two saxophones and drums. His work centres on live performance of original compositions and arrangements of jazz standards, spanning bop, blues and improvised music, at festivals and jazz clubs in western Norway. Other listed activities include duo improvisation and a repeat concert project.

name: Theodor Barsnes Onarheim
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Theodor Barsnes Onarheim is a double bassist whose work is in live musical performance, mainly jazz and pop. His publications document concerts and tours in Norway, including a Christmas tour with a vocalist, performances with a jazz ensemble and a quartet, and appearances with the Fint Fransk Orkester and a railway brass band. The venues range from churches and cultural centres to concert halls, libraries and a conference.

name: Thomas Eide Torstrup
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Thomas Eide Torstrup is a performing musician working as an organist and pianist across church music, jazz and contemporary concert settings. His publications are mainly concert appearances at venues and festivals in Stavanger, Copenhagen and Sveio, including a premiere of an electronics-supported ensemble work, collaborations with jazz and folk musicians, and a choral arrangement and composition. He has also taken part in a panel discussion at a Nordic church music symposium.

name: Tor Yttredal
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Tor Yttredal is a saxophonist whose listed outputs are live jazz performances, mainly in Norway. They include concerts with the organ quartet Organ Jam, which pairs Hammond B3 organ, drums and two saxophones, and the bossa nova and Brazilian-influenced Trio de Janeiro. His work also covers jazz festival and club appearances, ensemble performances, and leading an annual jazz jam session.

name: Wayne Thomas Brasel
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Wayne Thomas Brasel is a jazz musician whose listed outputs are live performances rather than written papers. They span solo, duo, trio and quartet formats and include collaborations with other artists such as Cathy Segal Garcia and Skage Larsen. The performances took place at jazz clubs, cafes, theatres and music schools in Norway, the United States and elsewhere between 2024 and 2026.

name: Elina Sofie Christ Borg Björnström
department: Faculty of Performing Arts (department not stated)

name: Abdelrahman Talat Ahmed Abdelaal
summary: Abdelrahman Talat Ahmed Abdelaal's research centres on oilfield scale management, especially recyclable magnetite nanoparticles coated with polymers or phosphonates (polyaspartate, PSSMA, carboxymethyl inulin, EDTMP) that block gypsum, calcite and barite scale. The work combines nanoparticle synthesis and characterization (XRD, FTIR, TGA, SEM, TEM), static jar tests and high-pressure dynamic tube-blocking tests, calcium compatibility and magnetic recovery trials. Related studies cover the design of phosphonate scale inhibitors and the ecotoxicity of coated nanoparticles in a zebrafish embryo model, with the aim of cutting chemical discharge in oil and gas production.

name: Ali H. Karaly
summary: Ali H. Karaly works on polymer-coated superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles and phosphonated polymers, mainly as recyclable, lower-discharge inhibitors of oilfield mineral scale and gas hydrates. Methods include nanoparticle synthesis and spectroscopic characterization, static and high-pressure dynamic tube-blocking tests, DFT simulations and zebrafish embryo ecotoxicity assays. Related work covers heavy metal removal from water, and biomedical and materials applications such as hemostatic sponges, wound-healing nanomaterials, antimicrobial fabrics and nanovesicle drug delivery.

name: Ali Hasan Saber Alkaraly
summary: Ali Hasan Saber Alkaraly works on magnetic nanoparticles and phosphonated polymers for oil and gas flow assurance, covering mineral scale inhibition and gas hydrate control. His methods include synthesizing and coating iron oxide nanoparticles, characterizing them by spectroscopy and microscopy, testing them in static and high-pressure dynamic rigs, and running density functional theory simulations. He also studies the environmental safety of these materials using a zebrafish embryo model, and applies similar nanocomposites to heavy metal removal from water, with a book chapter on conductive nanomaterials for wound healing.

name: Ananya Chari
summary: Ananya Chari works on the synthesis and functionalization of zirconium metal-organic frameworks, including sulfonic acid-functionalized frameworks and post-synthetic modification of UiO-66-NH2 with epoxides and other electrophiles. Her methods include high-throughput synthesis screening, structure determination, PXRD, gas sorption, NMR and HPLC-MS analysis, and scalable routes to bifunctional organic linkers. The work is aimed at adsorbents for recovering and separating critical metals, and at gas adsorption of CO2, water and ammonia.

name: Andrea Bagi
summary: Andrea Bagi studies microbial communities in aquaculture and marine environments, using cell counts, fluorescence in situ hybridization, qPCR, amplicon sequencing and shotgun metagenomics. The work covers nitrifying bacteria and plankton in biofloc shrimp and tilapia culture, hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria and genes as indicators of marine oil pollution, and microbial source tracking of sewage contamination at a coastal outfall. A recent title also points to work on microbial hydrogen consumption in depleted oil reservoirs.

name: Ashika Dilshani Wackwella Gamage
summary: Ashika Dilshani Wackwella Gamage studies how supercritical carbon dioxide can be used to coat and modify metal-organic framework particles, specifically ZIF-8 treated with adipic dihydrazide, for use in composite membranes. The work combines high-pressure impregnation methods with characterization by FTIR, XRD, TGA, BET and electron microscopy, and tests cellulose acetate mixed matrix membranes for hydrogen permeation. The application focus is gas separation, particularly hydrogen and carbon dioxide mixtures.

name: Behzad Heidariahootapeh
summary: Behzad Heidariahootapeh studies plant molecular biology in Arabidopsis thaliana, focusing on protein phosphatase 2A regulation, shugoshin-mediated chromosome cohesion, and trehalose-6-phosphate signalling in flowering, nitrogen use and photosynthesis. Methods include mutant and overexpression lines, gene expression and element analysis, chlorophyll fluorescence measurements and microscale thermophoresis binding assays. A second strand of work uses DNA metabarcoding, checklists and global datasets to describe fungal biodiversity in aquatic and forest habitats and the plant and bacterial partners recorded in honey from honey bees across latitudes.

name: Camilla Christina Pedersen
summary: Camilla Christina Pedersen studies fluid biomarkers for early diagnosis and prognosis of Parkinson's disease and related disorders such as dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease. Her work combines a systematic review with laboratory assay development (SIMOA, proximity extension assays) and statistical modelling of data from Norwegian longitudinal patient cohorts. The markers examined include phosphorylated alpha-synuclein, neurofilament light chain and inflammation-related proteins in cerebrospinal fluid and serum.

name: Cathrine Lillo
summary: Cathrine Lillo studies how protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) subunits and related signalling pathways, including trehalose-6-phosphate, regulate development, metabolism and stress responses in plants, mainly Arabidopsis. Her work combines mutant phenotyping, gene expression, photosynthesis and enzyme activity measurements, phosphoproteomics, protein interaction assays and microscale thermophoresis. She also examines nutrient supply, waterlogging and cultivation systems in tomato, Artemisia annua and Hypericum perforatum, including effects on nitrogen metabolism and the accumulation and root exudation of medicinal compounds.

name: Cato Brede
summary: Cato Brede works on liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry methods for measuring hormones, vitamin D, bile acids, tryptophan metabolites and iron-related biomarkers in human serum, fish plasma and fish feces. These methods are applied to clinical questions such as pneumonia outcomes, gastrointestinal cancer metabolomics and patient-derived tumor organoids, and to aquaculture questions such as salmon stress, vitamin D synthesis from sunlight and net-cleaning effects. He is also involved in natural product isolation and NMR-based structure determination of plant compounds tested for cytotoxicity against leukemia cells.

name: Daniela Maria Pampanin
summary: Daniela Maria Pampanin studies the effects of emerging contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, nanogold-containing diagnostic kit waste and polyhalogenated carbazoles on aquatic and mammalian models. Her methods include zebrafish embryo and larval tests, fish cell lines, visual behaviour assays, histology, transcriptomics and machine-learning digital pathology. She also works on seaweed (Palmaria palmata, Alaria esculenta) cultivation, stress responses and bioactivity for functional foods, and on public attitudes and willingness to pay for reducing pharmaceutical pollution.

name: Dugassa Nemie-Feyissa
summary: Dugassa Nemie-Feyissa studies how protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) and related signalling components regulate development and stress responses in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The publications combine mutant and overexpression plant lines, gene expression, element and enzyme analyses, photosynthesis measurements and microscale thermophoresis binding assays to examine chromosome cohesion in meiosis, flowering time, nitrogen responses, photosynthetic performance and metal homeostasis. The work also includes a review of PP2A B' subunit families and covers trehalose-6-phosphate signalling and environmental stress tolerance in plants.

name: Eduardo Alexandre Barros e Silva
summary: Eduardo Alexandre Barros e Silva works on biomaterials and tissue engineering, mainly alginate and other hydrogels used to deliver antimicrobial peptides, stem cell spheroids or other biologically active agents for wound and muscle repair. His methods include hydrogel characterization, 3D cell and spheroid culture, and preclinical mouse models of diabetic and MRSA-infected wounds and volumetric muscle loss, and he has also written reviews on diabetic foot ulcer dressings and COVID-19 muscle impairment. Related work uses 3D hydrogels to study how matrix composition and glucose affect cancer cell metabolism, and one listed output addresses optimization of wind-powered reservoir management.

name: Eli Drange Vee
summary: Eli Drange Vee studies how pharmaceutical contaminants affect marine invertebrates, focusing on oxidative stress responses in the blue mussel (Mytilus edulis). The work involves exposing mussels to the antibiotic ciprofloxacin and the anti-inflammatory drug diclofenac, both individually and as a mixture, and measuring biological stress markers. The research is relevant to aquatic ecotoxicology and environmental risk assessment of drug residues in coastal waters.

name: Emiel A.M. Janssen
summary: Emiel A.M. Janssen works in computational and digital pathology, developing and validating deep learning models (including multiple instance learning and foundation-model approaches) on whole-slide images for tumour segmentation, mitotic counting, Gleason and cribriform detection in prostate cancer, breast cancer subtyping, bladder cancer outcome prediction and inflammatory bowel disease grading. The work also covers scanner colour calibration and tissue detection to make diagnostic AI reliable across laboratories. In parallel, publications address breast cancer clinical and translational research, such as neoadjuvant endocrine therapy trials, circulating tumour DNA monitoring, biomarker prognostics in triple-negative disease, wearable-based fatigue monitoring, and spatial immune profiling and HPV-related biomarkers in other tumours.

name: Emil Anders Lindbäck
summary: Emil Anders Lindbäck works on the synthesis of iminosugars and azasugars (such as isofagomine, deoxynojirimycin and arabinitol derivatives) and tests them as glycosidase and cholinesterase inhibitors. His group uses copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition to build hybrid molecules, including sugar–coumarin, sugar–tacrine and human milk oligosaccharide–fluoroquinolone conjugates, and evaluates them in enzyme, antimicrobial, cancer cell and neurotoxicity assays supported by docking and DFT modelling. Application areas are drug discovery for Alzheimer's disease, cancer and bacterial infections.

name: Emilius Adrianus Maria Janssen
summary: Emilius Adrianus Maria Janssen's research centres on diagnostic and prognostic pathology in cancer, covering breast, prostate, cervical and melanocytic tumours. His work includes blood-based tumour DNA sequencing to detect breast cancer relapse, survival analyses of histological markers in triple-negative breast cancer, and prospective screening studies for HPV-positive women using p16/Ki-67 dual staining. He also develops and validates AI and machine learning tools for digital pathology, including scanner color calibration and prostate biopsy grading, and algorithms for classifying spitzoid tumours.

name: Federico Fenaroli
summary: Federico Fenaroli studies nanoparticle-based drug delivery, with a focus on polymeric micelles, polymersomes and semiconducting polymer nanoparticles as carriers for antibiotics, host-directed drugs, anticancer agents and immune stimulants. He uses zebrafish embryo and larval infection and xenograft models, together with mouse studies, cell assays and microscopy, to evaluate toxicity, circulation, cellular uptake and therapeutic efficacy, especially for tuberculosis and Mycobacterium marinum infection. His work also includes antitubercular compound design and pharmacokinetic profiling, microfluidic micelle production, and the effect of polymer design on protein fouling.

name: Georgeio Semaan
summary: Georgeio Semaan studies the conversion of regional lignocellulosic and food-industry wastes, such as spent coffee grounds, brewers' spent grain and greenhouse crop residues, into chemicals and fuels. The work combines laboratory pretreatment and fractionation experiments, anaerobic digestion assays, process simulation and techno-economic assessment with sensitivity and Monte Carlo analysis. It also examines Bitcoin mining as an added revenue stream for biorefineries, using stochastic financial modelling.

name: Gopalakrishnan Kumar
summary: Gopalakrishnan Kumar's publications cover bioenergy and biorefinery processes, including anaerobic digestion of sludge and manure, microwave-assisted pyrolysis, and the fermentation and catalytic conversion of lignocellulosic biomass into ethanol, butanol, lactic acid and sustainable aviation fuel. Other work addresses emerging contaminants such as PFAS, microplastics, antibiotic resistance genes and nitrosamines, using methods including metagenomics, molecular docking, field monitoring, life cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis. Further topics include waste-derived biopolymers, microalgae wastewater treatment, fungal recycling of hygiene products, carbon capture policy and urban water circular economy governance.

name: Guido Werner Alves
summary: Guido Werner Alves studies the clinical course, prognosis and biology of Parkinson's disease and related disorders, with a focus on cognitive decline, dementia and institutionalisation. His work combines individual patient data meta-analyses of population-based cohorts, longitudinal statistical and prognostic modelling, genetic analyses, fluid biomarker assays and brain tissue proteomic and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling. He also works on clinical rating scale validation and on cognitive outcomes in long-term survivors of brain metastases.

name: Hanne Røland Hagland
summary: Hanne Røland Hagland works on cancer biology and biomedical materials, combining laboratory models with clinical registry data. Her work uses 3D spheroid and patient-derived organoid cultures, metabolic flux analysis and drug-sensitivity testing in pancreatic, colorectal and lung cancer, as well as preclinical testing of anti-CD47 antibody-based therapies for lymphoma and leukemia. She also studies additively manufactured scaffolds and graphene materials, assessing mechanical strength, cell compatibility and toxicity in cell and zebrafish models, and has carried out national cohort analyses of outcomes after pancreatic cancer surgery.

name: Ilke Pala Øzkøk
summary: Ilke Pala Øzkøk studies biological wastewater treatment, including hybrid biofilm and moving bed reactors, activated sludge kinetics and nutrient removal. The work combines lab, pilot and full-scale reactor operation with respirometry, process modelling and microbial community sequencing to examine how micropollutants such as anti-inflammatory drugs, antibiotics and disinfectants affect treatment performance and resistance. Related publications address producing polyhydroxyalkanoate bioplastics from saline and organic-acid-rich waste with mixed microbial cultures, biogas production, and treating industrial and textile effluents.

name: Janronel Calog Pomicpic
summary: Janronel Calog Pomicpic studies chemical additives that stop gas hydrates from blocking oil and gas production pipelines, with a focus on kinetic hydrate inhibitor polymers and their synergists. The work combines polymer synthesis (including oxazoline, dipeptoid, piperidine-based and maleic copolymers) with high-pressure rocking cell tests using methane and natural gas mixtures, plus tetrahydrofuran hydrate and CO2 corrosion tests. Applications are flow assurance in the oil and gas industry, including combined hydrate, corrosion and scale control, and the study of mixed clathrate hydrates for possible gas storage and separation.

name: Jason Tyler Magnuson
summary: Jason Tyler Magnuson studies the toxic effects of environmental contaminants such as PFAS, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, preservatives, antioxidants and plastic-product leachates, mainly using early life stage zebrafish. His methods include transcriptomics, metabolomics, mass spectrometry, behavioral and visual function assays, histology, and machine learning and benchmark dose modeling for toxicity prediction and safety thresholds. The work also covers human exposure and health, through a PFAS placental transfer cohort, a meta-analysis of prenatal PFAS and gestational diabetes, a review of artificial sweeteners and cardiovascular risk, and PFAS intake from marine fish.

name: Jeff Tomiak
summary: Jeff Tomiak studies the human gut microbiome, with a focus on intestinal protists such as Blastocystis and Dientamoeba fragilis and on faecal microbiota transplantation. The work includes a clinical case report on clearing multidrug-resistant bacteria with FMT capsules and a population study using 16S and 18S rDNA sequencing and machine learning to link Blastocystis carriage to bacterial and eukaryotic gut communities. It also includes commentary on Blastocystis as a possible marker of gut health and on parasite transmission through FMT.

name: Jeffrey Stephen Tomiak
summary: Jeffrey Stephen Tomiak studies the human gut microbiome, including how intestinal protists such as Blastocystis relate to bacterial and eukaryotic community composition and gut health. The work uses 16S and 18S rDNA sequencing with machine learning classifiers in population studies, along with clinical case reporting. It also examines faecal microbiota transplantation as a way to clear multidrug-resistant and carbapenemase-producing bacteria and to consider parasite transmission.

name: Jens Vikse
summary: Jens Vikse works in rheumatology, with a focus on IgG4-related disease and lung involvement in connective tissue diseases. His work includes observational multicenter cohort studies of rituximab and glucocorticoid use, a European survey of adherence to treatment guidelines, and a Delphi consensus study of drug-induced lung toxicity risk in rheumatic patients. He also contributes to clinical practice guideline development, including a framework for structuring expert opinion, and to Norwegian-language clinical overviews of rheumatic topics.

name: Jodi Maple Grødem
summary: Jodi Maple Grødem studies Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, focusing on disease progression, prognosis and biomarkers. Her work uses pooled analyses of population-based incidence cohorts, genetic association and survival analyses, and fluid biomarker assays (SIMOA, seed amplification, cell-free DNA, enzyme activity) alongside scale validation and risk-prediction modelling. The applications include diagnosis, dementia and institutionalisation risk prediction, clinical trial design and patient information.

name: Johannes Lange
summary: Johannes Lange studies fluid and genetic biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognosis of Parkinson's disease and related disorders such as dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease. The work analyses cerebrospinal fluid and serum from population-based cohorts like ParkWest, using seed amplification assays, SIMOA, proximity extension proteomics, cell-free DNA sequencing and enzyme activity measures, with mixed-effects and survival models relating markers to cognitive and motor decline. It also includes systematic reviews, an individual patient data meta-analysis of disease prognosis, multi-laboratory assay comparisons, and cell-based retinal neuroprotection research.

name: John Senith Ravishan Fernando
summary: John Senith Ravishan Fernando studies porous adsorbent materials for capturing CO2 from flue gas, focusing on zirconium- and cerium-based metal-organic frameworks and pillar[5]arene-based supramolecular organic frameworks. The work combines synthesis, functionalization with groups such as amino and sulfonic acid, structural and physicochemical characterization, and gas and water vapour adsorption measurements, including selectivity, cyclability and humidity effects. It also covers shaping powders into beads and simulating breakthrough curves for flue gas separation, with a related publication on decarbonizing hydrogen production.

name: Kjetil Bårdsen
summary: Kjetil Bårdsen studies the biological basis of fatigue in chronic inflammatory and neurological diseases, including Parkinson's disease, Crohn's disease and psoriasis. The work combines patient-reported fatigue scales with molecular measurements such as cerebrospinal fluid proteomics, plasma biomarkers and blood gene expression (RNA sequencing and RT-qPCR), analysed with regression and principal component analysis. It focuses on innate immune and cellular stress pathways, including HMGB1, interleukin-1 signalling and heat-shock proteins.

name: Klevia Dishnica
summary: Klevia Dishnica works across computational and laboratory life sciences, with a focus on infectious disease and molecular biology. Her publications use molecular dynamics simulations, interaction-based drug repositioning screens, genomic sequencing and variant analysis, mass spectrometry proteomics, and clinical diagnostic evaluation to study SARS-CoV-2, the parasite Strongyloides stercoralis, and chemokine receptor signalling. She has also applied cell-based assays and transcriptomics to test how seaweed extracts affect intestinal epithelial cells, relevant to functional foods.

name: Krista Michelle Kaster
summary: Krista Michelle Kaster studies antibiotic resistance and microbial communities in wastewater treatment, using lab-scale activated sludge reactors, qPCR, 16S rRNA and high-throughput sequencing, and resistance testing of isolates. Her work examines how low antibiotic concentrations and disinfectants influence the spread of resistance genes, and tracks resistance genes across Norwegian treatment plants by season and wastewater source. She has also investigated low-temperature anaerobic granule reactors for treating municipal wastewater and producing methane.

name: Kåre Bredeli Jørgensen
summary: Kåre Bredeli Jørgensen works in synthetic organic and materials chemistry, with a focus on pillararene and pillarquinone macrocycles, metal-organic frameworks, and polycyclic aromatic compounds. His publications cover new synthetic routes (including photochemical, electrochemical flow and oxidative methods), spectroscopic and computational characterization, and adsorption testing of porous materials for CO2 capture. Related work applies synthesized PAH isomers and metabolites in fish embryo toxicity studies on crude oil components, and also includes biomass fractionation and azasugar glycosidase inhibitors.

name: Liza Maeva Nguyen van Sang
summary: Liza Maeva Nguyen van Sang works on antibacterial drug design, combining organic synthesis with antimicrobial testing to address antibiotic resistance. Her work includes light-degradable antibiotics, whose breakdown products are identified by LED-illuminated NMR and mass spectrometry, as well as conjugates of human milk oligosaccharides with fluoroquinolones or antibacterial peptides. She has also developed a peptide-based hydrogel for drug delivery and written on greener antibiotics that decompose after leaving the patient.

name: Lutz Andreas Eichacker
summary: Lutz Andreas Eichacker's publications span plant molecular physiology, structural biology and nanomedicine. They include work on how a trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase affects flowering time, nitrogen responses and photosynthesis in Arabidopsis mutants and overexpressing lines, and an X-ray free-electron laser study that recorded a diffraction pattern from a single GroEL protein. They also include a comparison of oxidized and PEGylated graphene as carriers for the cancer drug phenformin, tested in human cells and zebrafish larvae.

name: Magne Olav Sydnes
summary: Magne Olav Sydnes works in synthetic organic and medicinal chemistry, preparing azasugar (isofagomine) derivatives, indoloquinoline alkaloids, sugar–antibiotic conjugates, nickel complexes and PEGylated peptides, and testing them for glycosidase inhibition, antimicrobial, anticancer and cholinesterase activity. He also studies light-induced and hydrolytic degradation of antibiotics using NMR and mass spectrometry, aiming at greener drug design. His publications further cover pharmaceutical pollution from wastewater (chemical monitoring, risk modelling and fish transcriptomics), lipid metabolism and fatty acid oxidation in rodent studies, and polymer hydrogel formulations for drug release.

name: Malcolm Andrew Kelland
summary: Malcolm Andrew Kelland's publications cover flow assurance chemistry for oil and gas production, mainly kinetic hydrate inhibitor polymers and synergists, and mineral scale inhibitors and dissolvers for gypsum, calcite and barite. His methods include polymer and phosphonate synthesis, magnetite nanoparticle coatings that allow magnetic recovery and reuse, high-pressure rocking cell and dynamic tube-blocking tests, materials characterization, and DFT calculations. He also studies environmental aspects such as zebrafish embryo ecotoxicity of nanoparticle inhibitors and biodegradation and persistence of chemicals in offshore produced water.

name: Mari Mæland Nilsen
summary: Mari Mæland Nilsen works on molecular approaches to fatigue in chronic disease and on DNA-based detection in aquaculture. Her publications use proteomics of cerebrospinal fluid in Parkinson's disease and RNA sequencing with RT-qPCR of heat-shock protein genes in psoriasis, and she also developed a qPCR assay to detect and quantify salmon lice from seawater environmental DNA samples near fish farms.

name: Mark van der Giezen
summary: Mark van der Giezen studies the human and animal microbiome and gut protists, with a focus on Blastocystis, Entamoeba and Balantioides coli. His work combines 16S/ITS sequencing, phylogenetics, comparative genomics, biochemistry, crystal structure analysis and genetic tool development, and also covers microbiome changes in clinical and nutritional trials and in the oral cavity and skin. He also contributes to digital health and AI projects on cancer-related fatigue, Alzheimer's screening and inflammatory bowel disease pathology.

name: Melinda Lillesand
summary: Melinda Lillesand works in digital and computational pathology, building deep learning models for tumour segmentation and mitotic figure counting in whole-slide images and testing them across many cancer types and external cohorts. Her work on non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer combines digital image analysis, immunohistochemistry, targeted sequencing and imaging mass cytometry to find prognostic and BCG-response biomarkers and to study the tumour microenvironment. She has also applied image-analysis AI to progression risk in endometrial hyperplasia and studied gene expression in cervical precancer.

name: Mitchellrey Magbanua Toleco
summary: Mitchellrey Magbanua Toleco studies gut-dwelling single-celled eukaryotes, including Blastocystis and the pig parasite Balantioides coli. The work combines molecular methods such as PCR, sequencing and phylogenetics for parasite detection in farmed animals, with genetic tool development and cell biology in Blastocystis, including a restriction-enzyme-free DNA assembly cloning approach and studies of mitochondrial metabolism. Application areas include veterinary parasitology and surveillance in pig production, and genetic engineering of non-model organisms.

name: Oddmund Nordgård
summary: Oddmund Nordgård studies liquid biopsy biomarkers in breast and pancreatic cancer, focusing on circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, disseminated tumor cells and extracellular vesicles. His work uses targeted sequencing, PCR, DNA methylation and fragmentomics with machine learning, plus survival modelling, to predict outcomes and detect relapse or progression earlier than imaging. It also includes development of a sensitive error-corrected sequencing method, a prospective breast cancer biobank protocol, and earlier laboratory work on platelet interactions with blood progenitor and leukemia cells.

name: Pierre Edouard Liboureau
summary: Pierre Edouard Liboureau studies seaweeds, covering the physiology, cultivation and bioactive potential of red and brown algae such as Palmaria palmata, Alaria esculenta and Laminaria pallida. The work combines growth and photosynthesis measurements, stress and thermal-history experiments, proteomics, transcriptomics and cell-based assays to examine climate resilience, antioxidant properties and gut-health effects, with applications in sustainable aquaculture and functional foods. He also works in environmental toxicology, using machine-learning histology on fish livers and modelling and bioassays to assess pharmaceutical contaminants in wastewater effluent.

name: Sachin Maruti Chavan
summary: Sachin Maruti Chavan works mainly on metal-organic frameworks (especially Zr- and Ce-based) and related porous materials, using them for CO2 capture, silver removal from water, and as supports for Cu/ZnO catalysts that convert CO2 to methanol. The work combines framework synthesis and functionalization, adsorption and catalytic testing, and characterization including in situ Raman, X-ray diffraction and X-ray absorption spectroscopy. Other publications cover single-atom electrocatalysts for CO2 reduction, ethylene-to-propylene catalysts, oil-water displacement measurements, and modelling and systems evaluation of energy use and tomato yield in closed greenhouses.

name: Sittana Matar
summary: Sittana Matar works on preclinical development of antibody-based cancer immunotherapies, focusing on CD47-targeting fusion proteins that both block the CD47–SIRPα immune checkpoint and trigger direct programmed cancer cell death. Her studies combine cell-line assays, flow cytometry, phagocytosis and binding analyses, ex vivo blood compatibility testing, and mouse xenograft models. The work is applied to B-cell lymphoma, including rituximab-resistant and low-CD20 disease, and to B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia, with attention to reducing off-tumor toxicity such as red blood cell binding.

name: Solveig Auranaune Markussen
summary: Solveig Auranaune Markussen works on glycosidase inhibitors, focusing on iminosugars and isoiminosugars, which are sugar-mimicking compounds relevant to drug discovery. Her review of in vitro enzyme assay data examines how adding substituents at the 1- and 5a-positions of polyhydroxylated piperidine isoiminosugars changes inhibitory activity and specificity compared with the parent compounds. It also compares common iminosugars with isoiminosugars to show how moving the ring nitrogen to the anomeric position alters inhibition.

name: Umay Kiraz
summary: Umay Kiraz works in computational and digital pathology, applying deep learning, weakly supervised and multiple-instance learning, and machine learning to whole-slide images of cancer tissue. Her work covers prediction of breast cancer molecular subtypes, metastasis and chemotherapy response, bladder cancer grading and prognosis, and artifact detection with uncertainty estimates for slide quality control. She also studies prognostic histopathological and immunohistochemical biomarkers in population-based breast cancer cohorts, especially triple-negative breast cancer, and has contributed to reviews on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and multiplex immune profiling.

name: Venkatesh Bollabathini
summary: Venkatesh Bollabathini works on the synthesis and characterization of pillararenes and pillarquinones, macrocyclic host molecules, with a focus on their use for CO2 capture. His work combines synthetic organic chemistry, including oxidation routes to pillarquinones, with adsorption measurements under dry and humid conditions, NMR and infrared spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations of host-guest interactions. The applications centre on supramolecular organic frameworks for selective CO2 separation and the design of supramolecular materials.

name: Yohannes Seyoum Demissie
summary: Yohannes Seyoum Demissie studies the gut and skin microbiome and its links to nutrition, disease and parasite carriage, mainly using 16S rRNA and ITS sequencing, PCR and metabolomics. The work covers human cohorts and randomized trials (inflammatory bowel disease, irritable bowel syndrome, anthocyanin supplementation, fortified rice in schoolchildren), mouse diet and iron studies, and microbial communities of traditional fermented cereal foods. He also contributes to public health work on anemia and vitamin A supplementation in Africa, intestinal parasites in pigs, and digital monitoring of cancer-related fatigue.

name: Ahmad Opeyemi Zubair
summary: Ahmad Opeyemi Zubair studies power distribution networks, focusing on optimal power flow and how AI-based surrogate models perform when distributed energy resources such as solar and wind are added. His work uses simulation on realistic networks to test how well these models meet operating constraints and how errors from earlier workflow stages affect results, and it also applies the forward/backward sweep power flow method to quantify technical losses and voltage problems on a real Nigerian 11 kV feeder. The applications are in distribution network operation and planning for utilities, including high-DER grids and loss reduction.

name: Ali Gohar
summary: Ali Gohar studies resource allocation in virtualized and mobile networks, focusing on 5G network slicing, multi-access edge computing and virtual network embedding. The work formulates these as optimization problems and solves them online with deep reinforcement learning, including policy gradient methods, and compares the results against benchmark and existing algorithms. Application areas include cost-efficient slice brokerage between infrastructure providers and tenants, and secure, isolated virtual networks for smart city and IoT services.

name: Alvaro Fernandez Quilez
summary: Alvaro Fernandez Quilez develops deep learning methods for medical imaging, mainly structural MRI of the brain and prostate, with further work on EEG and clinical text. Projects include early Alzheimer's risk prediction with ensembles, normative modelling and multimodal embeddings; prostate segmentation, volume estimation and cancer detection; and brain tumour segmentation and Parkinson's detection from EEG. Methods emphasise uncertainty quantification such as conformal prediction, model calibration, fairness analysis across gender, self-supervised and out-of-distribution learning, and large language model resources for clinical decision-making.

name: Annisa Sarah
summary: Annisa Sarah studies resource orchestration in 5G and beyond networks with Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC), covering network slice allocation, traffic path computation, and service migration and relocation. Her methods include mathematical optimization, heuristic scoring algorithms, and reinforcement learning (Q-routing and deep Q-networks), which she evaluates against competing approaches in simulated scenarios, alongside survey work. Her work addresses cost, latency, service availability and user location privacy, with applications in smart cities and low-latency mobile services.

name: Antorweep Chakravorty
summary: Antorweep Chakravorty works on artificial intelligence and data-driven methods for industrial settings, including a study on virtual flow meters that uses text information to select better training data. He has also been involved in editing and introducing conference proceedings on AI theory and applications, information technology and smart computing technologies for engineering.

name: Arezo Shakeri
summary: Arezo Shakeri develops natural language processing and machine learning methods that detect Alzheimer's disease, dementia and mild cognitive impairment from speech transcripts and conversations. The work covers classical classifiers, transformer and large language model fine-tuning, embedding comparisons, statistical analysis of interpretable linguistic features, and a systematic literature review. It also builds multilingual and low-resource language datasets, including Norwegian, English and Chinese, for early cognitive screening.

name: Azadeh Jirdehi
summary: Azadeh Jirdehi works on modelling, system identification and control of unmanned aerial vehicle platforms, using the Quanser 3DoF Hover as a test system. Her publications build a nonlinear model that includes friction and gravity, estimate its parameters through lab experiments and genetic algorithm optimisation, and then test whether the more detailed model improves trajectory tracking. The control work combines feedforward control with linear parameter-varying error feedback designed through linear matrix inequalities, and is validated in real-time experiments.

name: Boyu Cui
summary: Boyu Cui develops automated, data-driven methods for processing and interpreting pressure and rate data from permanent downhole gauges, centred on identifying shut-in and multi-rate pressure transients without manual tuning. These methods feed into time-lapse pressure transient analysis workflows that are tested on North Sea water injection wells and geothermal wells in Indonesia, with checks against commercial software and reservoir simulation. Related work applies machine learning to other energy-sector problems, including federated learning for drilling rate of penetration, a federated language-model assistant for knowledge management, and an autoencoder for assessing control parameters.

name: Casper Cappelen
summary: Casper Cappelen works on deep learning for medical image analysis, focusing on automatic segmentation of the myocardium in late gadolinium enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance images. The publication compares two U-Net variants, one with residual connections and one multiresolution, and tests how different pixel value scaling strategies in preprocessing affect performance when models are applied to a different dataset. The work is relevant to cardiac MRI and semi-automated segmentation workflows, with evaluation based on Jaccard scores.

name: Chunming Rong
summary: Chunming Rong's research covers federated and distributed machine learning, including methods for client drift, mixed-precision aggregation and privacy-preserving training, as well as continual and online learning, reinforcement learning for edge computing and network service placement, and blockchain-based security, consent management and incentive design. The work also applies machine learning to other fields: automated pressure-transient analysis and alarm systems for oil and gas wells, federated learning on drilling data, video analysis of neonatal resuscitation, and building segmentation from RGB and LiDAR imagery.

name: Damiano Rotondo
summary: Damiano Rotondo works on control theory for dynamic systems, with emphasis on fault estimation and fault-tolerant control, sampled-data systems, linear parameter-varying systems, model predictive control and iterative learning control. His methods combine linear matrix inequality design, data-driven and identification-based modelling, observers and genetic-algorithm optimisation, tested in simulation and on laboratory platforms such as tank systems, a Quanser Aero, a 3DoF Hover and a DC motor-propeller. Application examples also include underwater vehicle design and anaesthesia regulation, alongside work on control education and outreach.

name: Daniel Osmundsen Dirdal

position.nb: Stipendiat i datateknologi : Verifikasjon av distribuerte systemer

summary: Daniel Osmundsen Dirdal works on formal modeling and verification of concurrent and distributed systems. His publications write a TLA+ specification of the Beefy light-client protocol used in Polkadot and check it with the TLC and Apalache model checkers, and also build a Petri net simulation platform in GPenSIM for comparing multiprocessor scheduling algorithms. The work applies to blockchain protocol assurance and to performance evaluation of parallel computing systems.

name: Didrik Efjestad Fjereide
summary: Didrik Efjestad Fjereide works on automatic control education and on modeling of laboratory control systems. His publications include a board game adapted from Zendo that teaches system properties such as linearity and time variation, along with student feedback from using it in a basic control course. He also builds and experimentally identifies nonlinear models of the Quanser Aero, an aerospace teaching rig, using detailed friction and centripetal force descriptions validated in real-time tests.

name: Eivind Sandve Haus
summary: Eivind Sandve Haus studies identifiability and parameter estimation in mathematical models of biomolecular systems, focusing on negative-feedback controller motifs. The work combines structural identifiability analysis across thousands of model and measurement combinations, the use of flow measurements as model outputs, and augmented extended Kalman filters for estimating parameters under noisy and noise-free conditions. It also includes a model of cancer metabolism, built around Seahorse analyzer flow data, that captures shifts between aerobic and anaerobic metabolism.

name: Enrico Guerriero
summary: Enrico Guerriero works on automated recognition of fine-grained activities in video, with a focus on newborn resuscitation. His work compares locally run vision-language models, paired with large language models, against a supervised TimeSformer vision transformer baseline on simulated resuscitation recordings. The methods include zero-shot prompting and fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation, applied to support clinical documentation and quality improvement.

name: Erlend Tøssebro
summary: Erlend Tøssebro works on applied machine learning and computing education. His publications include deep learning for video-based activity recognition in neonatal resuscitation, and recurrent neural network models that forecast traffic in Norwegian road tunnels. He also studies programming education and graduate skills, using national prior-knowledge testing and industry surveys on AI-related competence needs, and he has written encyclopedic entries on databases and SQL.

name: Felix James Cardano Pacis
summary: Felix James Cardano Pacis works on applying deep learning to oil and gas drilling, with one strand predicting rate of penetration from sequential drilling data using transfer learning, continual learning and quantile regression neural networks to quantify prediction uncertainty. A second strand develops language-model tools for drilling text, including zero-shot question answering, contrastive-learning embeddings for document retrieval, and locally hosted retrieval-augmented chatbots for internal knowledge bases. The work uses public field data such as Volve, Alvheim and Norwegian Petroleum Directorate records, and includes released datasets and open-source code.

name: Ferhat Özgur Catak
summary: Ferhat Özgur Catak works on trustworthy and secure machine learning, including federated learning, uncertainty quantification for large language and vision-language models, and adversarial robustness. His publications apply deep learning and transformer models to wireless communications such as spectrum sensing, channel estimation and modulation classification, and to healthcare, energy forecasting and document classification. He also writes on quantum machine learning theory, quantum key distribution for secure model training, and generative AI in smart grids.

name: Florenc Demrozi
summary: Florenc Demrozi works on machine learning for sensor-based human activity recognition and health monitoring, using wearable inertial sensors, event cameras, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth signals. His work covers fall detection (including pre-impact detection on embedded devices), freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease, indoor localization, automatic data labeling and zero-shot learning, and he has released several public datasets and benchmarks. He has also written reviews and opinion pieces on multimodal, distributed and adaptive AI for healthcare, and edited conference proceedings and editorials.

name: Gabriel Emerson Iturra Bocaz
summary: Gabriel Emerson Iturra Bocaz works on information retrieval and natural language processing, with a focus on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for multi-hop question answering, including metacognitive and multi-agent designs and a reproducibility study. He also contributes to longitudinal and temporal evaluation of retrieval systems through the LongEval lab, studies how relevance judgment depth affects BERT-based reranking, and has co-organised a fact-checking task on numerical claims. His applied work builds and evaluates RAG systems and datasets for aerospace documentation and clinical decision-making, and he has released an open-source library for incremental word embeddings on text streams.

name: Gianfranco Nencioni
summary: Gianfranco Nencioni studies resource management, service placement and migration, and security and dependability in 5G and beyond networks that use multi-access edge computing and network slicing. His work combines optimization, multi-objective heuristics, graph-based path computation, reinforcement learning, and dependability and security modeling, tested through simulation and Kubernetes-based testbeds. Application areas include low-latency and mission-critical services, vehicular communication, smart cities, and the economics of slice brokers.

name: Hein Meling
summary: Hein Meling works on distributed systems and blockchain infrastructure, with a focus on Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, committee-based blockchains and decentralized storage. His work includes designing and implementing protocols for role assignment, vote aggregation, incentive mechanisms, proof-of-storage and authenticated queries, and validating them through experiments, testing frameworks and formal TLA+ model checking.
