Applications include scalable blockchains, light clients, digital credential certification and data availability in peer-to-peer storage networks, along with reproducibility reviews of database research papers.

name: Ivica Kostric
summary: Ivica Kostric studies conversational recommender systems and conversational search, covering preference elicitation, user modeling and evaluation practices. The work combines dataset and protocol design, crowdsourcing, neural question generation and query rewriting, controlled user experiments and reproducibility studies of existing methods with large language models. It also covers research platforms and tools such as a movie recommendation bot, a conference assistant chatbot and robot, and personal knowledge graph management software.

name: Jakob Svane
summary: Jakob Svane studies how high-intensity and endurance exercise affects the heart in people with and without coronary artery disease or coronary artery calcification. His work combines exercise physiology measurements (blood pressure, heart rate variability, cardiac troponin I after exercise testing and cycling sessions) with coronary CT imaging, and applies machine learning and time series methods to correct artifacts in heart rate data and to classify individuals with coronary calcification. Applications include identifying people who may benefit from cardiac imaging and judging how exercise relates to cardiac risk.

name: Jayachander Surbiryala
summary: Jayachander Surbiryala works on applied artificial intelligence, data engineering and cloud computing. His publications cover testing pre-trained language models such as BERT and T5 for predicting table metadata in data-integration pipelines, and a blockchain-based design for decentralized cloud marketplaces that uses auctions and witness committees to manage service agreements, evaluated through a prototype on Ethereum. He also appears as editor of a conference volume on AI technologies, ethics and uses in sectors such as healthcare, agriculture and law.

name: John Håkon Husøy
summary: John Håkon Husøy works on adaptive digital signal processing, with a focus on subband adaptive filtering and its relationship to the normalized least mean square algorithm. His 2022 work proposes a very simple two-band filter bank for the normalized subband adaptive filter, supported by theoretical arguments and simulation studies of convergence performance against computational cost. The research is relevant to system identification and other applications where efficient adaptive filters are needed.

name: Jorge Garcia-Torres Fernandez
summary: Jorge Garcia-Torres Fernandez develops deep learning and computer vision methods to analyse thermal and visible light video from births and newborn resuscitation. His work covers detecting the time of birth and cord clamping, recognising resuscitation activities such as ventilation, stimulation and suction, and explaining model decisions with interpretability techniques. These methods are applied at Stavanger University Hospital to build automated timelines, a clinician dashboard and a privacy-conscious, consent-based data collection system to support documentation, debriefing and quality improvement in neonatal care.

name: Jungwon Seo
summary: Jungwon Seo studies federated learning, focusing on optimization methods that reduce client drift under non-IID data, partial client participation and mixed-precision quantization, with theoretical analysis and benchmark experiments. The work also covers secure aggregation (quantum key distribution, neural homomorphic cryptography, secure multi-party computation), large language model uses such as automated code deployment, federated chat systems and uncertainty quantification, and trustworthy AI for 6G networks. Application areas include wireless communications, medical question answering, customer support and oil and gas subsurface and industrial control data.

name: Karl Skretting
summary: Karl Skretting works on sparse representation and signal processing, developing online dictionary learning methods and sparse approximation techniques. His publications cover a kernel-based recursive least squares algorithm for updating dictionaries as data arrive, tested on classification tasks across four datasets, and a block-based sparse coding method that separates the frequency content of nonlinear signals using chirp-like atoms and a modified orthogonal matching pursuit.

name: Kathinka Dæhli Kurz
summary: Kathinka Dæhli Kurz works in clinical and AI-based radiology, with a focus on acute stroke imaging and care, and also on breast, brain tumour, cardiac and dementia imaging. Her studies combine deep learning methods (ensemble models, 4D CNNs, GANs, few-shot and segmentation networks) with retrospective and registry-based clinical studies, health service surveys and simulation training. Applications include stroke segmentation and treatment selection, access to thrombectomy, breast MRI and mammography screening, CT contrast dosing and Alzheimer's detection from MRI.

name: Ketil Oppedal
summary: Ketil Oppedal's research centres on quantitative MRI analysis of neurodegeneration, especially dementia with Lewy bodies, where he studies regional brain atrophy, sex differences, grey matter networks, patient subtypes and links to regional gene expression and co-pathologies. He also develops deep learning methods, including self-supervised, out-of-distribution and fairness-focused approaches, for Alzheimer's disease classification and prostate cancer lesion detection on MRI. Further work covers MRI markers and clinical measures in older people, such as tongue muscle and malnutrition in dementia, gait and cortical thickness in subjective cognitive decline, an anthocyanin supplementation trial, and X-ray calibration for hip replacement planning.

name: Kjersti Engan
summary: Kjersti Engan works on deep learning and computer vision for medical data, with two main strands: computational pathology and neonatal care. In pathology she builds weakly supervised and multiple instance learning models for whole-slide images, artifact detection with uncertainty estimates, and spatial immune profiling for bladder cancer and inflammatory bowel disease. In neonatal care she develops thermal and visible-light video systems that detect time of birth and recognise resuscitation activities, supported by clinical observational studies, consent-based data collection with blockchain, and work on generative imaging and multimodal healthcare AI.

name: Kjetil Thorsen
summary: Kjetil Thorsen conducts clinical research on prehospital care for acute stroke, focusing on how paramedics identify and triage suspected stroke patients in Oslo, Norway. The work is a stepped wedge cluster randomised trial testing whether e-learning, NIHSS scoring in the ambulance and a mobile app linking paramedics to the on-call stroke physician improve identification accuracy, measured by positive predictive value. It applies to emergency medical services, digital communication tools and acute stroke treatment pathways.

name: Kristian Thorsen
summary: Kristian Thorsen works on control theory and system identification, applying them to both engineered and biological systems. His publications cover modelling and LPV observer and controller design with LMI-based methods, validated experimentally on UAV-type platforms such as the Quanser 3DoF Hover and a DC motor-propeller. He also studies structural identifiability, Kalman filter parameter estimation and synthetic biology control circuits in yeast, along with AI surrogate models for optimal power flow in distribution networks with distributed energy resources.

name: Krisztian Balog
summary: Krisztian Balog studies how people interact with search, recommender and conversational systems, with a strong focus on user simulation, benchmark datasets and evaluation methods for these systems. His work covers conversational recommender systems, retrieval-augmented generation (grounding, source attribution and user trust), and the use of large language models as rankers and judges. He combines dataset and toolkit creation, reproducibility studies, crowdsourced benchmarking and controlled user studies, including applications in scientific literature recommendation.

name: Leander Nikolaus Jehl
summary: Leander Nikolaus Jehl works on distributed systems and blockchain technology, with a focus on Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, including role assignment, scalability techniques, vote aggregation and protocol implementation frameworks. His work also covers trusted execution environments for edge and cloud deployments, formal verification with TLA+ and model checking, incentive fairness in decentralized storage networks, and decentralized and privacy-preserving identity and credential systems. Methods include system design and prototyping, simulation, experimental evaluation, formal specification and survey analysis, applied to areas such as railway data recording, edge machine learning inference and light clients.

name: Mahdieh Khanmohammadi
summary: Mahdieh Khanmohammadi develops machine learning and deep learning methods for medical imaging and biosignals, with a main focus on acute ischemic stroke. Her work uses CT perfusion data to segment core and penumbra regions with 4D and multi-input neural networks, random forests and few-shot self-supervised learning, and to generate synthetic perfusion scans with GANs and vision transformers. She has also applied EEG-derived features and classifiers to distinguish neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.

name: Mariam Arustashvili
summary: Mariam Arustashvili works on recommender systems for scientific literature, focusing on user interest profiles written in natural language. Her work builds a synthetic test dataset from authors' publication histories and uses it to compare sparse retrieval, dense retrieval and large language model rerankers. The research centers on evaluation resources and benchmarking for transparent, user-controllable scholarly recommendation.

name: Martin Gilje Jaatun
summary: Martin Gilje Jaatun works on cybersecurity for industrial control systems, IoT devices and connected medical devices, drawing on standards analysis, threat modeling, interview and multi-case studies, and firmware fuzzing and monitoring tools. His work covers zone and conduit design under IEC 62443, smart grid and cloud-hosted critical infrastructure, and regulatory compliance for medical device manufacturers. He also studies the security risks of generative AI in software organizations using causal mapping and socio-technical analysis.

name: Matteo Iervasi
summary: Matteo Iervasi works on human activity recognition using wearable and ambient sensing, including inertial sensors, BLE beacon signal strength and Wi-Fi channel state information. His work develops ways to generate training labels automatically so that deep learning models need less manual annotation, and he checks these labels against video-based ground truth. He has also co-authored a systematic review of wearable cueing technologies for people with Parkinson's disease, covering auditory, visual and haptic cues for motor symptoms.

name: Matthias Anton Schedel
summary: Matthias Anton Schedel works on modeling and simulation of automated guided vehicle (AGV) systems in manufacturing, using modular Petri nets implemented in the GPenSIM simulator on MATLAB. The publication studies how AGV battery discharge rates, fleet size and the number and placement of charging stations affect output in a toy car production line. The approach aims to give practitioners an accessible, extensible model for testing AGV operating scenarios without advanced mathematics.

name: Md Sazidur Rahman
summary: Md Sazidur Rahman works on computer vision, with the single publication provided focusing on depth information in images and how it can be used or perturbed as part of visual learning. The title, "Depth Jitter: Seeing Through the Depth" (2025), points to a data augmentation style of approach involving depth variation. Only the title is available, so the specific methods, datasets and application domains cannot be described in more detail.

name: Merkebu Zenebe Degefa
summary: Merkebu Zenebe Degefa studies the operation, control and planning of power systems with high shares of distributed energy resources, covering microgrid interconnection, voltage regulation, and TSO-DSO coordination. His work combines optimisation, distributed control, AI-based optimal power flow surrogates and wide-area oscillation monitoring, tested through numerical simulation, real-time simulators and power-hardware-in-the-loop setups. Application areas include distribution network operational planning, flexibility resources and the integration of local energy communities into distribution grids.

name: Michal Chudoba
summary: Michal Chudoba works on applying large language models and knowledge-based methods to structured data, including ontologies and knowledge graphs. The publications cover autonomous agents that traverse large knowledge graphs for retrieval, comparisons of structured representations (AMR, RDF, Python code) in LLM prompting, and human-in-the-loop AI that maps WITSML mnemonics to the D-WIS standard. Application work focuses on the drilling and energy data domain, including AI tools that automatically populate D-WIS semantic models.

name: Mina Farmanbar
summary: Mina Farmanbar works on machine learning and natural language processing for health, particularly early detection of Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment from speech and conversation transcripts in several languages, including low-resource ones such as Norwegian. Her methods include linguistic feature analysis, transformer and large language model fine-tuning, multilingual dataset construction, and systematic and opinion reviews on multimodal AI and online learning. She also applies deep learning, optimization and regression to building segmentation from aerial RGB and LiDAR data, fatigue life prediction of structural steels, and financial time-series forecasting.

name: Morten Mossige
summary: Morten Mossige works on software testing and verification for industrial robotic systems, in close collaboration with ABB Robotics. His publications apply constraint programming to automate test case generation and test execution scheduling across robots and test machines, and use model checking and hardware/software co-verification to assess the safety of robot control software. The work centres on cyber-physical systems and reports on transferring these methods into industrial practice.

name: Morteza Esmaeili
summary: Morteza Esmaeili works on medical imaging, mainly magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy, combined with deep learning. His work covers glioma and glioblastoma, including tumor segmentation, molecular subtype classification, white-matter growth patterns, MRSI resolution enhancement and combined MRSI-PET diagnosis, as well as cervical cell classification from Pap smear images. He also applies AI models of functional brain connectomes to predict cognition and relate it to dopamine and brain health factors, and has written reviews on pediatric MRI, cardiac MR spectroscopy and exercise in heart failure rehabilitation.

name: Muhammad Sulaiman
summary: Muhammad Sulaiman works on building segmentation from aerial RGB imagery and LiDAR data, comparing shallow models, U-Net-based encoder–decoder networks, pre-trained models such as YOLOv8 and SEEM, and unsupervised pipelines tuned with genetic algorithms. He also studies evolutionary and metaheuristic optimization, including a multimodal variant of artificial bee colony and genetic-algorithm feature selection for document classification. In addition, he has surveyed online deep learning for streaming data, covering concept drift and catastrophic forgetting.

name: Naeem Khademi
summary: Naeem Khademi works on information and communication technology for road tunnel safety and on Internet transport protocols. His tunnel research applies deep learning to forecast traffic volume, speed and rush hours from Norwegian tunnel data, simulates inertial positioning where satellite signals are unavailable, and proposes a framework for risk-aware decision support. His networking work uses emulated testbed experiments to assess congestion control for QUIC over geostationary satellite links.

name: Nan Zhang
summary: Nan Zhang works on petroleum and subsurface engineering, covering CO2 storage and enhanced oil recovery in tight and shale reservoirs, well monitoring, and drilling automation. The work combines laboratory core-flooding experiments with NMR and visualization, reservoir simulation, machine-learning surrogate models (physics-informed networks, GANs, self-attention, federated learning) and automated pressure transient analysis of permanent gauge data. It also covers downhole sensing and control, including MEMS accelerometer calibration, attitude data compression on FPGA, and rotary steerable system control tested by hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

name: Nejm Saadallah
summary: Nejm Saadallah works on the formal modeling and verification of blockchain protocols, focusing on justification layers that let resource-constrained light clients verify block finalization. The work specifies the Beefy protocol used in the Polkadot ecosystem in TLA+ and checks safety, liveness and an inductive invariant with the TLC and Apalache model checkers. It also compares the formal specification against Polkadot's informal specification and implementation, identifying a deadlock in the informal specification.

name: Nolwenn Bernard
summary: Nolwenn Bernard studies conversational recommender systems and conversational information access agents, focusing on how to train, evaluate and debug them using user simulation, including large language model-based simulators. Her work produces toolkits, benchmarking platforms, datasets and evaluation methodologies, such as simulation toolkits, a crowdsourced pairwise benchmarking arena and an e-commerce dialogue collection. She also works on personal knowledge graph management and on systematic reviews of fairness, accountability, transparency and ethics in information retrieval.

name: Peter Røysland Aarnes
summary: Peter Røysland Aarnes works on automated fact-checking with large language models, focusing on how reliably they verify claims that involve numbers. His publications use counterfactual explanations, controlled numerical perturbations and adversarial training to test and improve model robustness and interpretability, evaluated on the QuanTemp dataset. He has also applied fine-tuned transformer models, data augmentation and cross-language transfer to detect check-worthy claims in English, Dutch and Arabic political debates and Twitter data.

name: Petra Galuscakova
summary: Petra Galuscakova works on information retrieval, with a focus on evaluating how retrieval systems perform as documents, queries and relevance judgments change over time, including organising the LongEval evaluation lab. Her work also covers retrieval-augmented generation with large language models, applied to NASA aerospace documentation and clinical decision-making with electronic health records, as well as reproducibility studies, neural reranking and relevance judgment depth. Further work includes fact-checking of numerical claims and navigation interfaces for speech archives, using benchmark evaluation, user studies and dataset creation.

name: Reggie Davidrajuh
summary: Reggie Davidrajuh works on Petri net modeling and simulation of discrete-event systems, centered on GPenSIM, a MATLAB-based simulator he developed. His publications extend the tool with features such as modular nets, delayed transitions, application interfaces and zero testing, and use it for supervisory control, queuing, scheduling and structural analysis of job completion time. He applies these models to manufacturing and AGV charging, warehouse robotics, retail checkout, city traffic, multiprocessor scheduling and game analysis, and has compared Petri net and differential equation SIR epidemic models numerically.

name: Shaima Ahmad Freja
summary: Shaima Ahmad Freja works on detecting early dementia from the language people use in speech transcripts, applying natural language processing and machine learning. Her studies use DementiaBank data, including the Pitt Corpus and ADReSS challenge sets, and compare classical classifiers with transfer learning and fine-tuned large language models such as BERT variants, Mistral and Llama, using parameter-efficient methods like LoRA and QLoRA. The work is aimed at healthcare screening and diagnostic support for neurodegenerative disease.

name: Solveig Kristina Hammonds
summary: Solveig Kristina Hammonds works on deep learning for detecting and predicting Alzheimer's disease from structural MRI, with emphasis on how reliable and fair the models are. Her studies compare ensemble decision strategies, examine model calibration, and run subgroup analyses by gender. She has also developed a zero-shot multimodal approach that combines MRI embeddings from the SigLIP foundation model with routinely collected clinical variables to estimate early disease risk, using ADNI data.

name: Stein Ørn
summary: Stein Ørn studies cardiovascular disease and the heart's response to exercise, covering exercise-induced troponin release, myocardial work and efficiency, and coronary artery calcification in recreational athletes. His work also includes registry-based studies of heart failure treatment and outcomes in Norway, and imaging studies after myocardial infarction using cardiac MRI with machine learning and deep learning segmentation. Methods include echocardiography, cardiac biomarkers, coronary CT, heart rate variability, observational cohorts and classification models, with applications in sports cardiology, heart failure care and post-infarction assessment.

name: Syed Tahir Hussain Rizvi
summary: Syed Tahir Hussain Rizvi works on applied machine learning and deep learning, with studies spanning time series forecasting, video-based action and crowd behavior recognition, and missing-data imputation. He also applies convolutional, Transformer and ensemble models to medical imaging (brain tumor, prostate cancer, skin cancer, COVID-19), newborn resuscitation video analysis, and sensor-glove sign language recognition. Other work covers social media sentiment analysis after disasters, comparisons of IPv6 routing protocols in simulated networks, and fuzzy control algorithms for vehicle motion simulators.

name: Thilina Dhanushka Kalahe Pathirana
summary: Thilina Dhanushka Kalahe Pathirana works on security and dependability of 5G mobile networks and Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) systems that support mission-critical services. His publications cover a survey of joint security and dependability modeling, a two-level analytical model for estimating the availability of 5G-MEC systems under different redundancy settings, and the use of threshold secret sharing with trust-based node selection to protect and keep edge-stored data available.

name: Tom Ryen
summary: Tom Ryen's publications focus on artificial intelligence and its effects on society, with attention to opportunities, challenges and social change. Much of the work addresses education, including how generative AI such as ChatGPT affects teaching, assessment and the future of degree programmes. The outputs are mainly talks and outreach-style contributions in Norwegian, along with a piece on the University of Stavanger's AI strategy and its plans for a national AI centre.

name: Tomasz Wiktorski
summary: Tomasz Wiktorski works on applied machine learning and natural language processing, with a strong focus on the drilling and subsurface industry. His publications cover large language model question answering, retrieval-augmented generation, domain-adapted embeddings, ontology mapping for data standards, and deep learning for rate of penetration prediction using transfer and continual learning. He also applies signal processing and machine learning to physiological data such as heart rate variability and blood pressure in studies of coronary artery calcification and exercise, and has worked on distributed acoustic sensing, social media text analysis and early childhood educational robots.

name: Tormod Drengstig
summary: Tormod Drengstig studies mathematical modelling of biomolecular regulatory systems, focusing on negative-feedback controller motifs such as basic and antithetic controllers. The work combines structural identifiability analysis, applied across a large set of motif structures and measurement combinations, with parameter estimation using augmented extended Kalman filters under noise-free and noisy conditions. These methods address which measurements are needed to determine model parameters uniquely in biological models with limited observable outputs.

name: Trygve Christian Eftestøl
summary: Trygve Christian Eftestøl works on machine learning and signal and image analysis for clinical problems. His publications cover deep learning on MRI and histopathology slides for Alzheimer's disease, prostate cancer, bladder cancer and cardiac injury, as well as ECG and defibrillator signal analysis, statistical risk modelling in cardiac arrest and newborn resuscitation, EEG classification of neurodegenerative disorders, and circulating tumor DNA detection in pancreatic cancer. Methods include ensemble and weakly supervised learning, model calibration and fairness evaluation, parametric survival models, and a systematic review of wearable cueing technology in Parkinson's disease.

name: Vinay Jayarama Setty
summary: Vinay Jayarama Setty studies automated fact-checking, covering claim detection, claim normalization, evidence retrieval, stance detection and claim verification, with particular attention to numerical claims and multilingual settings. His work uses large language models, multi-task fine-tuning, test-time scaling, sparse and dense retrieval, and index compression, and builds benchmarks, annotation tools and shared-task evaluations such as the CLEF CheckThat! labs. Application areas include live fact-checking of audio streams and podcasts, political debates, and web-based evidence for combating misinformation.

name: Yao Lu
summary: Yao Lu applies deep learning to medical imaging, Alzheimer's disease risk prediction, remote sensing object detection and IoT-based time series forecasting. The work includes segmentation of prostate MRI under varying scan protocols, normative modelling and multimodal embeddings that combine brain MRI with routine clinical variables, and an improved YOLOv8 detector for aerial imagery. Other publications cover smart home energy prediction with edge computing, transformer and LSTM models and explainability methods, as well as stroke prediction from wearable EMG signals.

name: Øyvind Meinich-Bache
summary: Øyvind Meinich-Bache develops AI and computer vision methods, including deep learning on thermal and visible light video and on audio, to detect births and recognize resuscitation activities such as ventilation, stimulation and suction in newborn care. The work also covers clinical observational studies of newborn heart rate and stimulation, consent-based data collection with blockchain support, mothers' acceptability of recording, and analysis of resuscitation timelines. Applications centre on delivery-room documentation, quality improvement and clinical decision support, with additional work on semi-supervised learning, vision-language models and interpretability for video action recognition.

name: Aigul Taimour Alvi
summary: Aigul Taimour Alvi works on applying deep learning and machine learning to subsurface geoscience problems. Her publications compare neural network architectures (LSTM, Conv1D and fully connected models) with quantile regression to estimate reservoir parameters and their uncertainty from deep-sensing borehole electromagnetic logs to support geosteering, and use machine learning to classify seismic data for facies prediction. The work is aimed at oil and gas reservoir characterisation, including pinch-out structures on the Norwegian Continental Shelf.

name: Alejandro Escalona Varela
summary: Alejandro Escalona Varela studies the geology of the Norwegian North Sea and Barents Sea, combining seismic interpretation, well logs, detrital zircon provenance work, sequence stratigraphy and machine learning. The work covers Palaeozoic basin evolution and reservoir quality in the Rotliegend Group, and extends to the energy transition: hydrogen storage in Zechstein salt caverns, thermal modelling and geothermal repurposing of late-life oil fields such as Ula, and mercury in source rocks. He has also contributed to an autonomous acoustic survey system for buried archaeological objects in intertidal settings.

name: Ali Karimi
summary: Ali Karimi studies small-scale and building-level multi-energy systems that combine renewables, hydrogen, batteries, micro gas turbines, cogeneration and waste heat recovery. The work uses techno-economic and risk analysis (Monte Carlo, sensitivity analysis), 1D dynamic modelling, mixed integer linear programming, fuzzy control and a literature review of deep reinforcement learning for energy management. Applications include hospital energy supply, decentralized hydrogen-integrated energy systems and microgrids.

name: Anders Tokheim Hetland
summary: Anders Tokheim Hetland works on drilling engineering, focusing on estimating and controlling rate of penetration, drillstring vibration and downhole pressure. His work combines physics-based models such as lumped-mass drillstring dynamics and hydraulics with data-driven techniques including Ensemble Kalman Filtering, data analytics and rule-based control, tested through simulation and field data. The applications are real-time monitoring, drilling optimization, automation and detection of problems like kicks, lost circulation and packoffs.

name: Andrianifaliana Herimonja Rabenjafimanantsoa
summary: Andrianifaliana Herimonja Rabenjafimanantsoa studies multiphase and interfacial fluid flow, combining laboratory experiments, optical measurement and numerical simulation. Work includes laser-sheet imaging of capillary–gravity waves to estimate interfacial tension and viscosity, comparison of Volume of Fluid and Level Set solvers, and miscible displacement of shear-thinning fluids in a vertical channel. Application areas include non-intrusive liquid characterization for process monitoring and gas movement during well bullheading in drilling and well control.

name: Aqsa Batool
summary: Aqsa Batool works on chemistry and materials research spanning green extraction of plant bioactives, graphene-based adsorbents and electrocatalysts. Her publications cover deep eutectic solvent-ultrasound extraction of phenolics optimized with response surface methodology and neural networks, synthesis of poly(amidoxime)-grafted graphene oxide for removing hexavalent chromium from water, and hydrothermal preparation of graphite/iron oxide composites for methanol oxidation in fuel cells. Materials are characterized with FTIR, XRD, SEM and electrochemical techniques, and the work targets sustainable processing, water treatment and energy conversion.

name: Arash Mohammadi Vaniar
summary: Arash Mohammadi Vaniar works on the operation and planning of power and multi-energy systems, combining machine learning, metaheuristic optimization and reinforcement learning. His publications cover battery remaining useful life prediction with gradient boosting, neural networks and physics-based models, degradation-aware scheduling of an agricultural microgrid, and distribution network reconfiguration with capacitor placement tested on IEEE benchmark feeders. He has also reviewed deep reinforcement learning in multi-energy systems and assessed the resilience of interdependent gas and electricity networks under multiple hazards.

name: Arild Saasen
summary: Arild Saasen studies drilling fluids and well construction, focusing on the rheology and stability of oil-based and water-based muds, barite sag, and emulsion conditioning with shear guns. His work combines flow loop experiments, laboratory and field tests, CFD and analytical modelling of non-Newtonian annular flow, cuttings transport and hole cleaning. It also covers lost circulation materials, cement plug support tools, magnetic ranging for geothermal wells, and drilling waste handling.

name: Arnfinn Aas Eielsen
summary: Arnfinn Aas Eielsen works on improving the precision of digital-to-analogue converters by reducing errors from element mismatch, quantisation, and glitches. His methods include dithering, noise-shaping, moving-horizon model predictive control, and learning control, evaluated through simulation and experiments on off-the-shelf and custom hardware. Application areas include high-precision signal reconstruction, nanopositioning, and precision measurement electronics, plus thermal estimation for piezoelectric actuators.

name: Behzad Amiri
summary: Behzad Amiri studies subsurface energy and storage using reservoir simulation, including thermal and compositional models, analytical diffusion modelling, and machine-learning surrogate models with genetic-algorithm optimization. His work covers underground hydrogen storage, CO2 storage and enhanced oil recovery, and geothermal reuse of late-life offshore oil fields, with case studies from the Norwegian shelf such as Norne, Ula and Smeaheia. It also includes techno-economic assessment of storage operations and caprock screening criteria.

name: Benyamin Khademolomoum
summary: Benyamin Khademolomoum works on seismic reservoir characterization, combining rock physics modeling with machine learning and Bayesian stochastic inversion. The publications cover neural-network inversion of seismic attributes to acoustic impedance using rock-physics-generated pseudo-wells in an Iranian offshore oilfield, and a sampling-based workflow for generating and ranking posterior realizations of porosity, shale volume and water saturation in the Volve field. Applications focus on data-limited reservoirs and uncertainty quantification for subsurface modeling.

name: Bernt Sigve Aadnøy
summary: Bernt Sigve Aadnøy works on drilling and well engineering, covering well design, casing strength, well barriers, trajectory planning and drilling fluids. His publications combine analytical and numerical modelling, optimization algorithms, machine learning and laboratory testing, with case studies from field and drilling data. Application areas include extended reach and sidetrack well paths, rate of penetration estimation and optimization, wellbore temperature prediction, and well integrity in sour-gas and North Sea wells.

name: Bikash Adhikari

position.nb: Forsker i styring og regulering av digital til analog omformere svitsjede syst.

summary: Bikash Adhikari works on control and signal processing methods for improving digital-to-analogue converters, including model predictive and moving-horizon quantisation, noise-shaping and digital calibration to counter element mismatch and non-linearity. The work uses simulation and experiments on off-the-shelf converters, and compares mitigation methods on candidate integrated circuit designs. He also studies networked systems made of densely linked clusters, using singular perturbation and multi-time-scale modelling to design synchronisation controllers with guaranteed cost bounds.

name: Carita Augustsson
summary: Carita Augustsson studies the sedimentary geology of the Norwegian North Sea, focusing on Palaeozoic to Triassic basins, their structural evolution and the sources of their sediments. Her work combines seismic and well-log interpretation, core and facies analysis, detrital zircon dating and whole-rock geochemistry to reconstruct basin formation, sediment transport and reservoir quality, with applications to petroleum exploration. She has also applied machine learning to predict porosity and water saturation from well logs and has studied deltaic shoreline deposits in northeastern Mexico.

name: Dagfinn Søndenaa Sleveland
summary: Dagfinn Søndenaa Sleveland studies fluid flow in porous rock, combining core-plug experiments, analytical solutions and numerical simulation. The work examines forced and spontaneous water imbibition for oil displacement in water-wet sandstones, looking at how capillary forces, relative permeability and viscosity affect recovery and pressure behavior. It also applies the fluctuation dissipation theorem to thermally driven pressure fluctuations in fluid-saturated sandstone and chalk, linking molecular-scale effects to macroscopic flow.

name: Dan Sui
summary: Dan Sui works on vibration, acoustics and drilling engineering, combining physical modeling with machine learning and state estimation. Publications cover acoustic metamaterials, porous liners and composite panels for noise control, as well as drillstring dynamics, rate-of-penetration and wellbore pressure estimation, gas kick detection, directional drilling control and drilling automation. Methods include theoretical vibroacoustic models, field and laboratory experiments, neural networks, reinforcement learning, Kalman filtering and simulation, applied to pipelines, offshore drilling and machinery, and oil reservoirs.

name: Daniele Blancone
summary: Daniele Blancone studies the potential of underground hydrogen storage in salt caverns, with a focus on the Zechstein salt of the Norwegian North Sea. The work combines seismic and well log interpretation, GIS-based capacity screening, machine learning to map heterogeneities within salt, and 2D viscoelastic geomechanical modelling of cavern stability. It is aimed at the energy transition and energy security, and also covers the wider role of subsurface use on the Norwegian shelf, including CO2 storage and geothermal energy.

name: David Scott Hall
summary: David Scott Hall studies degradation and interfacial chemistry in lithium-ion batteries, with a focus on nickel-rich layered oxide cathodes and the solid-electrolyte interphase on graphite anodes. His work combines NMR and operando Raman (SHINERS), acoustic emission, atomic force microscopy and optical microscopy with chemo-mechanical modelling, mechanical testing, electrolyte additive trials and coating synthesis. Applications include designing electrolytes, cathode materials and cycling protocols for long-lived, high-energy cells, plus related work on oxide catalyst films for water oxidation and gas sensing in batteries.

name: Elvin Mirzayev
summary: Elvin Mirzayev studies CO2 storage in deep saline carbonate aquifers, using laboratory coreflooding of limestone with CO2-saturated brine and micro-CT imaging to examine how wormholes form and how rock porosity, permeability and mechanical strength change. These experiments vary injection rate, pore pressure, rock permeability, salinity and temperature. He also contributes to offshore work on methane seepage near wells, including a review of well plugging and abandonment and seabed survey cruise work using remotely operated vehicles, gas flux measurements and hydroacoustic imaging.

name: Foster Dodzi Gomado
summary: Foster Dodzi Gomado studies well cementing and zonal isolation for oil and gas wells, with emphasis on granite-based geopolymers as lower-carbon alternatives to Portland cement. Laboratory work covers hydraulic sealability, shear bond strength, linear expansion, compressive strength and slurry behavior at low temperatures, supported by calorimetry, microscopy and diffraction. Applications include shallow-depth cementing and plug and abandonment, including a regulatory review and sealing tests of stacked annular cement.

name: Fredrik Skaug Fadnes
summary: Fredrik Skaug Fadnes works on heat pump and building energy systems, using artificial neural networks and other data-driven models built from operational data to monitor performance, detect faults and support predictive control. His work covers sewage and wastewater heat pumps, CO2 heat pumps, geothermal borehole systems and the university campus energy plant, as well as microgrids combining wind power, hydrogen storage and micro gas turbines. Methods include machine learning, Modelica-based simulation, and techno-economic and design optimization, applied to municipal and residential buildings and local energy plants in collaboration with industry and municipalities.

name: Hallgjerd Håbakk Ravnås
summary: Hallgjerd Håbakk Ravnås studies underwater cultural heritage by combining marine geophysical surveys, such as sub-bottom profiling, multibeam and side-scan sonar, with sediment core analysis and diver inspection. Her work uses autonomous surface vehicles for non-invasive seabed and subsurface mapping, applied to a medieval harbour and shipwreck at Avaldsnes and to the Klostervågen test area in Norway. It also looks at how these survey methods and data interpretation can transfer to heritage detection ahead of offshore energy developments.

name: Hamed Sahebi

position.nb: forsker i intelligent og autonom boring

summary: Hamed Sahebi works on data-driven and AI-based methods for drilling operations in the oil and gas sector, with a focus on real-time monitoring and optimization of rate of penetration. His work combines trend analysis, drillstring vibration analytics, extremum seeking and rule-based control, and machine learning models, tested mainly in drilling simulators and with replayed field data. He also builds software systems, including microservice platforms with digital twins and LLM agents, and a web tool for 3D wellbore trajectory design and visualization.

name: Hans Joakim Skadsem
summary: Hans Joakim Skadsem studies well construction and well integrity, combining laboratory experiments, finite element and OpenFOAM CFD modeling, and pressure transient analysis. The work covers cement sheath sealing, microannulus leakage and repair, expanding cement additives, casing centralization, reverse-circulation cementing and fluid displacement in annuli and Hele-Shaw cells. Applications include oil and gas wells, plug-and-abandonment, geothermal wells, and drill string and bearing fluid dynamics.

name: Helleik Rosenvinge Syse
summary: Helleik Rosenvinge Syse studies building energy use and flexibility in Norway, combining day-ahead load forecasting, scheduling of virtual batteries and electric vehicles, and building performance simulation with measured data from dormitories, municipal buildings and a university living lab. His work also compares calculated and measured energy in energy performance certificates, examines how energy data infrastructure and access shape policy implementation, and contributes to electricity market design modelling for high shares of renewables.

name: Herimonja Andrianifaliana Rabenjafimanantsoa
summary: Herimonja Andrianifaliana Rabenjafimanantsoa studies liquid interfaces and multiphase flows, combining laboratory experiments, optical imaging and numerical simulation. One strand develops laser-sheet and inverse ray-tracing methods to reconstruct capillary and capillary–gravity wave surfaces so that interfacial tension and viscosity can be estimated without contact, alongside comparisons of simulation approaches for such waves. Another strand examines miscible displacement of shear-thinning fluids in vertical channels, including viscous fingering instabilities, and the rise of Taylor bubbles in an annulus.

name: Hibat Errahmen Djecta
summary: Hibat Errahmen Djecta works on AI-driven geosteering, the real-time steering of drilling trajectories under geological uncertainty. The publications combine generative adversarial networks, ensemble data assimilation, particle filters, dynamic programming and deep reinforcement learning to update subsurface models from logging-while-drilling data and recommend steering decisions. Work also covers sequence machine learning for probabilistic forecasting of layer boundaries, simulator-based validation, and interactive open-source demonstrations for hydrocarbon, geothermal and CO2 storage drilling.

name: Homam Nikpey Somehsaraei
summary: Homam Nikpey Somehsaraei works on modelling, simulation and optimization of energy systems, with a main focus on micro-gas turbines (including humidified and hydrogen-fuelled cycles) and on heat pumps, thermal storage and building energy use. His methods include physics-based and grey-box dynamic models, Modelica simulation, Taguchi and multi-objective optimization, and neural networks for condition monitoring and data denoising. Application areas include distributed power and heat generation, solar-assisted CO2 ground-source heating, phase change material cooling for residential buildings, and comparison of calculated and measured energy in municipal buildings.

name: Ivan Dario Pinerez Torrijos
summary: Ivan Dario Pinerez Torrijos studies enhanced oil recovery through Smart Water injection, tailoring brine chemistry to alter rock wettability in chalk, limestone and sandstone reservoirs. The work uses laboratory core experiments such as spontaneous imbibition and flooding, supported by surface and chemical analysis and geochemical simulation. It also examines how carbonated water interacts with reservoir and caprock minerals for CO2 storage, and how core restoration methods affect wettability reproducibility.

name: Jan Aage Aasen
summary: Jan Aage Aasen works on well integrity and barrier materials for oil and gas wells, including plug and abandonment. His publications combine laboratory testing of geopolymer and Portland cement sealants (shear and hydraulic bond strength, expansion, calorimetry) with characterization of 33-year-old field cement from a Norwegian well. He also uses analytical stress models and probability data to estimate burst limits of oval, hydrogen-sulfide-embrittled steel casing in a North Sea gas-condensate well.

name: Jassem Abbasi
summary: Jassem Abbasi studies multiphase flow in porous and fractured rocks, mainly using physics-informed neural networks to solve flow equations and to history-match core-scale experiments such as spontaneous imbibition and capillary pressure tests. His work also covers new PINN techniques (change of variables, physical activation functions, methods for shock fronts), hybrid deep learning to speed up numerical solvers, and machine learning for permeability prediction, alongside numerical modeling of centrifuge capillary pressure setups. Applications include CO2 storage, hydrocarbon recovery and special core analysis.

name: Jelena Popovic-Neuber
summary: Jelena Popovic-Neuber studies ion transport and electrode–electrolyte interfaces in batteries, with a focus on alkali metal, silicon, magnesium and aluminium electrodes, and on solid-state, polymer and liquid electrolytes. Her work relies on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, galvanostatic polarization, solid-state synthesis and mathematical modelling to measure interphase properties, transference numbers and diffusion, including sulfide-based potassium electrolytes. She also contributes reviews and roadmaps on solid electrolytes, binders and electrodics for energy storage, as well as a human geography perspective on energy communities.

name: Jonas Grill
summary: Jonas Grill studies ion transport and interphase behavior in battery materials, focusing on alkali metal (Li, Na, K), Mg, Al and silicon electrodes in contact with liquid, polymer and solid-state electrolytes. The work relies mainly on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, polarization experiments and mathematical modeling to measure quantities such as transference numbers, diffusion coefficients, activation energies and interphase resistance. Applications include post-lithium batteries, solid-state potassium electrolytes, polymer electrolytes and cation-conducting binders.

name: Jorunn Hamre Vrålstad
summary: Jorunn Hamre Vrålstad studies how lost circulation materials, which are added to drilling fluids to prevent fluid loss into underground formations, affect fluid flow behavior. The work measures the viscosity of fluids containing fresh and worn granular and cellulose fibre additives, models it with the Herschel-Bulkley approach using dimensionless shear rates, and compares it with the additives' effect on filtration loss. The application areas are drilling of geothermal, CO2 injection and petroleum wells.

name: Joshua Mugisha
summary: Joshua Mugisha works on pressure transient analysis and well testing for monitoring and controlling injection wells, using numerical flow simulation, analytical interpretation models and Python-based automated workflows applied to real-time downhole gauge data. His publications cover detecting induced fracture opening with step-rate tests, automated injection-rate control, and finding leakage along active and abandoned wells. The applications span oil and gas water injection, geothermal injectors (including a field case in Indonesia) and well testing for CO2 storage.

name: Jostein Djuve
summary: Jostein Djuve works on well construction materials for oil and gas wells, focusing on spacer fluids designed to work with rock-based geopolymer as an alternative to cement. The research uses rheology tuning with polymer and clay additives, surfactant adjustment for surface cleaning and water-wetting, and tests of compressive and tensile strength and heat evolution when fluids intermix. The work addresses mud displacement, zonal isolation and wellbore integrity in drilling and well cementing.

name: Kaan Kizmaz
summary: Kaan Kizmaz studies the electrochemical behavior of alkali metal electrodes (lithium, sodium and potassium) in contact with liquid battery electrolytes, using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and galvanostatic polarization in symmetric cells. This work examines interphase formation, charge transfer, diffusion and cationic transference numbers to understand degradation and stability in high energy density batteries. Related work covers polymer synthesis and self-assembly, including miktoarm block copolymers made by living anionic and ring-opening polymerization to produce nanoporous, redox-active templates characterized by cyclic voltammetry.

name: Kasra Saberi Beglar
summary: Kasra Saberi Beglar works on the operation and control of multi-energy systems, covering deep reinforcement learning, load forecasting and optimization-based pricing. The publications include a structured literature review of reinforcement learning for energy management, a data-driven study of day-ahead forecasting and storage-based flexibility using data from a Norwegian student dormitory, and a bi-level optimization model for dynamic pricing between energy providers and consumers. Application areas are building and urban energy management, demand response, electric vehicle and battery scheduling, and tariff design.

name: Kate Lorna Powell
summary: Kate Lorna Powell studies sediment provenance and depositional systems in ancient continental basins, with a focus on the Permian Rotliegend Group of the Norwegian North Sea. Her work combines detrital zircon U–Pb geochronology, facies analysis, palaeocurrent data from wells and palinspastic restoration to trace sediment sources, transport pathways and tectonic influences. The results are applied to understanding how sediment origin affects reservoir quality and to predicting reservoir distribution in subsurface energy-related settings.

name: Kenan Dikilitaş
summary: Kenan Dikilitaş studies language teacher education and higher education pedagogy, with a focus on action research, practitioner research and research-based teaching that positions students and teachers as researchers. His work also covers English-medium instruction, translanguaging, bilingual and CLIL education, and teacher identity, using methods such as scoping and systematic reviews, interviews, narrative inquiry and mixed-methods surveys. The settings range from preschools and schools to universities, mainly in Türkiye, along with international and online teacher communities.

name: Kim Andre Nesse Vorland
summary: Kim Andre Nesse Vorland studies geochemical and materials processes relevant to the energy transition, covering metal recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries and geological CO2 storage. His laboratory work includes optimizing leaching of lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese from black mass with citric acid and choline chloride solvents, and measuring how CO2 exposure changes porosity and permeability in Danish chalk.

name: Kjell Kåre Fjelde
summary: Kjell Kåre Fjelde works on gas behavior in oil and gas wells, studying how gas moves, expands and builds pressure during well control and drilling operations. His work combines drift-flux transient simulation, analytical models and laboratory flow-loop experiments, covering bullheading, kick migration in closed wells and gas unloading from marine risers. The studies address safety and equipment integrity questions in well kill, managed pressure drilling and offshore drilling.

name: Kristian Gjerstad
summary: Kristian Gjerstad studies drilling fluid rheology and wellbore hydraulics, including thixotropic and gelling behavior, stress-overshoot tests, and the effect of temperature on bentonite and polymer muds. He develops physical, data-driven and hybrid models, such as fast water density polynomials and pressure reconstruction from distributed downhole sensors, validated against laboratory measurements, historical well data and digital-twin simulations. Applications include real-time estimation of downhole pressure, hole cleaning, gel breaking pressure and swab/surge effects from heave in drilling operations, including HPHT wells.

name: Lothar Schulte
summary: Lothar Schulte works on subsurface characterisation, combining seismic and well-log data to study faults and to estimate rock properties such as porosity, water saturation and shale volume. His work includes fault modelling, stress and fracture prediction using elastic dislocation models, and the analysis of low acoustic impedance in fault zones in the Wisting field, Barents Sea. He also applies and tests machine learning and deep learning methods, including transformer-based networks with uncertainty estimates, on synthetic models and on North Sea field data such as the Troll Field.

name: Lucas Volpi
summary: Lucas Volpi develops numerical models of particle-laden and non-Newtonian fluid flows, mainly using the lattice-Boltzmann method coupled with discrete element and finite element methods. His work addresses drilling operations, including hydraulic forces on drill-string tool-joints, drill-string whirling and vibration, cuttings transport and particle grinding. It also covers particle settling and shape effects, and torque measurement in rotational viscometry.

name: Mahmood Fani
summary: Mahmood Fani studies carbonated water and CO2-rich brine injection for enhanced oil recovery and geological CO2 storage in sandstone and chalk reservoirs. The work uses laboratory core flooding, spontaneous imbibition, mineral exposure and surface reactivity tests, SEM/EDX/XRD analysis, and geochemical (PHREEQC) and compositional wellbore simulation. It also covers low salinity water flooding, microfluidic pore-scale methods for chemical EOR, and thermal and pressure effects on wellbore integrity during intermittent CO2 injection.

name: Mahmoud Khalifeh
summary: Mahmoud Khalifeh's research centres on wellbore sealing and well integrity, especially rock-based and one-part geopolymers as lower-carbon alternatives to Portland cement for plug and abandonment, shallow cementing, remedial operations and CO2 storage. Laboratory work covers mechanical, hydraulic sealability, durability and microstructural testing under CO2, H2S and brine exposure, complemented by pore-scale numerical and thermodynamic modeling and reviews of regulations and offshore well leakage. The publications also address drilling fluid stability, supplementary cementitious materials from industrial slag, and leaching of critical metals from lithium-ion battery waste with deep eutectic solvents.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Masoumeh Amiri Mikal
summary: Masoumeh Amiri Mikal studies the properties and stability of drilling fluids used in well construction, covering both oil-based emulsion muds and water-based bentonite muds. Her work combines laboratory measurements, such as viscometer-based rheology across temperatures, shear rates and concentrations, with model fitting using the Herschel-Bulkley model, as well as field and mud plant tests of shearing equipment offshore Norway. The applications include maintaining emulsion quality, preventing barite sag and controlling mud behavior at elevated temperatures.

name: Mesfin Belayneh Agonafir
summary: Mesfin Belayneh Agonafir works on drilling and well engineering, covering drilling fluid formulation and testing, wellbore hydraulics and temperature, well control, and well barriers. His methods combine analytical and physics-based modelling, laboratory experiments on lubricity, rheology and lost circulation materials, and machine learning applied to field telemetry and safety datasets. The work is aimed at the oil and gas industry, including safer, more efficient drilling and the use of digital tools in well planning.

name: Mohammad Mansouri
summary: Mohammad Mansouri works on decentralised and multi-energy systems, covering techno-economic and life cycle assessment of biogas, hydrogen, solar and storage-based power supply, as well as optimisation and deep reinforcement learning for energy management and distribution networks. A second strand focuses on gas turbines and micro gas turbines, using physics-based and 1D transient models, machine learning and regression to study control, fault diagnostics and remaining useful life, especially with hydrogen fuel. Further work covers building-level load forecasting and flexibility, and phase change material cooling systems for residential buildings.

name: Mohsen Assadi
summary: Mohsen Assadi's publications cover decentralized and low-carbon energy systems, including micro gas turbines running on hydrogen and natural gas blends, hydrogen systems with electrolyzers, fuel cells and batteries, and microgrids with renewables. The work combines experiments, 1D and CFD simulation, digital twins, neural networks, MILP scheduling, and Monte Carlo risk analysis to assess technical and economic performance. It also addresses shallow and deep geothermal energy (borehole heat exchangers, thermal response tests, repurposed oil and gas wells), wave energy converters, home energy management and distribution network reconfiguration, with case studies mainly in Norway, Poland and Portugal.

name: Mojtaba Ghaedi
summary: Mojtaba Ghaedi studies subsurface storage of hydrogen and CO2 in porous rock, covering capillary sealing, caprock and salt cavern leakage, density-driven convection, diffusion, and geochemical reactions with minerals such as calcite and pyrite. His methods include analytical formulations, PHREEQC geochemical and reactive transport modeling, reservoir simulation (e.g., Norne field), Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, pressure-decay diffusion experiments, and literature reviews. He has also applied modeling to calcite scaling in geothermal wells and appears as an author on biomedical studies of a nanoparticle-loaded amniotic membrane for burn healing and of dexmedetomidine during surgery.

name: Muhammad Baqir Hashmi
summary: Muhammad Baqir Hashmi studies the performance, health monitoring and control of industrial and micro gas turbines, with emphasis on hydrogen-fueled machines and operation alongside variable renewable energy. His work combines physics-based simulation (e.g. GasTurb models validated against OEM or test-rig data) with machine learning, regression and particle-filter methods for fault diagnostics, degradation estimation and remaining useful life prediction. Application areas include decentralized power generation, retrofitting turbines for hydrogen, transient and load-change operation with control schedules, and the effect of faults and environmental conditions on efficiency and emissions.

name: Nestor Cardozo
summary: Nestor Cardozo's publications cover subsurface geoscience on the Norwegian shelf and beyond, combining seismic and well-log interpretation, deep learning and physics-based inversion, geomechanical and thermal modelling, and statistical verification of exploration forecasts. The work is applied to reservoir characterization, fault and fracture analysis (Wisting, Troll), salt-cavern hydrogen storage, geothermal reuse of late-life oil fields, and seismic attenuation and faulting in Colombia.

name: Nina Egeland
summary: Nina Egeland's publications span nursing education and breast cancer research. One paper compares national legislation on public health nurse education and services across the Nordic countries to identify ways the programmes could collaborate. Another is a protocol for a long-term observational biobank study in Western Norway that follows women with early-stage breast cancer using repeated blood and urine samples and patient-reported questionnaires to look for biomarkers of relapse and to study fatigue and quality of life.

name: Nisar Ahmed
summary: Nisar Ahmed develops seismic inversion methods that estimate subsurface elastic, petrophysical and attenuation properties from seismic reflection data. The work uses adjoint-state gradients with quasi-Newton optimization, genetic algorithms, Bayesian approaches and deep learning (convolutional transformer networks), and rock-physics models for time-lapse saturation and pressure monitoring. Applications include reservoir characterization in the North Sea (Troll, Edvard Grieg, Smeaheia CO2 storage), along with seismic facies, geomechanics and seismic hazard studies in South Asia.

name: Norman Urrez
summary: Norman Urrez studies the Palaeozoic and early Mesozoic basins of the Norwegian North Sea, reconstructing their tectonic evolution, sediment routing and burial history. The work combines seismic interpretation, well log and core analysis, palinspastic restoration, petrography and detrital zircon U–Pb geochronology. It is applied to petroleum exploration, linking sediment provenance, facies and salt influence to reservoir quality and petroleum system risks in pre-salt successions.

name: Pål Østebø Andersen
summary: Pål Østebø Andersen studies multiphase flow in porous media, using numerical simulation, analytical solutions and physics-informed neural networks. His work covers capillary and imbibition processes, interpretation of core-flood and centrifuge experiments, and enhanced oil recovery methods such as low-salinity and polymer flooding. He also applies reservoir and wellbore modeling to subsurface energy storage and reuse, including hydrogen storage, CO2 storage, aquifer thermal storage and geothermal repurposing of mature offshore fields.

name: Raoof Gholami
summary: Raoof Gholami's research centres on subsurface energy storage and geothermal energy, particularly underground hydrogen storage and CO2 storage in porous formations and salt caverns. His work combines numerical and analytical modelling, geochemical reaction simulation with PHREEQC, and laboratory measurements to study gas mixing, dispersion, diffusion, leakage, caprock sealing, mineral reactions and salt mechanics. He also models shallow geothermal borehole heat exchangers and scaling in geothermal wells, using field and plant operating data from sites such as Norway, Portugal and the USA.

name: Reidar Brumer Bratvold
summary: Reidar Brumer Bratvold's publications address sequential decision-making under uncertainty in subsurface energy, especially geosteering of wells. His work combines reinforcement learning, decision transformers, particle filters and deep neural networks with statistical analysis of expert decisions. He also studies forecast verification and calibration in petroleum exploration on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, real option valuation, multi-objective decision analysis for energy transition projects, and Bayesian optimization of reservoir production.

name: Reidar Inge Korsnes
summary: R. I. Korsnes studies the mechanical and geochemical behavior of subsurface rocks and wellbore materials using laboratory triaxial testing, core flooding, and microscopy and diffraction analysis. The work covers chalk and carbonate reservoirs (brine-rock reactions, mineral precipitation, water weakening, temperature cycling, and chemical strengthening for fracturing), creep behavior of impure Zechstein salt for hydrogen storage caverns, and granite-based geopolymers as sealing materials for wells. Applications include improved oil recovery, CO2 and hydrogen storage, geothermal wells, and wellbore integrity.

name: Remus Gabriel Hanea
summary: Remus Gabriel Hanea works on ensemble-based history matching, data assimilation and optimization under uncertainty for subsurface reservoirs. His publications use methods such as ES-MDA, Bayesian seismic inversion, facies modeling, localization, derivative-free and stochastic-gradient optimization, and physics-informed neural networks. Applications include CO2 storage monitoring with 4D seismic data, oil field development planning, well trajectory design and decision support, with some extension to wind, geothermal and solar projects.

name: Ressi Bonti Muhammad
summary: Ressi Bonti Muhammad's research applies reinforcement learning, including Deep Q-Networks and dual-network variants, to sequential decision-making under uncertainty. Most of the work combines these methods with particle filters to automate geosteering, steering well trajectories in real time using well-log data. The methods are tested in synthetic and industrial simulator environments, including a cloud-based geosteering platform where an automated robot is compared with human experts, and the same decision framework is also applied to energy-transition investment planning.

name: Rune Wiggo Time
summary: Rune Wiggo Time studies fluid mechanics through two linked strands: optical measurement of capillary–gravity waves to determine interfacial tension and viscosity, and numerical modelling of complex flows. The measurement work uses laser sheet imaging, inverse ray-tracing and high-speed cameras, with simulations in OpenFOAM and COMSOL comparing interface-capturing methods. The modelling work uses the lattice-Boltzmann method, finite elements and discrete element methods to examine drill-string and tool-joint fluid forces, non-Newtonian rheology, viscometry, particle settling and Taylor bubbles, mainly for drilling and process-monitoring applications.

name: Sadegh Ahmadpour

position.nb: Stipendiat i hydrogen lagring i porøse medier

summary: Sadegh Ahmadpour studies fluid transport and reactions in porous subsurface formations, with a focus on underground hydrogen storage and CO2 storage. The work combines numerical simulation, including PHREEQC reactive transport and advection-dispersion models, with new mathematical formulations and laboratory pressure-decay measurements of gas diffusion in water and brine. Topics include hydrogen dispersion and loss, density-driven convection, hydrogen sulfide formation from pyrite and sulfate reactions, cushion gas selection, and multiphase relative permeability.

name: Samitha  Weerakoon
summary: Samitha Weerakoon studies decentralized low-carbon energy systems, with a focus on micro gas turbines, hydrogen technologies, microgrids and shallow geothermal systems. The work uses techno-economic assessment, Monte Carlo risk analysis, mixed-integer optimization, neural network prediction, 1D and CFD simulation, digital twins and experiments on electrolyzer and fuel cell units, as well as operational data from borehole heat exchanger fields. Applications include day-ahead market scheduling, natural gas-to-hydrogen fuel transitions, building heating and cooling, and wave energy converters, with case studies in Norway, Portugal and other European cities.

name: Seyed Hasan Hajiabadi
summary: Seyed Hasan Hajiabadi studies granite-based geopolymers as alternatives to Portland cement for sealing wells used in carbon capture and storage and in sour gas settings. His work combines mix design, mechanical testing (uniaxial and triaxial), permeability and flow-through exposure experiments, and microstructural analysis (XRD, SEM-EDS, FTIR, CT), together with pore-scale reactive transport modelling of carbonation. He has also examined drilling fluids and clay surface modification, including nanocomposite-based muds and formation damage imaged with CT.

name: Siv Marie Åsen
summary: Siv Marie Åsen works on polymer flooding for enhanced oil recovery, with a focus on how polymer solutions flow and build resistance in porous media. Her publications combine laboratory core-flood experiments at centimetre and metre scale with mathematical modelling to identify parameters, and examine factors such as temperature, salinity, flow velocity and time for thermo-thickening associative polymers. Her work also covers workflow recommendations for applying polymer flooding on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, including environmental and carbon footprint considerations, and participation in the NCS2030 industry project.

name: Skule Strand
summary: Skule Strand's publications address enhanced oil recovery and CO2 storage in porous reservoir rocks such as chalk, limestone, sandstone and diatomite. Using laboratory methods including spontaneous imbibition, core flooding, mineral-brine reactivity tests, microscopy and geochemical modelling, the work studies wettability alteration with tailored Smart Water brines, polysulphate additives, ionic liquids and carbonated water. Applications include North Sea chalk fields, produced water reuse, and the integrity of reservoir and caprock minerals during CO2 injection.

name: Slawosz Adrian Kleszcz
summary: Slawosz Adrian Kleszcz studies energy systems and thermal-fluid engineering, combining experiments with numerical modelling. The publications cover techno-economic and risk assessment of micro gas turbine combined heat and power units running on natural gas and hydrogen blends in Norway, a periodic counterflow heat exchanger for heat and moisture recovery in building ventilation, and CFD-validated flow measurement with multi-hole orifices in turbulent pipe flow.

name: Steinar Evje
summary: Steinar Evje works on mathematical and computational modeling of nonlinear partial differential equations, especially identifying unknown flux and diffusion functions of conservation laws and convection-diffusion equations from observed data. His methods combine symbolic neural networks, graph neural networks, entropy-satisfying numerical schemes and Bayesian ensemble Kalman filter inversion. He applies these to multiphase flow, gas leakage along wells in CO2 storage, parameterized ODE learning, and continuum models of tumor progression, migration and interstitial fluid pressure.

name: Tale Egeberg Aasland
summary: Tale Egeberg Aasland studies fluid flow using direct numerical simulation, mainly vortex dynamics, shear layer behaviour and flow regimes around straight and curved tandem cylinders at moderate to turbulent Reynolds numbers. More recent work combines laboratory experiments with OpenFOAM simulations to examine displacement of one fluid by another, including shear-thinning fluids, in a horizontal annulus with a washout section. The work is relevant to bluff-body flow and fluid forces on slender structures, and to annular displacement flows such as those in well operations.

name: Thomas Meldahl Olsen
summary: Thomas Meldahl Olsen works on near-surface geophysical mapping, especially high-resolution sub-bottom profiling and chirp sonar carried on autonomous surface vehicles to image buried objects and sediment layers in shallow and intertidal waters. His publications apply these methods to underwater archaeology, including a buried medieval shipwreck at Avaldsnes and a seabed survey in Klostervågen designed to guide heritage assessment ahead of offshore development. He has also combined ground-penetrating radar, drilling, aerial imagery and laser scanning to build a 3D subsurface model of an urban lake area in Stavanger.

name: Tina Puntervold
summary: Tina Puntervold studies enhanced oil recovery and CO2 storage in chalk, limestone, sandstone and diatomite reservoirs, focusing on wettability, capillary forces and rock-brine interactions. Her laboratory work uses spontaneous imbibition, core flooding, mineral and brine analysis (SEM, EDX, XRD, ion chromatography) and geochemical modelling to test modified brines, carbonated water, additives such as polysulphate, ionic liquids and nanoparticles. The applications are North Sea and other reservoirs, produced water reuse, and the suitability of outcrop rocks as analogues for reservoir material.

name: Tomasz Adam Skrzydlo
summary: Tomasz Adam Skrzydlo works on heterogeneous catalysis for chemical production and hydrogen generation. His publications examine how silver catalysts behave and change shape during the oxidation of methanol, CO and hydrogen, using a structured reactor and scanning electron microscopy to link gas composition to activity and surface restructuring. He also studies catalytic cracking of methane to produce hydrogen, including nickel-iron hydrotalcite-derived catalysts and the carbon nanotubes formed.

name: Veronika Abdulina
summary: Veronika Abdulina studies the mineralogy and petrophysics of porous reservoir rocks, mainly diatomite and chalk, using X-ray diffraction, mercury intrusion, surface area analysis and spontaneous imbibition tests to link composition, pore structure and wettability to oil recovery and CO2 storage. She also investigates hydrated iron sulfate minerals and related synthetic compounds with in situ single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis and magnetic measurements across wide temperature ranges and low vacuum, with relevance to Mars surface conditions.

name: Victor Nogueira Lima
summary: Victor Nogueira Lima studies oil well cement and the integrity of cement barriers in wells, including plugging and abandonment. The work uses laboratory and full-scale experiments such as triaxial, push-out, shear bond, seepage and tracer tests, with rheology and microstructural analysis (XRD, SEM, micro-CT), to examine expanding additives, fiber reinforcement, acid gas exposure, rock-cement interfaces and microannulus sealing. A smaller set of publications covers fiber-reinforced concrete under impact loading.

name: Wendpanga Jean Donald Minougou
summary: Wendpanga Jean Donald Minougou studies underground hydrogen storage, with a focus on salt caverns in impure Zechstein salt and on porous reservoirs. The work combines laboratory tests on salt cores (mineral characterization, hydrogen diffusion, creep and cyclic loading) with geochemical and bio-reactive transport modeling of hydrogen sulfide generation and biomethanation. It also uses machine learning trained on reservoir simulations to predict hydrogen production and residual volumes during cyclic storage.

name: Wiktor Waldemar Weibull
summary: Wiktor Waldemar Weibull works on seismic inversion, developing nonlinear amplitude-versus-offset, pre-stack and post-stack methods that use adjoint-state gradients and quasi-Newton optimization to estimate elastic properties, attenuation and reservoir changes. His work also covers Bayesian rock physics inversion, deep learning compared with physics-based approaches, full waveform inversion and seismic forward modelling, tested on North Sea fields such as Troll, Volve, Edvard Grieg and Smeaheia. He also applies marine and near-surface geophysics, including autonomous surface vehicle chirp surveys of buried shipwrecks and integrated 3D subsurface models of urban areas.

name: Yao Zhang
summary: Yao Zhang studies how one fluid displaces another in confined geometries such as pipes, vertical ducts and Hele-Shaw cells, with emphasis on shear-thinning (power-law) and Newtonian fluid pairs. The work combines laboratory experiments, including a dye and spectroscopy method for measuring micrometre-scale residual oil films, with OpenFOAM simulations, a gap-averaged two-dimensional model and linear stability analysis of viscous fingering. The findings relate to oil recovery, well cementing, pipeline cleaning and microfluidic applications.

name: Yasaman Cheraghi
summary: Yasaman Cheraghi works on sequential decision-making under uncertainty in the energy sector, with a focus on automated geosteering of horizontal wells. Her work combines reinforcement learning with particle filters and generative geomodeling, benchmarks automated steering against human experts using data from a large geosteering competition, and applies statistical analysis to expert decisions. She has also compared reinforcement learning with least squares Monte Carlo for real option valuation, modeled energy-transition investment strategies, and built neural network tools for screening enhanced oil recovery methods.

name: Zhixin Yu
summary: Zhixin Yu's publications cover materials chemistry for energy and environmental applications, including electrocatalysts for water electrolysis, CO2 and nitrate reduction, and CO2-to-methanol and zeolite-catalysed reactions. Related work designs interfaces and protective layers for zinc and sodium metal battery anodes, ion-selective membranes for lithium extraction by electrodialysis, and electrospun or composite films characterised by positron annihilation spectroscopy. Methods combine materials synthesis, electrochemical and spectroscopic characterisation, and density functional theory or molecular dynamics simulation, with one paper on hyperchaotic systems for DNA-encoded image encryption.

name: Åsmund Aamodt Resell
summary: Åsmund Aamodt Resell studies the mechanics of slender rods and pipes in curved and irregular boreholes, and the fluid flow in the annular gaps around them. The work combines beam theory and finite element modelling, for example for drill strings and casing with centralizers, with analytical solutions and computational fluid dynamics for flow and forces in eccentric annuli. The applications are well construction and drilling, with links to journal bearings and biomedical annular geometries.

name: Øystein Arild
summary: Øystein Arild studies well integrity in permanent plugging and abandonment, focusing on how annulus cement behind casing is qualified as a barrier under the NORSOK D-010 standard. His work examines the 30 m cement length requirement and compares continuous with stacked bond log evidence, using flow and capillary pressure calculations alongside qualitative assessment of cracking and failure. He has also developed a method to evaluate missing-data imputation in real-time drilling logs by estimating bounds on the coefficient of determination.

name: Joachim Gümüs Kallevig
department: Faculty of Science and Technology (department not stated)
summary: Joachim Gümüs Kallevig writes about university leadership, governance and priority-setting under limited resources, drawing on debates within the University of Stavanger (UiS). His 2025 contributions are opinion pieces on how to handle disagreement respectfully within the institution and on the university's international strategy, including its participation in the ECIU university alliance.
