The pieces call for fact-based discussion and collaboration when making difficult strategic choices.

name: Kjersti Riiber
department: Faculty of Science and Technology (department not stated)
summary: Kjersti Riiber is associated with NCS2030, the National Centre for Sustainable Subsurface Utilization of the Norwegian Continental Shelf, hosted by the University of Stavanger with research and industry partners. Her publications are annual reports and a meeting presentation that document the centre's activities, collaborations, training courses and industry engagement from 2022 to 2025. The work relates to petroleum engineering and subsurface resource use, with attention to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and supporting energy security on the Norwegian continental shelf.

name: Norbert Puttkamer
department: Faculty of Science and Technology (department not stated)

name: Abhishek Banerjee
summary: Abhishek Banerjee studies solid-state hydrogen storage in titanium-iron (TiFe) alloys, focusing on how dopants such as niobium, vanadium and tantalum alter crystal structure and hydrogen uptake. The work combines arc-melting synthesis, synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction, EXAFS spectroscopy and hydrogen absorption and pressure-composition-temperature measurements to link structure with activation and sorption kinetics. Related activity includes machine learning and thermodynamic modelling for designing storage alloys, along with university teaching in physics and involvement in a materials science network.

name: Aksel Hiorth
summary: Aksel Hiorth works on computational modeling of fluid flow and reactive transport in porous media, using physics-informed neural networks, lattice Boltzmann methods and field-scale geochemical simulation (IORSim). His publications cover multiphase flow in fractured rock, low-salinity and surface-charge effects on carbonate oil recovery, pore-scale relative permeability, and reservoir applications on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. The same numerical methods are also applied to non-Newtonian and blood flow, including wall shear stress, coronary and Fontan hemodynamics, alongside work on course material design for lifelong learning.

name: Aleksi Kurkela
summary: Aleksi Kurkela works on the equation of state of dense matter in neutron stars, using Bayesian inference, Gaussian-process priors, and constraints from chiral effective field theory, perturbative QCD, gravitational-wave and X-ray observations to probe possible quark-matter cores. He also studies the early out-of-equilibrium stages of heavy-ion collisions with QCD kinetic theory, including jet quenching, heavy-quark diffusion, hydrodynamization attractors, a parton cascade code and neural-network evaluation of collision integrals. Related work covers transport properties such as the bulk viscosity of quark matter, using perturbative and holographic methods.

name: Alex Bentley Nielsen
summary: Alex Bentley Nielsen works on gravitational-wave astrophysics, with a focus on testing general relativity and the nature of black holes using signals from compact binary mergers. His work includes post-Newtonian waveform modelling, Bayesian parameter estimation, black hole ringdown analysis and constraints on modified-gravity models, as well as contributions to LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA event papers, catalogs, and searches for bursts, continuous waves and electromagnetic counterparts. He also contributes to planning the science case for the Einstein Telescope.

name: Alexander Karl Rothkopf
summary: Alexander Karl Rothkopf works on lattice QCD and quantum field theory, with a focus on heavy quarkonium and the static quark potential in the quark-gluon plasma, and on spectral function reconstruction as an inverse problem. He also develops variational action principles and symmetry-preserving numerical discretizations for initial value problems, covering constrained mechanics, gravity and wave propagation, and applies machine-learning-assisted complex Langevin methods and open quantum systems approaches to real-time dynamics and temperature probes in heavy-ion collisions.

name: Alexander Ulanovskii
summary: Alexander Ulanovskii works in harmonic and complex analysis, focusing on sampling and reconstruction in shift-invariant, Paley-Wiener and Bernstein spaces, and on Gabor frames built from Gaussian, hyperbolic secant and related generators. His publications derive sharp density conditions for sampling sets, including lattices, semi-regular patterns and families of lines or curves, and study the geometry of unit balls, with extreme and exposed points. He also treats completeness and basis properties of exponential and shift systems, with links to atomic and crystalline measures, lacunary polynomials and convolution theorems.

name: Anders Tranberg
summary: Anders Tranberg studies out-of-equilibrium quantum field theory, with a focus on real-time dynamics in the early universe such as post-inflationary reheating, tachyonic instabilities, bubble nucleation and stochastic inflation. His work develops and tests numerical methods, including 2PI effective action truncations of Kadanoff-Baym equations, classical-statistical lattice simulations and Lefschetz thimble Monte Carlo techniques for real-time path integrals. He also applies these tools to Q-ball dynamics and to instabilities in SU(2) gauge theory backgrounds.

name: Anna Maria Raukh
summary: Anna Maria Raukh works in algebraic geometry and topology, focusing on Fano threefolds and their connections to mirror symmetry. Her publications use cohomology computations, Euler characteristic calculations, and log-crepant resolutions to study smoothings of singular toroidal crossing spaces and the topology of nearby fibers. She also extends the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem to hypersurfaces in weighted projective spaces, with integer coefficients, to obtain cohomological invariants of Fano 3-folds.

name: Bjørn Henrik Auestad
summary: Bjørn Henrik Auestad's publications span sports cardiology and psychiatry. In cardiology, studies of middle-aged recreational athletes use echocardiography, cardiac troponin measurements and coronary imaging to examine how prolonged high-intensity exercise affects heart function, myocardial efficiency and non-obstructive coronary disease. In psychiatry, work includes a randomized trial comparing electroconvulsive therapy with pharmacological treatment in bipolar depression using patient-reported outcomes, and a registry-linked longitudinal study of suicidality trajectories in first-episode psychosis analyzed with growth mixture modelling and regression.

name: Cristhian David Hinostroza Vargas Machuca
summary: Cristhian David Hinostroza Vargas Machuca studies ion transport in solid-state superionic conductors, focusing on garnet-type lithium lanthanum zirconium niobium oxide. The work combines single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering, inelastic and quasi-elastic neutron scattering, density functional theory and machine-learned molecular dynamics to examine lithium disorder, lattice vibrations and diffusion mechanisms. The application domain is solid electrolytes for solid-state batteries and other energy materials.

name: Daniil Krichevskiy
summary: Daniil Krichevskiy works in theoretical particle physics, mainly on chiral effective field theories for QCD-like strongly coupled gauge theories, calculated to next-to-leading and next-to-next-to-leading order and fitted to lattice simulation data for Sp(4) gauge theory. He applies these results to composite pionic dark matter, including SIMP scenarios with vector mesons, dark photon portals and relic abundance, and to gravitational waves from dark-sector phase transitions. Earlier work covers large-charge effective field theory of the unitary Fermi gas and joint data-analysis algorithms for gravitational-wave and neutrino detectors.

name: David Ploog
summary: David Ploog works in algebraic geometry and representation theory, focusing on triangulated categories, their t-structures and hearts, and stability conditions. His publications study simple-minded collections and systems in cluster categories, their links to noncrossing partitions of Weyl groups, and extensions of Bridgeland stability spaces. He also writes on rigid divisors on surfaces, and one listed item is a paper on whether the universe is conscious.

name: Eirik Eik Svanes
summary: Eirik Eik Svanes studies the mathematical structure of heterotic string compactifications, focusing on moduli spaces, deformation complexes and cohomology for SU(3), G2 and related backgrounds, with a focus on supersymmetric vacua and anomaly cancellation. The work uses differential and algebraic geometry, generalised geometry, and holomorphic and topological field theories (including Kodaira-Spencer-type gravity and Chern-Simons theories) with one-loop calculations based on analytic torsion. Related papers cover moduli space metrics, effective field theory for gravity with a Kalb-Ramond field, Deligne cohomology for real line bundles, and discrete symmetries in five-dimensional superconformal theories.

name: Enrico Riccardi
summary: Enrico Riccardi works on computational modelling and machine learning, combining molecular simulation with statistical learning. His molecular work uses path sampling and molecular dynamics to study rare events such as drug unbinding from kinases, crystal phase transitions and thin film rupture in emulsions, and includes development of the PyRETIS software. He also applies regularised regression, random forests, neural networks and reinforcement learning to immune receptor data, histology images of fish livers and CO2 storage injection planning.

name: Eva Rauls
summary: Eva Rauls studies pillar[n]arene and dyn[4]arene macrocycles as materials for capturing and separating CO2 and other small gas molecules, combining density functional theory and tight-binding calculations with experimental work. Her research examines how cavity size and functional groups affect adsorption, host-guest binding and humid-condition performance, and includes synthesis, recrystallization, spectroscopic characterization and adsorption measurements of pillararene-based frameworks. She has also worked on scanning tunneling microscopy of single-molecule dielectric relaxation and on computational studies of 2D heterostructures.

name: Germano Nardini
summary: Germano Nardini works on gravitational-wave cosmology, focusing on how the LISA space detector can detect and reconstruct stochastic backgrounds from early-universe sources such as inflation, first-order phase transitions, cosmic strings and scalar-induced waves. He also studies primordial and stellar-origin black hole populations, and applies template-based forecasting, Bayesian parameter estimation and Gaussian-process inference to LISA data. His work links these signals to physics beyond the Standard Model, including warped extra dimensions and collider complementarity, and includes contributions to large collaborative white papers and design reports.

name: Gøran Jan Nilsen
summary: Gøran Jan Nilsen studies magnetic and soft-matter materials using neutron scattering, including inelastic, polarized and quasi-elastic techniques. The publications cover frustrated and quantum magnets (pyrochlores, spinels, honeycomb magnets, altermagnets, crystal electric field effects) that are interpreted with spin-wave theory, simulations and density functional calculations. They also cover molecular motion in liquids, mixtures and protein solutions, where polarization analysis and Bayesian methods separate collective from single-particle dynamics.

name: Helena Kolešová
summary: Helena Kolešová works on theoretical particle physics and cosmology, with a focus on dark matter and the early universe. Her publications cover cosmic-ray-boosted sub-GeV dark matter and its detection in DUNE and Xenon-1T, strongly coupled dark sectors in reheating, phase transitions and gravitational waves, and pion dark matter in QCD-like theories. She uses chiral effective field theory and next-to-leading-order calculations, fits to lattice data, and event-generator-based cross sections, and has also studied the chiral soliton lattice in QCD at finite density and magnetic field.

name: Helge Bøvik Larsen
summary: Helge Bøvik Larsen works on the role of universities and regional knowledge institutions in oil-dependent societies, focusing on the University of Stavanger and its ties to the petroleum economy. His publications examine how research and education could support critical reflection and a shift toward more sustainable ways of living, and they also address regional energy policy, including the case for investing in nuclear power in Norway's energy capital.

name: Helge Paul Ruddat
summary: Helge Paul Ruddat works in algebraic and symplectic geometry, focusing on mirror symmetry, logarithmic and tropical Gromov-Witten theory, and the Gross-Siebert program. His publications use scattering diagrams, theta functions, toric degenerations and log structures to study curve counts, open mirror maps and quantum periods, and to build Lagrangian torus fibrations on Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces. More recent work with Bridgeland connects cluster algebras, stability conditions, Donaldson-Thomas invariants and twistor spaces built from ADE quivers, using exact WKB analysis of ODEs.

name: Jan Terje Kvaløy
summary: Jan Terje Kvaløy is a statistician whose publications apply survival analysis, regression modelling and cumulative sum monitoring methods to health registry and clinical cohort data. The work covers nationwide registry studies of liver and pancreatic surgery, intensive care and vascular outcomes, and clinical studies in long-COVID, dry eye, breast cancer ctDNA and newborn care. It also includes trial and cost-effectiveness analyses of a maternal and newborn care programme in Tanzania.

name: Javier José Murgas Ibarra
summary: Javier José Murgas Ibarra works in mathematical string theory, focusing on the moduli of heterotic string compactifications and the Hull–Strominger system. He studies holomorphic topological field theories of Kodaira-Spencer type, computing one-loop partition functions in terms of holomorphic Ray-Singer torsions and analysing how anomalies are cancelled. His work also develops new cohomological and bundle-extension structures and links the theories to ten-dimensional supergravity and the swampland distance conjecture.

name: Jimmy Huy Tran
summary: Jimmy Huy Tran works on statistical methods for monitoring survival times in health registry data, developing cumulative sum (CUSUM) procedures built on relative survival and excess hazard models that adjust for risk factors and changing population mortality, with application to cancer registry data. He also works on computational statistics, studying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling, including adaptive tuning of diagonal scale matrices and extensions for piecewise smooth target densities, using numerical comparisons of sampling efficiency.

name: Jonas Elias El Gammal
summary: Jonas Elias El Gammal works on Bayesian inference and gravitational wave data analysis, with a focus on the LISA space mission. He develops Gaussian-process and active-learning methods (the GPry package) that cut the number of likelihood evaluations needed for parameter estimation, and applies them to cosmological data and to LISA sources such as white dwarf and black hole binaries. He also forecasts how LISA could constrain primordial curvature perturbations through scalar-induced gravitational waves, using binned, template-based and inflation-model approaches in a JAX-based pipeline.

name: Jörn Schulz
summary: Jörn Schulz develops geometric and statistical methods for shape analysis, including skeletal and elliptical tube representations that guarantee valid, non-self-intersecting mean shapes and support hypothesis testing of local shape differences, applied to structures such as the hippocampus in Parkinson's disease and autism-related multi-object complexes. He also conducts clinical and epidemiological studies using regression and survival models, covering orthostatic hypotension and cognitive decline in Parkinson's disease, sleep and cognition in older adults, and CT perfusion measures for predicting tissue outcome in acute ischemic stroke.

name: Konstantinos Alektoridis
summary: Konstantinos Alektoridis studies carbon dioxide capture using computational chemistry. His publication uses density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) calculations to compare how two functionalized dyn[4]arene macrocycles adsorb CO2, including binding inside the cavity and the uptake of multiple molecules until saturation. The work applies to materials for greenhouse gas capture and climate mitigation.

name: Martin Gunnar Gulbrandsen
summary: Martin Gunnar Gulbrandsen works in algebraic geometry, studying moduli spaces of geometric objects through Bridgeland stability conditions. His publication examines how the moduli space changes across walls, starting from the Hilbert scheme of pairs of skew lines in projective 3-space, and uses Mori theory to show the resulting spaces are smooth and projective. The work is theoretical and concerns the birational geometry of Hilbert schemes and related moduli spaces.

name: Olena Zavorotynska
summary: Olena Zavorotynska studies solid-state hydrogen storage materials, especially doped TiFe alloys and magnesium borohydride, linking their crystal structure to hydrogen uptake. She also works on zirconium and cerium metal-organic frameworks, including functionalized variants for gas capture and silver recovery from solution, and on mechanochemical synthesis of vanadium oxides. Her methods center on in situ and synchrotron X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption (EXAFS, NEXAFS), Raman and infrared spectroscopy, arc melting, and machine-learning-assisted alloy design.

name: Qian Zhang
summary: Qian Zhang works on building and energy systems, using Modelica-based physical modeling, neural-network surrogate models and deep learning forecasting with explainable AI. Applications include ground-source and CO2 heat pumps, solar-assisted heating, borehole thermal storage, phase change material cooling, micro gas turbine microgrids, and design and operation optimization with Taguchi, grey relational and scheduling methods. Further work covers fluid flow and heat transfer in flywheel energy storage systems and a review of polymer design for kinetic hydrate inhibitors.

name: Quoc Duy Ho
summary: Quoc Duy Ho studies materials mainly through first-principles computation (density functional theory, hybrid functionals, tight-binding, molecular dynamics and machine-learning force fields), with some experimental work on synthesis and gas adsorption. The work covers gas capture in pillar[5]arene frameworks, including CO2 adsorption and selectivity under dry and humid conditions. It also covers the electronic, magnetic and thermal properties of doped graphene, germanene and penta-graphene nanostructures, and point defects and dopants in wide-band-gap semiconductors such as β-Ga2O3 and ZnS for optoelectronic uses.

name: Shipra Singh
summary: Shipra Singh studies fluid flow in petroleum reservoirs using a 3D streamline-based modelling approach. Her work combines analytical streamline tracing in anisotropic reservoirs with two-phase displacement and pressure corrections near wells, and checks results against the open-source simulator OPM Flow. It is applied to how the vertical placement of injection and production perforations influences water breakthrough, oil recovery and the energy needed for pumping.

name: Sigbjørn Hervik
summary: Sigbjørn Hervik studies pseudo-Riemannian geometry and Lie theory, including left-invariant metrics on Lie groups analysed through group actions on Lie algebras and the null cone. He also builds new Einstein spaces by deforming symmetric ones while preserving curvature invariants, and applies dynamical systems methods to anisotropic cosmological models in general relativity with matter and gauge fields. His output also includes edited symposium volumes and popular science and educational pieces on cosmology, quantum mechanics and mathematics.

name: Tomas Brauner
summary: Tomas Brauner works in theoretical physics on effective field theories of spontaneous symmetry breaking, studying scattering amplitudes of pions, phonons and other Nambu-Goldstone bosons, including relativistic and nonrelativistic theories and dualities among them. He also uses chiral perturbation theory and numerical solution of field equations to map phases of quark matter, such as chiral soliton and vortex lattices, in magnetic fields and at finite density. His work further covers dipole and higher-form symmetries, a textbook on symmetry breaking, and a geometric treatment of electrostatic field lines for teaching.

name: Tore Selland Kleppe
summary: Tore Selland Kleppe develops Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms, with a focus on Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, including locally adaptive step sizes in the No-U-Turn Sampler, randomized and numerically integrated Hamiltonian processes, Riemann manifold metrics, scale tuning, and sampling on constrained domains. He also applies Bayesian state-space and stochastic volatility models to commodity markets, such as modeling the maturity structure of crude oil futures, and has examined how storage constraints shape oil price volatility. Work is evaluated through numerical experiments on multiscale and high-dimensional targets and on real data sets, with some methods released as software.

name: Tyson Ritter
summary: Tyson Ritter works in several complex variables, studying proper holomorphic embeddings of multiply connected domains into the complex plane. The publication builds parametric versions of the Andersén–Lempert procedure and Carleman-type approximation so that whole continuous families of domains can be embedded at once. The work is theoretical and rooted in complex analysis and approximation theory.

name: Vegard Undheim
summary: Vegard Undheim works in gravitational-wave astrophysics as a member of the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA Collaboration, analysing detector data from compact binary mergers and searching for other signal types such as supernova bursts, pulsar emission and signals linked to fast radio bursts. His work tests general relativity and the Kerr nature of black holes through ringdown spectroscopy and parametrized waveform fits, and also reports on individual black hole and neutron star coalescences and on catalog releases. He also does theoretical work, using effective field theory to derive post-Newtonian binary dynamics in a string-theory-motivated modified gravity model, and gives public talks on gravitational waves.

name: Adugna Deressa Akessa
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Adugna Deressa Akessa studies the mechanical behavior, microstructure and fracture of additively manufactured parts across polymers, fiber composites and metals. The work combines mechanical testing, electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction, heat treatment studies and numerical simulation, and it also applies Gaussian Process Regression to predict the properties of fused deposition modeling parts. Materials examined include PLA+, continuous carbon fiber with Onyx, 17-4 stainless steel from a Markforged Metal X printer, and Inconel 625 made by wire arc additive manufacturing, with a focus on process parameter optimization and testing standards.

name: Anders Sagvåg Birkemo
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Ayushi Rai
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Ayushi Rai studies thermochromic vanadium dioxide (VO2) and VO2/TiO2 bilayer thin films grown by pulsed laser deposition for energy-saving smart window coatings. Her work links growth conditions, substrate and buffer layer choice, phase composition, grain structure and residual strain to the metal–insulator transition and to optical and electrical switching. She uses a multimodal set of characterization methods, including transmission electron microscopy, electron diffraction, X-ray diffraction, confocal Raman and tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, and has also applied electron microscopy to atomic site distributions in thermoelectric materials.

name: Bjørn Helge Hjertager
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Bjørn Helge Hjertager works on computational modelling of accidental gas explosions, with a focus on porosity/distributed resistance (PDR) solvers that predict explosion consequences in geometrically complex facilities. The publication describes an international, pre-competitive collaboration to develop these solvers so that industrial facility design can use models that are accurate enough and run in reasonable time. The application domain is safety and risk assessment for industrial installations.

name: Bjørn Skaare
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Bjørn Skaare's publications address the dynamics and marine operations of offshore wind turbines, covering both bottom-fixed and floating concepts. The work uses time-domain and frequency-domain simulations, finite element soil modelling, potential-flow hydrodynamics and analytical stability derivations to study monopile decommissioning with a crane barge, platform motions and crew workability, and aerodynamic motion instabilities. It also includes a review of decommissioning methods for bottom-fixed foundations.

name: Bruno Villoria
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Bruno Villoria studies fatigue of welded details in orthotropic steel and aluminium decks of long-span suspension bridges under multiaxial, variable-amplitude loading. The work combines finite element modelling of bridge response, stochastic simulation of wind and traffic, fatigue testing of welded specimens, and new models for damage accumulation and grain-scale plasticity, including structural stress methods with cycle counting for non-proportional stress. These are compared with nominal stress, hot spot stress and critical plane approaches to improve fatigue life assessment of existing and future bridges.

name: Chern Fong Lee
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Chern Fong Lee studies floating offshore wind turbines and combined wind and wave energy systems, using fully coupled time-domain numerical models to analyse platform motions, mooring line tensions and power output. The work covers mooring design for intermediate water depths (synthetic rope, taut, shared and soft-chain systems), snap loads and extreme response statistics, dynamic power cables, simplified aerodynamic modelling, and vibration-based mooring damage detection. Applications include multi-rotor and wave-energy-integrated platforms, floating substations and wind farm arrays.

name: Daria Maria Larsson
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Daria Maria Larsson studies how lean management, agile methods and digital tools can improve efficiency and sustainability in engineering-to-order organisations, with a focus on office-based, knowledge-intensive engineering work. Her work relies on action research and industrial case studies, including interviews, SWOT analysis, digital and sustainable value stream mapping, balanced scorecards with analytical hierarchy process, and risk-based thinking. Application settings include Norwegian engineering firms, energy and power equipment companies, additive manufacturing, and the transition to a circular economy.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Dileepa Chathuranga Hettiarachchi
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Dileepa Chathuranga Hettiarachchi studies low-carbon cement binders, mortars and concrete in which large shares of Portland cement are replaced by silicomanganese slag, Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and ground granulated blast furnace slag. The work combines laboratory testing of strength, shrinkage, workability and heat of hydration with microstructural and mineralogical analysis (SEM, XRD, FTIR, TGA, calorimetry), and also uses response surface methodology to build predictive mix-design models. The application area is reducing clinker use and CO2 emissions in construction while keeping mechanical performance.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Dimitrios Pavlou
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Dimitrios Pavlou works on structural mechanics and integrity, including multiaxial and machine-learning-based fatigue life prediction, buckling of steel beams, and stress concentration in welded tubular joints. His studies also cover hydrogen-assisted cracking in pipeline steel through mechanical testing and fractography, statistical analysis of corrosion incidents in gas pipelines, and finite element and CFD modelling of offshore living breakwaters. He has also authored a textbook on advanced solid and structural mechanics and contributed to conference proceedings on AI and computational methods in engineering.

name: Endalkachew Mosisa Gutema
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Endalkachew Mosisa Gutema works on manufacturing and materials engineering, covering natural fiber (enset) polymer composites, 3D printing, carbon nanotube-reinforced aluminum composites, and machining and welding of metals. His methods include experimental testing, microscopy, finite element simulation, response surface methodology, Taguchi design, genetic algorithms and machine learning for process optimization. He also applies structural equation modeling and literature reviews to study how additive manufacturing affects supply chains, especially in Ethiopian footwear firms and textiles.

name: Espen Undheim
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Espen Undheim works on laser-based directed energy deposition, a metal additive manufacturing process, applied to super duplex stainless steel. The publication uses Taguchi-designed experiments and weighted grey relational analysis to optimise process settings such as laser power, deposition speed, pulse frequency and shielding gas flow. Builds are assessed through density measurement, tensile testing, electron microscopy and diffraction to link process parameters with melt pool shape, porosity, microstructure and ductility.

name: Even Englund
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Even Englund studies the fatigue strength and structural integrity of welded steel tubular structures, with emphasis on girth welds and repair welds made close together in S355 steel. The work is mainly experimental, combining cyclic tensile fatigue testing and S-N curve development with residual stress measurement, digital image correlation, strain gauges, microstructure and fractography, supported by finite element modelling. It targets offshore, pipeline, wind turbine tower and oil and gas applications, including specimen design for fatigue tests and the effect of post-weld heat treatment on pipe strength.

name: Fredrik Bjørheim
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Fredrik Bjørheim studies fatigue and corrosion in steel structures and pipelines, with a focus on the maintenance and service life of ageing infrastructure. His work combines nonlinear fatigue damage modelling based on S-N curves, experimental testing (hardness measurements, tension tests of additively manufactured steel), literature reviews of damage detection methods, and statistical analysis of pipeline incident data. He has also examined reuse of decommissioned offshore steel in buildings and surveyed civil engineering students' views of building information modelling.

name: Gerhard Ersdal
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Gerhard Ersdal works on the safety and integrity of offshore structures and on how existing structures are assessed for continued use. His publications combine structural reliability and risk analysis, fatigue testing and finite element analysis of tubular joints, and reviews of incident data from Norwegian continental shelf installations such as semisubmersibles and mooring systems. They also cover decision-making under uncertainty, inspection and repair, and ageing and life extension of offshore facilities and pipelines.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Guang Yin
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Guang Yin works on computational and data-driven modelling of marine and offshore hydrodynamics, using CFD (mainly OpenFOAM and SedFoam), lumped-mass models, surrogate models, neural networks and physics-informed neural networks. The publications cover aquaculture systems (dissolved oxygen in fish cages and vessel tanks), ship and trimaran resistance, subsea pipelines and cables (scour, vortex-induced vibration, wave-current boundary layers, snap loads) and mooring optimization for floating offshore wind turbines. The work is aimed at early-stage design and risk assessment for offshore aquaculture, shipping, subsea infrastructure and floating wind.

name: Guillem Rojas
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Guillem Rojas studies fibre-reinforced concrete, focusing on how cracks form and widen in members that combine steel bars and fibres, and on how fibre content and orientation affect strength. The work extends an analytical tension chord model to predict crack widths, crack spacing and tension stiffening, and compares it with experimental tie data and with the Eurocode 2 Annex L approach. It also tests characterisation methods such as the Montevideo splitting test against three-point bending, and uses CT scanning, inductive testing and digital image correlation to assess fibre distribution in large wall elements, with relevance to structural design and quality control.

name: Hadi Pezeshki
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Hadi Pezeshki studies the fatigue and structural dynamics of offshore wind turbines, combining analytical modelling with experimental work. His publications derive analytical solutions for natural frequencies and dynamic response of monopile turbines under nonlinear waves, including soil-structure and wave-structure interaction and gyroscopic effects of the spinning rotor. He also develops multiaxial fatigue life models for nonproportional loading, validated against experiments, and reviews and proposes model-based structural health monitoring frameworks for offshore and marine structures.

name: Hirpa Gelgele Lemu
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Hirpa Gelgele Lemu works on additive manufacturing and the mechanical behavior of engineering materials, including 3D and 4D printing of natural-fiber and cellulose-reinforced polymer composites, wire arc additive manufacturing of Inconel 718, and TPMS scaffolds for bone tissue engineering. The work combines experiments (tensile, compression, SEM, XRD, thermal analysis, rheology) with finite element, Monte Carlo and thermodynamic modeling. Application areas include sustainable composites, energy-absorbing structures, foams, aluminum nanocomposites, boiler tube stress analysis, orthopedic implants and photovoltaic module degradation.

name: Idriss El-Thalji
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Idriss El-Thalji studies maintenance engineering and asset management, with a focus on predictive and risk-based maintenance for wind turbines and offshore oil and gas assets. His work combines vibration-based machine learning and deep learning (fault detection, remaining useful life forecasting) with agent-based and other simulation models of system availability, spare parts and offshore logistics, alongside wind-tunnel tests of blade erosion. He also publishes on maintenance management practice under Industry 4.0 and the green transition, and on gamified active learning in engineering education.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Jakob Emanuel Beer
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jakob Emanuel Beer studies the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies in logistics, with a focus on warehousing. The publication provided uses a systematic literature review of 56 documents to build a conceptual framework linking the factors that influence adoption, the benefits companies can achieve and the barriers they face. The work takes the perspective of companies adopting the technologies and is relevant to both academics and logistics practitioners.

name: Jan Frick
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jan Frick studies logistics and supply chains, with a focus on resilience, customs compliance and digital document flow in international trade. His work combines literature reviews, conceptual design frameworks, scenario and sensitivity analysis, expert interviews and a warehouse case study, and it looks at how AI, blockchain, the European Product Passport and freight exchanges can support efficient, sustainable operations. Application areas include maritime and geopolitical disruption, 3PL warehousing, the energy sector, circular economy and regional industrial digital strategy.

name: Jan Magne Nygård
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jan Magne Nygård works on predicting oil recovery in layered, heterogeneous reservoirs under water, gas and water-alternating-gas injection. The work uses a large set of black oil reservoir simulations and physics-informed machine learning, in which least square support vector machine models are trained with optimizers such as particle swarm, genetic algorithm, grey wolf and gravitational search. It is applied to enhanced oil recovery, including how mobility ratios, gravity effects and hysteresis affect recovery.

name: Jan-Tore Jakobsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jan-Tore Jakobsen works on engineering education, with a focus on how digital manufacturing tools can be taught within product development and manufacturing courses. The single publication provided is a didactic guide for using such tools (ProDeM) in higher education, which points to an interest in teaching methods and curriculum support. The application domain is university-level engineering and manufacturing training.

name: Jarle Berge
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jarle Berge studies the structural behavior of aluminum columns, focusing on global buckling of extruded rectangular hollow profiles made from the 6082-T6 alloy. The work combines laboratory compression and cyclic loading tests, with digital image correlation to track deflection and strain, and compares the results with Eurocode 9 and Euler buckling calculations. It applies to structural design and code assessment for aluminum construction, including the safety margins in current design rules.

name: Jasna Bogunovic Jakobsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jasna Bogunovic Jakobsen works on wind engineering and the structural safety of long-span bridges, wind turbines and urban environments. Her publications combine wind tunnel tests, full-scale field measurements with sonic anemometers, pressure sensors and scanning lidars, and numerical modelling (finite element, large eddy simulation and stochastic wind simulation). Application areas include bridge aerodynamics and buffeting, fatigue of welded steel and aluminium bridge details, floating bridges and floating wind turbines, pedestrian wind comfort, and bridge response to scour and ship collisions.

name: Jawad Raza
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jawad Raza studies asset management in infrastructure-heavy industries, focusing on road tunnels and the Norwegian oil and gas sector. His work combines an industry survey of practitioners with a literature review to compare how asset management is applied in each sector and to clarify what counts as a best practice. The aim is to support the transfer of practices from oil and gas to road infrastructure, with attention to safety, maintenance costs and asset availability, and with a systems-theoretic approach proposed for the transfer process.

name: Jayantha Prasanna Liyanage
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jayantha Prasanna Liyanage studies how operators of complex, high-risk industrial systems can detect and make sense of process deviations and abnormalities early, in order to improve safety, reliability and resilience. The work combines conceptual development, critical literature review and industrial case observations to propose hybrid, context-aware decision-support approaches and an advanced form of situation awareness, with a focus on remote operations and digitalized assets. Related publications address maintenance and health management of rotating machinery fleets in oil refineries under Industry 4.0, and industrial agility as a strategic capability in engineering asset management.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Jianan Zhang
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jianan Zhang develops numerical models of floating docks used for vessel construction, maintenance and repair, combining six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body motion with hydrostatic, hydrodynamic, mooring, contact and ballast-piping hydraulic models. The work covers automatic ballast control with modified proportional controllers, stability and structural bending assessment, and analysis of failure scenarios such as valve or pump malfunctions and corrosion holes in ballast tanks, with validation against model-scale and full-scale measurements. Earlier work also applied nonlinear finite element simulation to ice floe sliding impact on ship hull structures.

name: Johan Andreas Håland Thorkaas
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Johan Andreas Håland Thorkaas is associated with a 2023 seminar on report writing and project work for bachelor-level engineering students. The single listed work points to an interest in engineering education, specifically helping students develop technical writing and project work skills. No research methods or application domains beyond this educational setting can be determined from the information given.

name: Jon Erik Karlsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jon Erik Karlsen studies how metal additive manufacturing and rapid casting can supply on-demand replacements for obsolete or undocumented components on ageing offshore installations on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. His work combines literature review, a roadmap and flow chart for the on-demand supply chain, and a multi-criteria decision analysis (Analytic Hierarchy Process) with industry expert input, applied to a valve body case from Statfjord-A. The outputs are intended for energy, oil and gas asset owners, suppliers and engineers.

name: Jonas Thor Snæbjörnsson
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jonas Thor Snæbjörnsson studies wind engineering and structural dynamics of long-span bridges, combining full-scale field monitoring with sonic anemometers, surface pressure sensors and Doppler lidars, plus wind tunnel tests, finite element models and numerical wind simulations. The work covers bridge aerodynamics and buffeting loads, wake and turbulence characterisation, system identification of bridge vibrations and damping, and vibration control under wind and seismic loads. Related work applies lidar and satellite wind measurements to offshore wind and urban flow, and addresses offshore floating energy platforms, FRP-concrete interface modelling and ground heat exchangers.

name: Kartika Nur Alfina
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Kartika Nur Alfina studies how circular economy principles can be adopted in healthcare supply chains, with attention to barriers, performance indicators, resilience and sustainability. Her work combines multi-criteria decision methods (analytic hierarchy process), risk tools (fuzzy logic, Bayesian networks, FMECA), systematic literature review and case studies of Indonesian primary care and medical device manufacturing, with a Norwegian benchmark. Application areas include medical product development under extended producer responsibility, critical supply shortages such as latex gloves, and cloud-based hand hygiene technology to reduce healthcare-associated infections.

name: Kenneth Alasdair Macdonald
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Kenneth Alasdair Macdonald's work on this publication concerns fracture control of offshore pipelines carrying liquefied CO2 for carbon capture and storage. It applies analytical methods for assessing running ductile fracture to the Northern Lights pipeline in the Longship project, checking whether the chosen wall thickness would arrest a propagating crack. The application area is safe pipeline design for CO2 transport and storage in the North Sea.

name: Kjell Tore Fosså
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Kjell Tore Fosså studies low-carbon cement-based materials, focusing on replacing large shares of cement with silicomanganese slag, Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and blast furnace slag. The work uses compressive strength tests, calorimetry, SEM and XRD, shrinkage measurements, and response surface modelling to link hydration, microstructure and mechanical performance in pastes, mortars and high-strength concrete. He has also carried out large-scale experiments and nonlinear finite element simulations of crack spacing in reinforced concrete members.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Knut Erik Teigen Giljarhus
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Knut Erik Teigen Giljarhus works on computational and experimental fluid dynamics, using CFD (including RANS, LES, OpenFOAM and lattice Boltzmann methods), wind tunnel and laboratory experiments, and machine learning surrogate models. His applications include urban pedestrian wind comfort, sports aerodynamics such as cycling, and non-Newtonian and multiphase flows in Hele-Shaw cells, annuli and thin films. He also applies deep learning and optimization to wind energy, covering turbine blade and bearing condition monitoring, leading-edge erosion, and floating offshore wind power cable design.

name: Lennart Vogt
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lennart Vogt studies how atmospheric stability shapes wind and turbulence in coastal and offshore settings, using synchronized scanning lidars, nacelle lidars, sonic and cup anemometers, and reanalysis data. His work compares analytical wind profile models with lidar observations and fits empirical turbulence spectra and coherence models as functions of stability. These results feed aeroelastic simulations of a 15-MW floating wind turbine, where he examines how shear, veer and low-level jets affect platform motion, loads and power.

name: Lichao Xiong
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lichao Xiong studies the hydrodynamic behaviour of offshore renewable energy structures, with a main focus on membrane-type floating photovoltaic platforms tested as 1:40 scale models and compared with numerical simulation. The work also covers coupled numerical modelling of floating offshore wind turbines, including a two-rotor turbine with wave energy converters and a simplified aerodynamic model, as well as laboratory and finite element tests of pile foundations for offshore wind. Applications include mooring design, sea-state response assessment, simulation efficiency and foundation capacity for offshore solar and wind systems.

name: Lin Li
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lin Li studies the dynamics, design and reliability of floating offshore structures, including floating wind turbines, offshore fish farm cages and multi-body marine systems. The work combines time-domain hydrodynamic and mooring simulation, Kriging surrogate models, sensitivity and reliability analysis, and faster ODE solving schemes with analysis of metocean and wind data (hindcast and lidar). Applications include shared mooring design, aquaculture-wind co-location, installation operations such as jacket lift-off, and site conditions for floating wind arrays.

name: Lorents Reinås
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lorents Reinås works on the safety and structural integrity of offshore drilling operations, covering subsea wellhead fatigue, drilling riser loads and dynamic positioning of mobile drilling units. His work combines global riser simulations, structural reliability analysis, incident data collection and statistical frequency estimation, and it includes the development and assessment of wellhead load relief equipment. It is applied to Norwegian Continental Shelf drilling, standards such as NORSOK U-001, and operating and disconnect criteria.

name: M. K. Samarakoon
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: M. K. Samarakoon studies low-carbon cementitious materials, focusing on mortars in which large shares of Portland cement are replaced by Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and silicon manganese slag, an industrial byproduct. The work uses compressive strength testing over 3 to 56 days, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction and isothermal calorimetry to assess strength, microstructure and heat development. The application area is sustainable construction, aiming to cut clinker use and CO2 emissions where fly ash is becoming less available.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Madushan Fernando
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: W. Madushan Fernando studies supply chains and logistics in developing economies, focusing on smallholder agri-food systems such as Sri Lankan tea, and on drone-based delivery and routing. The work uses multi-criteria decision methods (analytic hierarchy process, TOPSIS), causal loop and interpretive structural modelling, fuzzy inference, survey statistics and clustering, vehicle routing optimisation, systematic reviews and blockchain frameworks. Applications include farmer livelihoods, agricultural policy evaluation, digitalisation, sustainability standards, waste reduction, and UAV use in food delivery, medical supplies, flood relief and precision spraying.

name: Madushan Madhava Jayalath
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Madushan Madhava Jayalath studies agri-food and vegetable supply chains in developing economies, with a focus on Sri Lanka, covering waste, price volatility, risk, digital transformation and circular economy practices. The work uses fuzzy inference systems, analytical hierarchy process, interpretive structural modelling, social network analysis, process mapping, time series analysis and case studies to inform policy for food security and farmer livelihoods. He has also developed optimisation models for e-commerce reverse logistics and studied employee preferences for social sustainability in apparel supply chains using a discrete choice experiment.

name: Makafui Kwame Botsoe
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Makafui Kwame Botsoe studies reliability, availability and predictive maintenance of engineered assets. The publications compare deep learning and statistical time-series forecasting methods, including an LSTM autoencoder paired with Prophet, ARIMA and GRU, for predicting the remaining useful life of wind turbine bearings from vibration data. They also use agent-based simulation to compare availability estimates for subsea safety equipment at equipment and component levels.

name: Mats Ingdal
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Mats Ingdal's listed work is a seminar on report writing and project work for bachelor's engineering students, dated 2023. It points to an interest in engineering education, particularly teaching students how to write technical reports and carry out project-based assignments. Only one title is available, so the methods and wider application areas are not described.

name: Mesay Alemu Tolcha
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Mesay Alemu Tolcha works on manufacturing and materials engineering, covering additive manufacturing (FDM, SLA, direct-ink-writing and wire arc processes) with natural-fiber polymer composites, bioplastics and Inconel 718. He combines finite element simulation, analytical modeling, Monte Carlo and thermodynamic modeling, and optimization methods such as neural networks and response surface methodology with microscopy, diffraction and mechanical testing. Other work examines machining of aluminum composites, grain refinement of aluminum alloys, boiler tube and rolling die failure, and field degradation of silicon solar modules in Ethiopia.

name: Minh Jimmy Le
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Minh Jimmy Le studies the hydrodynamic resistance of trimaran vessels, focusing on how outrigger layout and forward speed affect the form factor used to estimate total resistance. The work combines OpenFOAM computational fluid dynamics simulations validated against experiments with potential flow theory for wave-making resistance, and more recently a neural network trained on the simulation results to predict the form factor. The applications are early-stage ship design and optimization of outrigger arrangements.

name: Mona Wetrhus Minde
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Mona Wetrhus Minde studies how materials and rocks change at the micro- and nanoscale, using electron, helium ion and X-ray based characterization. One strand examines the microstructure, crystallographic texture and mechanical behaviour of super duplex stainless steel made by directed laser deposition. A second strand uses flooding experiments and high-resolution imaging to study mineral dissolution, precipitation and fracture changes in North Sea chalk for improved oil recovery, along with analysis of aged well cement for well integrity.

name: Morten Andre Langøy
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Morten Andre Langøy studies safety and risk regulation in the offshore petroleum industry, with a focus on the Norwegian continental shelf. His work combines analysis of incident and experience data from regulator databases, including knowledge graphs and large language models for text-based incident analysis, with conceptual models and case studies of regulatory regimes. Application areas include structural and maritime safety of offshore units, risk governance and supervision, and regulation of emerging resource-based industries such as wind farms and fish farming.

name: Mudiyan Nirosha Damayanthi Adasooriya
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Mudiyan Nirosha Damayanthi Adasooriya studies the structural integrity and service life of steel infrastructure, focusing on corrosion, hydrogen embrittlement, environment-assisted cracking and fatigue in gas and hydrogen pipelines, offshore wind turbine structures and road bridges. The work combines laboratory mechanical testing (slow strain rate tensile, Charpy impact, hardness, fractography), statistical analysis of incident data, and conceptual and fatigue-life assessment frameworks. A second strand examines construction practice, including reuse of prefabricated hollow-core slabs and comparison of cast-in-place, precast and modular building methods in Norway.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Muk Chen Ong
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Muk Chen Ong's publications cover marine and offshore engineering, including floating offshore wind turbines, mooring and power cable dynamics, ship hydrodynamics and stability, and offshore and shipboard aquaculture. Methods include computational fluid dynamics (OpenFOAM, FLOW-3D), lumped-mass and quasi-static models, neural network and physics-informed machine learning, and optimization and structural health monitoring techniques. Application areas include ocean current and hydrokinetic energy, fish cage design and oxygen management, trimaran and suspension ship design, floating docks, and subsea cable and pipeline loading.

name: Navid Sayyar
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Navid Sayyar studies laser-based directed energy deposition of super duplex stainless steel, examining how pulsed versus continuous laser input and process parameters shape grain structure, phase balance, crystallographic texture, mechanical properties and corrosion behaviour. The work combines electron microscopy, EBSD, tensile and toughness testing, electrochemical tests and Taguchi-grey relational optimization, and also covers cold rolling of Inconel 718 and thermal management of thermoelectric modules using phase change material and metal foam.

name: Noorhan Firdaus Pambudi
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Noorhan Firdaus Pambudi studies circular economy business models and plastic and household waste management in Indonesia, using surveys, interviews, scenario planning, risk analysis (FMEA, DEMATEL), and system dynamics to examine public participation, risks, and policy factors. The work also covers urban mobility and logistics in Greater Jakarta, including ride-hailing in multimodal commuting, truck sharing, maritime port performance, and ambulance response times, using scenario planning, systems thinking, and agent-based simulation. Findings are framed for policymakers, businesses, and service operators.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Nursultan Jyeniskhan
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Nursultan Jyeniskhan works on digital twins and cyber-physical systems for additive manufacturing, with a focus on fused deposition modeling 3D printers. The publication builds a digital twin that combines convolutional neural network anomaly detection with model predictive control of material feed, and proposes real-time frameworks to guard against cyber-attacks. The work applies to smart manufacturing plants that need safer and more reliable process control.

name: Ove Kjetil Mikkelsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Ove Kjetil Mikkelsen works on fatigue of tubular joints in offshore energy structures, combining laboratory fatigue testing with finite element analysis and structural reliability methods. His work includes testing a cracked joint repaired by drilling crack-deflecting holes and grinding the weld toe, and statistical approaches for deriving characteristic stress concentration factors from test data and numerical models.

name: Ove Tobias Gudmestad
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Ove Tobias Gudmestad's publications address the design, safety and risk management of offshore and cold-climate infrastructure and operations. Using literature reviews, case studies, metocean statistics from hindcast data, risk analysis methods such as FMEA and STPA, and simple structural dynamics, he covers subsea cables and pipelines, offshore wind support structures and power cables, platform decommissioning and reuse, Arctic and polar-low marine operations, and design under climate change. He also studies maritime education and simulator-based training, ship accident lessons, and the link between winter road conditions and traffic accidents.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Pasindu Erange Yaddehi Guruge
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Pasindu Erange Yaddehi Guruge studies hydrogen-assisted cracking and environment-assisted cracking in API 5L X52 pipeline steel, with a view to repurposing natural gas pipelines for hydrogen transport. The work combines electrochemical hydrogen charging with slow strain rate tensile, Charpy impact and hardness testing, plus fractography and microstructural analysis to see how charging time and cathodic potential affect ductility and fracture behaviour. It also includes a review and a proposed conceptual framework and test procedure for assessing the structural integrity of pipelines in hydrogen service.

name: Peiqing Zhao
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Peiqing Zhao studies unsteady flow around a circular cylinder placed near a plane wall, using separable physics-informed neural networks that build the governing flow equations into training. The work reconstructs vortex shedding and wake structures at a Reynolds number of 200 for three gap ratios and checks the results against computational fluid dynamics simulations. It also examines how spatial and temporal sampling density affect reconstruction accuracy and computational cost, with relevance to fluid-structure interaction problems.

name: R.M. Chandima Ratnayake
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: R.M. Chandima Ratnayake's research covers risk, resilience and sustainability in supply chains and engineered assets. One strand examines smallholder agri-food and healthcare supply chains using fuzzy inference systems, analytic hierarchy process, causal loop diagrams, Bayesian networks, time series analysis and case studies, with applications to policy evaluation, price volatility, digital product passports and circular economy transitions. A second strand covers structural integrity and asset management, including fatigue testing and finite element modelling of closely spaced S355 girth welds, digital twins for technical safety, dynamic risk assessment for power distribution assets, and digital value stream mapping in engineering-to-order projects.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Sakura Attanayake
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Sakura Attanayake researches asset integrity management for electric power distribution systems, focusing on risk and reliability assessment of assets such as distribution transformers, fuses and overhead cables. The work combines Weibull analysis, time series forecasting, supervised machine learning, fuzzy inference systems and analytic hierarchy process prioritization, usually implemented in Python and tied to standards such as NORSOK Z-008, ISO 9001 and IEC. Applications are maintenance planning, inspection prioritization, resilience and circular economy practices for utilities, with case studies drawn largely from the Ceylon Electricity Board in Sri Lanka.

name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon studies sustainability in construction materials and in industrial and business systems. Experimental work covers low-carbon cement binders and mortars made with silicomanganese slag, Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and slag cement, using strength, shrinkage, calorimetry and microstructural tests, response surface modelling, and graphene oxide–treated textile waste fibres in mortar. Further studies use case studies, surveys, interviews and decision-analysis methods on circular economy and plastic waste management in Indonesia, circular fashion design in Sri Lankan apparel firms, digital value stream mapping and balanced scorecards in engineering-to-order firms, and life cycle costing of building façades. One study tests an interactive sensory ball for children with autism.

name: Samdar Kakay
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Samdar Kakay studies the lateral-torsional buckling of steel I-beams using laboratory three-point bending tests on several cross sections and beam lengths. The work measures load and lateral displacement of the compression flange to derive buckling moment capacities and elastic critical moments, then checks them against Eurocode 3 design methods. The research applies to structural steel design and verification of beam stability.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Shangming Wang
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Shangming Wang works on marine and ocean hydrodynamics, covering ship resistance, seakeeping and hull form optimization, with a strong focus on trimarans, and on wave interaction with floating breakwaters and wave energy converters. The work combines CFD with OpenFOAM and RANS, potential flow methods, semi-analytical models, neural networks, evolutionary optimization algorithms, and wave flume and towing model tests. Applications include early-stage vessel design, outrigger layout control, ship motion and resistance prediction in waves, coastal wave attenuation and offshore structure response.

name: Soheil Salahshour Langeroodi
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Soheil Salahshour Langeroodi studies the decommissioning of offshore wind turbine foundations, focusing on removing monopiles with vibratory hammers or hydraulic pressure. The work uses finite element modelling (Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian analysis in ABAQUS) for soil resistance in sand and clay, and time-domain simulations of crane barge motion, lifting wire tension and operability using extreme value analysis. Earlier work includes a review of decommissioning methods and combined experimental and finite element stress analysis of an expanding pin joint.

name: Sudath C. Siriwardane
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Sudath C. Siriwardane's research centres on the fatigue, durability and structural integrity of steel, aluminium, concrete and timber structures. The publications cover multiaxial and variable-amplitude fatigue models, orthotropic bridge decks, wind turbines, flare booms, pipelines, corroded reinforced concrete, buckling of beams and timber-concrete slabs, using analytical derivation, finite element and numerical simulation, statistical analysis and laboratory testing. Application areas include bridges, offshore and onshore wind energy, oil and gas infrastructure and nature-based coastal protection structures.

name: Swen Roemer
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Swen Roemer studies wind conditions and wind effects on structures using field measurements, including remote sensing with nacelle-mounted continuous-wave lidars, vertical wind profilers and sonic anemometers. The work compares lidar-reconstructed wind speeds and turbulence statistics with sonic anemometer data, fits wind profile laws to estimate shear and surface roughness in an urban campus setting, and examines full-scale surface pressures on a bridge deck. The results are relevant to wind monitoring in built environments, validation of numerical flow models and wind engineering of civil structures.

name: Tor Henning Hemmingsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Tor Henning Hemmingsen studies corrosion and structural integrity in energy infrastructure, including experiments on how weak acids drive carbon steel corrosion in petroleum pipelines and a framework with fatigue curves for corrosion damage in offshore wind turbine structures. The work also covers computational modelling of the depth control of a subsea shuttle tanker designed to carry liquid CO2. Methods combine laboratory electrochemical testing, mechanism-based damage assessment and dynamic simulation.

name: Torfinn Havn
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Udo Zimmermann
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Udo Zimmermann studies the mineralogy, geochemistry and rock mechanics of sedimentary rocks, using electron and helium ion microscopy, X-ray diffraction, detrital zircon dating and laboratory deformation and flow tests. His work covers subsurface energy applications, including hydrogen storage in Zechstein salt caverns, chalk reservoir response to water injection for improved oil recovery, and tight gas and CO2 storage in South African gas fields. He also reconstructs sediment provenance and tectonic history in Paleozoic basins of the central Andes.

name: Usman Shaukat
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Usman Shaukat studies urban wind environments using computational fluid dynamics, mainly large eddy simulation compared against RANS and partially-averaged Navier-Stokes models and validated with wind tunnel data. The work covers turbulent inflow generation, new validation metrics, statistical models for gusts and low-occurring wind speeds, and pedestrian wind comfort assessment with Lawson criteria. The same simulation approaches are also applied to flow around step cylinders for subsea power cables on floating offshore wind systems and to a simplified athlete geometry.

name: Vidar Folke Hansen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Vidar Folke Hansen studies how processing shapes the microstructure and properties of metals and functional thin films. His work covers laser-based additive manufacturing (directed energy deposition and powder bed fusion) of duplex stainless steel, tool steel, Inconel 718 and 316L, using parameter optimization, heat treatment, mechanical testing and electron microscopy with texture analysis. He also characterizes thermochromic VO2 thin films for smart windows and a few other materials, such as corroding magnesium and thermoelectric Mg2Si-based compounds, using electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction.

name: Wakshum Mekonnen Tucho
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Wakshum Mekonnen Tucho's publications centre on metal additive manufacturing, including laser directed energy deposition, laser powder bed fusion and wire arc processes applied to super duplex stainless steel, Inconel 625 and 718, and AlSi10Mg. The work links process parameters, heat treatment and cold rolling to microstructure, porosity, hardness and tensile and impact behaviour, using microscopy, diffraction, Taguchi/grey relational optimization and machine learning prediction for polymer 3D printing. A second strand covers materials for CO2 conversion and capture, such as MOF-supported Cu/ZnO methanol catalysts, sulfonic acid Zr-MOFs and dual-atom electrocatalysts, along with magnesium corrosion, mechanochemical synthesis and cellulose nanocrystals.

name: Waqar Ali
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Waqar Ali studies condition monitoring and predictive maintenance of wind turbines, focusing on blade faults such as cracks and leading-edge erosion and on bearing degradation. His work combines vibration signal analysis, machine learning and deep learning (autoencoders, anomaly detectors, LSTM/GRU and other forecasting models) for fault detection, classification and remaining useful life prediction. He also uses wind-tunnel experiments, blade element momentum modelling and SCADA data to link erosion to power loss and maintenance planning, and proposes risk-based evaluation frameworks.

name: Xueliang Wen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Xueliang Wen's research applies numerical modelling, computational fluid dynamics and surrogate-based optimization to offshore marine structures, especially offshore fish cages. The work covers dissolved oxygen and fish welfare in cage design, net and tendon failure and monitoring, and mooring design for floating wind turbines and floating solar. It also covers suspension ship stability, floating dock operations, and scour and vortex-induced vibration of subsea pipelines.

name: Yanyan Sha
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yanyan Sha studies how marine and civil structures respond to extreme loads, including ship and barge collisions with bridges, floating bridges and floating wind turbine columns, dropped objects on subsea rock berms, and wind-induced bridge motion. Her work uses nonlinear finite element simulation (LS-DYNA, OrcaFlex), particle-based modelling, coupled hydrodynamic-structural analysis, and AIS-based probability and risk methods, with case studies on Norwegian fjord bridges. She also carries out experimental, theoretical and numerical studies of rock fracturing in tunnel contour blasting under in-situ stress, using granite and sandstone model tests with digital image correlation.

name: Yihan Xing
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yihan Xing studies the dynamics, loads and reliability of offshore and marine structures, including floating wind turbines and farms, wave energy converters, mooring systems, risers and autonomous vessels. The work combines numerical simulation (e.g. ANSYS-AQWA, OpenFAST, dynamic wake meandering) with machine learning, such as active learning Kriging, TimesNet-based time-series prediction and CNN fault detection, to speed up fatigue assessment and forecast motions and mooring tensions. Applications include wind farm yaw and wake steering control, mooring risk and failure analysis, thruster fault detection for underwater vehicles, vibration damping with tuned liquid dampers, and inland ship manoeuvring.

name: Yingjie Gu
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yingjie Gu studies floating and bottom-fixed offshore wind turbines in cold regions, with a focus on ice loads, extreme wind and ice conditions, and mooring system response. The work couples a semi-empirical ice load model with the SIMA time-domain simulation tool, using parametric and ultimate limit state analyses, platform comparisons and an LSTM machine-learning model for response prediction. Reviews of icing models, ice detection and mitigation, and Arctic deployment feasibility complement the simulation studies, with case studies in the Baltic Sea and Gotland Basin.

name: Yosef Wakjira Adugna
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yosef Wakjira Adugna works on additive manufacturing for biomedical and engineering uses, especially stereolithography and fused deposition printing of triply periodic minimal surface bone scaffolds, patient-specific anatomical models and composite materials. His methods include mechanical testing, cell viability assays, electron microscopy, reverse engineering from CT and 3D scanning, finite element and meshless stress analysis, and statistical and machine learning optimization of process parameters. He also studies wire arc additive manufacturing residual stresses, 3D printed fiber composites, and machining optimization of aluminum composites.

name: Yu Ma
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yu Ma works on numerical modeling and simulation of floating marine structures, with a focus on offshore fish cages, shared mooring systems and fish cages combined with floating wind turbines. The publications use time-domain simulation, catenary mooring analysis, Kriging surrogate models, Sobol global sensitivity analysis and adaptive-time-step ODE solvers with a relaxation scheme for convolution forces. The work targets more efficient design and analysis of aquaculture arrays and offshore wind co-location, including digital-twin simulation.

name: Zihao Wang
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Zihao Wang studies how bridges and offshore structures respond to extreme and accidental loads, including ship and barge collisions, local scour, wind, waves and dropped objects. The work uses finite element modelling in LS-DYNA and OrcaFlex, coupled simulation algorithms for hydrodynamic and structural effects, and smoothed particle hydrodynamics for rock berm impact. Application areas include fixed-foundation concrete bridges, curved floating bridges such as fjord crossings, and subsea pipeline protection in offshore oil and gas operations.

name: Albert Lunde
summary: Albert Lunde works on climate risk and safety in mountain tourism, with a focus on the Jotunheimen area of Norway. The publications combine documentation of permafrost thaw, glacier change and rockfall and landslide hazards with interviews of mountain lodge hosts, guides, activity companies and nature managers, and a systems-theory study of safety governance. The work also covers future scenarios for mountain rescue services, a seminar report on Norwegian avalanche rescue operations, and public-facing communication about growing mountain hazards.

name: Alexander Kuran
summary: Alexander Kuran studies how the education of customs officers in Norway has changed with the move from in-house training to an academic bachelor's degree in customs and border control. His work looks at organizational change, workplace culture, recruitment and the passing of tacit knowledge from experienced staff to new graduates. He uses an exploratory qualitative approach based on conversations with students, field observation and interviews with customs officials, and proposes a follow-up research agenda.

name: Alexander Trengereid
summary: Alexander Trengereid studies public sector crisis management and governance, using the COVID-19 pandemic as the main case. His work examines Norwegian government decision-making, leadership, crisis communication, learning, and the balance between governance capacity and legitimacy, and also compares Nordic countries through case studies on how administrative size and informal elite networks shape knowledge sharing and policy responses.

name: Ana Llopis Alvarez
summary: Ana Llopis Alvarez studies how housing, neighbourhood conditions and digital tools shape everyday life in Norwegian and wider European urban settings. Her work combines questionnaire surveys, interviews, map-based subjective data, and geographic and statistical analysis to compare local and immigrant residents' quality of life and to examine household use of smart energy apps.
