The findings are aimed at residential planning, housing design, app development and policy for sustainable household energy practices.

name: Anders Riel Müller
summary: Anders Riel Müller studies sustainable urban development, with a focus on participatory and inclusive planning, smart city narratives, and how imagined futures and energy transitions are shaped in Norwegian cities such as Stavanger. His work combines case studies, participatory workshops, topic modelling of social media data, building energy data comparisons and critical analysis of frontier and petroleum imaginaries. It addresses urban living labs, cross-case learning, positive energy districts, and the governance of building energy performance and data infrastructures.

name: Andreea-Laura Cojocaru
summary: Andreea-Laura Cojocaru is an economist who studies seafood and coastal systems, including fisheries management, salmon aquaculture regulation and the economics of coastal communities. Her methods include difference-in-differences analysis, discrete choice modelling, fine-scale industry data analysis and policy design, along with survey and vignette experiments on stated preferences and willingness to pay. Application areas include Norwegian fisheries and salmon farming, global fisheries performance, aquatic food security, and public support for nature-based solutions and coastal flood adaptation in Europe.

name: Ari Krisna Mawira Tarigan
summary: Ari Krisna Mawira Tarigan studies urban sustainability, covering nature-based solutions and green infrastructure, sustainable transport, household energy use and pro-environmental behaviour. The publications use surveys, structural equation and nested logit modelling, spatial indicator assessment, systematic review, interviews, and text mining of social media posts and app reviews. Application areas include cities in Norway, Indonesia, Poland and South Africa, with topics such as green spaces for children's learning, smart energy apps, parking policy, circular economy readiness and energy security governance.

name: Atle Øglend
summary: Atle Øglend studies the economics of seafood and commodity markets, with a focus on Norwegian salmon aquaculture, international trade and regulation. His work applies firm-level customs and transaction data, cointegration analysis, instrumental-variable estimation, quasi-natural experiments and structural or search models to topics such as export supply chains, intermediaries, trade shocks, import price competition, disease management and licence quotas. Application areas include seafood exports, farm-level production and sea lice control, regional policy for aquaculture, and oil price volatility.

name: Ayda Joudavi
summary: Ayda Joudavi studies how cities and companies can encourage sustainable behaviour, with a focus on commute cycling and travel behaviour change in Stavanger, Norway, and on pro-environmental actions by urban residents. Her work uses literature reviews, policy document analysis, stakeholder engagement, case studies and mixed-method indices, including a reward-valuation framework applied in Gdańsk and a circularity readiness index for Norwegian companies. Application areas include sustainable urban mobility, ICT-based smart solutions, incentive and reward schemes such as Greencoin, and corporate transitions to a circular economy.

name: Bjørn Ivar Kruke
summary: Bjørn Ivar Kruke studies risk governance, emergency preparedness and decision-making, mainly through interviews and document analysis. His work covers police armed confrontations and situational awareness, climate risk and adaptation in Arctic communities such as Longyearbyen, and evacuation and flood risk. He also addresses risk communication and trust, school preparedness, Arctic maritime search and rescue, ship noise governance and the definition of good practice in disaster risk management.

name: Brynhild Stavland
summary: Brynhild Stavland studies the safety regulation and societal acceptance of hydrogen and ammonia as energy carriers. Her work applies systems theory (including the STAMP model), regulatory theory and knowledge-quality frameworks to regulatory challenges, and uses document analysis, interviews and literature review to examine local resistance to an ammonia plant in Norway and how policy communication shapes industry hydrogen investment decisions.

name: Chinwe Philomina Oramah
summary: Chinwe Philomina Oramah studies climate change communication, climate security and adaptation, with a focus on Nigeria, using surveys, semi-structured interviews, document analysis and observation, and drawing on risk communication and securitization theories. Related work covers how language, framing and local knowledge shape community understanding and adaptation action. Further publications apply economic evaluation (social return on investment) to environmental protection plans in quarrying and multilevel regression to malaria net use among children in West Africa.

name: Christian Henrik Alexander Skadsheim Kuran
summary: Christian Henrik Alexander Skadsheim Kuran studies safety, risk and rule bending in Norwegian road-based heavy goods transport, using ethnographic fieldwork, systems theory, scoping and document analysis, and reviews of accident investigations, and he proposes the concept of adaptive non-conforming behaviour. He also works on crisis and disaster research, including resilience, vulnerability and social capital, and on risk analysis for dangerous goods transport in tunnels. In addition, he examines education and learning from practice in the Norwegian customs and border management bachelor programme through diary analysis, interviews and observation.

name: Claudia Morsut
summary: Claudia Morsut studies how climate change adaptation is governed, with a focus on risk management and securitisation approaches in international organisations, national governments and cities. Her work uses document analysis, interviews and comparative case studies of the UN, the EU, Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands and several European municipalities, and draws on Security Studies and Risk Governance. She also examines flood risk, disaster risk management good practice and vulnerability during the COVID-19 pandemic in the Nordic countries.

name: Cristian Tosa
summary: Cristian Tosa studies sustainability, spatial planning and technology adoption, with a focus on Romania, Norway and Poland. His work combines text mining of social media posts and app reviews, questionnaire surveys, stated-preference experiments and systematic reviews to examine household energy apps, residential and mobility choices, road infrastructure, circular economy practices and nature-based stormwater solutions. The findings are aimed at informing policy and planning for urban and rural regions.

name: Daniela Müller-Eie
summary: Daniela Müller-Eie studies sustainable urban mobility and planning, with a focus on combining bicycles and public transport, transport equity and job accessibility, and travel behaviour in Norwegian regions. Her work uses survey data with structural equation modelling, spatial accessibility and equity analysis, systematic literature review and policy document analysis. She also examines smart sustainable city development in Stavanger and other Nordic cities, and links housing and neighbourhood conditions to quality of life for local and immigrant residents.

name: David Chapman
summary: David Chapman studies walking as a mode of transport and how it fits into urban planning, including the 15-minute city concept, with a particular focus on small and Arctic communities. His work uses focus groups, surveys, questionnaires of older residents and literature reviews to examine how planning and safety fields treat walking, and what daily destinations matter for healthy ageing. He also contributes to work on urban design and planning for cities in the European Arctic and other northern regions.

name: Dikshya Bhandari
summary: Dikshya Bhandari studies risk and reliability of hydrogen systems, with a focus on how safety is regulated and analysed as hydrogen technology scales up. Her work includes qualitative comparison of risk assessment frameworks used by Norwegian regulators, evaluation of dynamic and multistate fault tree methods on hydrogen storage explosion cases, and treatment of uncertainty and the precautionary principle. She has also applied fault tree analysis and Monte Carlo simulation to estimate unavailability of an offshore energy island in the North Sea.

name: Eirik Bjorheim Abrahamsen
summary: Eirik Bjorheim Abrahamsen works on risk science and safety, including operational risk assessment models built on evidence reasoning, multi-criteria decision analysis and time series forecasting, and on systems thinking for risks such as explosive remnants of war and hydrogen systems. He also studies helicopter rescue operations using workload measurement, physiological monitoring and safe job analysis. A further body of work looks at higher education, covering learning from practice, learning management system implementation, exam appeals, assessment forms, feedback and teaching quality, using diary analysis, course evaluation data and platform usage data.

name: Eivind Lorentzen-Styr
summary: Eivind Lorentzen-Styr works on risk assessment, with a focus on how uncertainty and the knowledge underlying probability and risk judgments are characterised and communicated. His publications develop conceptual frameworks, including a proposed "strength of justification" concept, and use interviews with risk practitioners in Norway to study how existing schemes work in practice. He also examines how industry standards such as NORSOK Z-013 relate to current risk science, and has written on risk management in higher education.

name: Emmanuel Aduse Poku
summary: Emmanuel Aduse Poku works on mapping and classifying peatlands from satellite data, combining spectral reflectance with topographic and climate variables. He applies a random forest machine learning classifier to estimate peatland condition across Scotland at 100 m resolution, supporting national-scale status monitoring. His work also addresses the link between peatlands, greenhouse gas emissions and carbon storage.

name: Fabio Alberto Hernandez Palacio
summary: Fabio Alberto Hernandez Palacio studies how urban form, density and proximity shape sustainability and access to everyday services, using GIS network analysis, isochrones, statistical comparison and field observation, mainly in Norwegian cities such as Stavanger and Tromsø. His work covers walking and cycling access to groceries, kindergartens and open spaces, energy efficiency and solar access in Arctic urban patterns, and comparative bicycle policy analysis. He also contributes conceptual and survey-based work on proximity-centred accessibility and on cross-case learning through living labs and urban experimentation spaces.

name: Farnaz Eskandari
summary: Farnaz Eskandari studies how the built environment shapes health, safety and walkability in cities, using both qualitative and quantitative methods. Her work combines content analysis, factor analysis and importance–performance mapping for neighborhood health assessment, machine learning with remote sensing data for climate-related traffic risk, and Space Syntax modeling of historic street networks. Case studies cover Parand New Town and Urmia's old Bazaar in Iran, and Austin, Texas.

name: Frank Asche
summary: Frank Asche studies the economics of seafood systems, covering fisheries, aquaculture, trade, markets and supply chains across countries including Norway, Indonesia, India and the US. His work applies econometric methods such as cointegration analysis, synthetic control, firm-level trade data and stochastic bioeconomic simulation to questions of prices, ecolabels, fishing quotas, industry clustering, disease and production risk. It also reviews governance and scale in the seafood sector and examines data quality and corporate climate and energy behavior.

name: Frederic Emmanuel Bouder
summary: Frederic Emmanuel Bouder studies risk communication, risk perception and the handling of scientific uncertainty, with a focus on how public authorities and regulators communicate with citizens. Methods include surveys analysed with structural equation modelling, interviews, ethnographic fieldwork, case studies and systematic literature review. Application areas include COVID-19 policy, the Dutch energy transition, wind power, food safety regulation, and the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare and construction.

name: Frida Layti
summary: Frida Layti studies sustainability reporting and climate accounting in corporate value chains, with a focus on how small and medium-sized enterprises in the energy sector respond to customer and regulatory demands such as the CSRD. Her work combines surveys of hundreds of suppliers, interviews, a digital reporting platform with third-party verification, and dynamic capability theory to examine reporting coverage, emissions data quality and organizational capability development. She also examines the environmental impact of universities in relation to regional green transitions.

name: Geir Petter Novik
summary: Geir Petter Novik studies safety and risk management for explosive remnants of war, unexploded ordnance and dumped munitions, including leaking wartime shipwrecks. His work combines qualitative case studies, systems thinking and critiques of risk assessment methods with laboratory analysis of ageing explosives (impact and friction sensitivity, thermal and spectroscopic analysis) and statistical methods such as maximum likelihood estimation and confidence intervals for sensitivity testing. The applications are societal safety, defence-sector decision making, environmental protection and the safe handling of energetic materials.

name: Guicang Peng
summary: Guicang Peng studies operational risk assessment and management in complex, interconnected and fast-changing settings where several objectives must be balanced at once. The work combines multi-criteria decision analysis, evidence reasoning and time series forecasting with real-time data, alongside literature reviews, industry surveys and a field case study. Applications include country risk mapping across 161 countries and well control and barrier management in onshore oil drilling in Iraq.

name: Guizhou Wang
summary: Guizhou Wang studies cryptocurrencies, monetary systems and sustainable finance, using game-theoretic models, regression and stochastic simulation, network-based volatility analysis, and bibliometric reviews. The publications examine competition between hard money, fiat currencies and CBDCs, factors behind interest rates, and the integration of Bitcoin mining with biorefineries. Other work covers ESG stock volatility spillovers in China, business model innovation and firm performance, and the development of green finance and quantitative finance research.

name: Harald Nils Røstvik
summary: Harald Nils Røstvik studies energy use in buildings, with a focus on how well calculated energy performance matches metered consumption in Norwegian non-residential buildings. His work compares certificate calculations with sub-metered end-use data and examines how researchers can get access to consumer energy data from utilities. He also writes shorter pieces in Norwegian and English on solar energy in building facades, ventilation, climate emissions, climate adaptation in planning, and positive energy districts.

name: Hassan Gholami
summary: Hassan Gholami studies solar photovoltaic deployment in cities and national power systems, with a focus on building-integrated and urban-integrated PV in Norway and across Europe. His methods include PVsyst and Rhinoceros/Grasshopper simulation, GIS-based solar mapping, hourly matching of PV output with electricity demand, and multi-criteria assessment frameworks. He has also worked on robust optimization for planning hybrid AC/DC microgrids with energy storage and converter aging.

name: Heidi Helledal Griegel
summary: Heidi Helledal Griegel studies workplace safety in large, inter-organisational construction projects, particularly in the energy sector, treating these projects as temporary organisations. Using qualitative methods such as fieldwork, interviews, workshops, document analysis and literature review, she examines how safety is practised, how teams learn across organisational boundaries, and how subcontracting shapes control and compliance. Her work also looks at job safety analysis as a tool for decentralised risk handling and at what safety theory and practice need to change for project-based work.

name: Henrik Kvadsheim
summary: Henrik Kvadsheim writes opinion and commentary pieces on social and security issues in Norway, in Norwegian. His topics include youth mental health and smartphone use, honour-based violence and crime, immigrant integration, ethnic diversity and social cohesion, clan-related crime, and campus free speech. He also covers Norway's position in relation to EU investment screening, security policy and critical infrastructure, drawing on public debate, reported evidence and social-science arguments rather than original empirical studies.

name: Håkon Bjorheim Abrahamsen
summary: Håkon Bjorheim Abrahamsen studies teaching quality and student learning in higher education, drawing on large-scale student course evaluations and survey data from the University of Stavanger, including how teaching held up during COVID-19. He also works on risk science, covering the teaching of safety risk management and the use of Safe Job Analysis and retrospective mission data to examine hazards and safety measures in Norwegian helicopter emergency medical service rope rescue operations.

name: Ingrid Glette-Iversen
summary: Ingrid Glette-Iversen works in risk science, studying how risk, uncertainty and knowledge are defined, assessed, characterized and communicated under an uncertainty-based perspective. Her conceptual and review-based work covers terms such as plausibility, unpredictable events and "real risk", and proposes improvements to risk management and decision-making frameworks. She applies these ideas to hydrogen energy safety and Norwegian regulation, as well as to COVID-19, vaccines and climate change.

name: Ioannis Kosmidis
summary: Ioannis Kosmidis studies how bicycles can be combined with public transport and how this supports sustainable commuting in mid-sized, car-oriented urban regions, mainly Nord-Jæren in Norway and also Athens. His work draws on surveys and stated and revealed preference data analysed with structural equation modelling, latent class analysis, choice analysis and ordinal regression, alongside spatial accessibility and equity measures, a systematic literature review and policy document analysis. Application areas include perceived transfer inconvenience, job accessibility and transport equity, the effect of electric cars on travel behaviour, road space allocation and smart mobility strategies in Nordic cities.

name: Jacob Taarup-Esbensen
summary: Jacob Taarup-Esbensen studies risk analysis, risk governance and organisational resilience, with a particular focus on Arctic settings such as Svalbard and Greenland. His work uses conceptual models based on sensemaking and systems theory, bow-tie analysis, interviews, document review and case studies to examine expert and local knowledge, business continuity, supply chain reliability and community resilience. Application areas include national risk registers, mining, Arctic shipping, snow avalanche and tsunami hazards, and climate adaptation in remote communities.

name: Jason Deegan
summary: Jason Deegan studies regional economic development and industrial transformation, with a focus on how regions and firms diversify into new activities, including the shift of Norway's oil and gas sector toward renewables such as offshore wind and aquaculture. His work combines interviews, policy document analysis, text mining and linked employer-employee data to examine knowledge transfer, occupational and industrial relatedness, and the role of policy. He also analyses Smart Specialisation strategies and regional policy in Europe, Norway and Poland, including how regions select priority domains and interpret entrepreneurial discovery processes.

name: Jon Tømmerås Selvik
summary: Jon Tømmerås Selvik studies risk, reliability and decision-making, with a strong focus on hydrogen energy systems and offshore oil, gas and lower-carbon technology. His work uses fault tree analysis, failure mode and effects analysis, probabilistic cause-and-effect graphs, evidence reasoning, multi-criteria decision analysis and time series forecasting, and also includes qualitative comparison of regulatory frameworks, standards such as ISO 20815, and analysis of policy communication and investment decisions. He additionally writes on higher education assessment and exam appeal procedures in Norway, and on triage methods for trauma-related conditions after mass violence.

name: Kaia Stødle
summary: Kaia Stødle studies risk analysis with a focus on how artificial intelligence and data-driven predictive modeling can be used and interpreted in risk assessments. Her work combines conceptual analysis of risk description, uncertainty and knowledge with case studies using spatial statistics (local Moran's I), machine learning and infrastructure modeling for power and water systems. Application areas include power outage and pipe break hotspot identification, vulnerability analysis of dependent infrastructures with limited data, and the limits of automating risk-informed decision-making.

name: Kenneth Arne Pettersen Gould
summary: Kenneth Arne Pettersen Gould studies how risks are perceived, communicated, amplified and attenuated in society, and how organisations manage safety and reliability. His work uses qualitative case studies, literature reviews, theory development and long-run survey trend analysis, with examples from construction projects, publicly procured air ambulance services, critical infrastructure in smart cities and public trust in government. He also writes on technological accidents, climate adaptation policy in Nigeria, and the role of universities in societal preparedness.

name: Kjartan Bjørnsen
summary: Kjartan Bjørnsen works in risk science, focusing on how uncertainty and knowledge strength are treated in risk assessment and how well current standards and regulations reflect contemporary risk concepts. His publications combine interviews with risk practitioners in Norway, conceptual analysis of regulations, guidelines and standards, and methodological work on classifying research methods. Application areas include environmental impact assessment, public and private sector risk management, and industry standards such as NORSOK Z-013.

name: Kjell Hausken
summary: Kjell Hausken studies strategic conflict and decision-making using game theory, differential and stochastic models, and simulation. His work covers counterterrorism, economic sanctions, military force modeling in the Lanchester tradition, infrastructure security and reliability, and the competition among cryptocurrencies, fiat and hard money. He also carries out bibliometric reviews of fields such as Bitcoin and green finance, and reviews game theory applied to pandemics, disasters and social media rumors.

name: Knut Erik Bang
summary: Knut Erik Bang studies operational risk management, covering well control in onshore drilling, country-level risk mapping, and adaptive risk assessment. The work combines case study analysis, literature reviews, industry surveys, and quantitative modelling that pairs time series forecasting with multicriteria decision analysis, using real-time conflict event data in Python. Application areas include oil and gas drilling, process safety, and international operations exposed to geopolitical and other external threats.

name: Kristin Helen Roll
summary: Kristin Helen Roll studies the economics of fisheries and aquaculture, especially Norwegian salmon and whitefish. Her work uses econometric methods such as difference-in-differences, cointegration, data envelopment analysis and productivity decomposition to examine fisheries management, market integration, trade, efficiency and energy use. She has also co-authored work on light pollution at high latitudes, welfare technology for dementia care, and the role of trust in the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: Kristoffer Andreas Auklend
summary: Kristoffer Andreas Auklend studies energy security and national security governance, focusing on how energy dependencies and critical infrastructure become targets of hybrid threats in a tense geopolitical environment. His work uses securitization and weaponization frameworks, case studies of the Norwegian petroleum sector, comparative analysis of Norway and Finland, document analysis and interviews with defense and industry actors. It addresses how legal and institutional arrangements assign security and resilience responsibilities to private companies, including for subsea pipelines.

name: Lasse Berg Andersen
summary: Lasse Berg Andersen works on environmental risk assessment for marine aquaculture, developing methods grounded in risk science that help stakeholders with different values reach a shared understanding of risk. His work has been tested in a study of environmental risk in Norwegian fish farming and applied in case studies of Atlantic cod farming, including structured analysis of the events and consequences involved in pathogen transmission. The emphasis is on risk analysis, evaluation and communication to support risk-informed decisions and governance.

name: Lisa Jean Watson
summary: Lisa Jean Watson works on geospatial and geoscience problems, using terrestrial laser scanning, ground-penetrating radar, drilling, remote sensing and machine learning to document archaeological sites, model urban subsurface geology and map peatland condition. She also applies spatial multi-criteria analysis to infrastructure planning, such as road by-pass alignment. In parallel, she leads education research with industry partners on the skills graduates need in the energy sector, including the effects of AI, and writes on the energy transition and subsurface teaching.

name: Lisbet Fjæran
summary: Lisbet Fjæran studies how risks are perceived, communicated and governed, with a focus on social amplification and attenuation of risk, the role of experts, and the idea of risk resonance. Her work uses conceptual and theoretical development, document analysis, literature and scoping reviews, and analysis of long-running survey data on public trust in the Norwegian government. Application areas include crisis management, risk communication, youth climate perceptions, adolescent health messaging, petroleum safety regulation, and sustainability in local education policy.

name: Lund Øystein Bø
summary: Lund Øystein Bø is the author of a 2023 publication, written in Norwegian, that looks at the University of Stavanger (UiS), the region's identity as an energy capital and the move toward investing in nuclear power. Only the title is available, so the methods used are not stated. The work appears to concern energy policy and the role of a university in regional energy development.

name: Maria Korkou
summary: Maria Korkou studies urban green infrastructure and green spaces, focusing on how to measure and plan for their multiple functions and ecosystem services. Her work combines spatial assessment with indicator sets, correlation and multivariate analysis, systematic literature review with network analysis, and mixed methods including mapping, surveys, interviews and observations. Applications centre on Stavanger, Norway, covering city-wide green space planning and the use of green spaces by children and teachers for outdoor learning and sustainability education.

name: Marianne Nitter
summary: Marianne Nitter studies how sustainability and climate change are addressed in public policy and planning, using document analysis and stakeholder interviews. Her work covers how Norwegian municipalities express sustainable development and the Sustainable Development Goals in education plans, and how climate risk and vulnerability shape adaptation and urban planning in Longyearbyen, Svalbard. She also writes on climate change in relation to societal safety, threats and challenges.

name: Marja Katariina Ylönen
summary: Marja Katariina Ylönen studies risk, safety and security, with a focus on customs and border control, cross-sector cooperation in societal security, and organised crime such as smuggling. Her work builds conceptual frameworks, drawing on systems and organisational theory, and applies thematic and qualitative content analysis to court verdicts, diaries, interviews and reports. Application areas include the nuclear and Seveso chemical industries, the Norwegian petroleum sector, Svalbard, and customs education, alongside theoretical work on the foundations of risk science.

name: Martin Meggele Sjøen
summary: Martin Meggele Sjøen studies teacher education and the prevention of violent extremism in Norway and the Nordic countries. His work uses qualitative methods such as interviews, document and critical discourse analysis, and literature synthesis, alongside a longitudinal questionnaire study grounded in self-determination theory. Topics include how school practicums, international placements and ethics discussions shape student teachers, how security policy affects schools, and how immigrant parents experience early childhood education.

name: Morten Sommer
summary: Morten Sommer studies safety and risk management in settings of high uncertainty, with a strong focus on explosive remnants of war and dumped ammunition. His work combines qualitative case studies, interviews and document analysis with conceptual critiques of risk assessment methods, systems thinking and organisational resilience. He also examines organisational learning, emergency exercises and emergency preparedness analysis in police and emergency organisations, and learning and feedback in risk science education.

name: Najmeh Mozaffaree Pour
summary: Najmeh Mozaffaree Pour studies urban planning and spatial analysis, with a focus on proximity-based planning such as the 15-Minute City, land use change and urban expansion, and urban resilience. Her methods include GIS accessibility and network analysis, spatial regression, mobile network data, remote sensing with machine learning and cellular automata models, agent-based simulation, and multi-criteria decision-making. Case studies cover Tallinn, Tartu and wider Estonia, and the historic districts of Yazd, Iran, addressing health access, pedestrian safety, heritage resilience, software-industry location and neighborhood land governance.

name: Nita Santika
summary: Nita Santika studies international trade in seafood, using firm-level and highly disaggregated export data from Norway. Her work examines how exporters and importers respond to supply disruptions and uncertainty, including the Chilean salmon disease crisis and the Brexit referendum, and how regional clustering of exporters shapes export volumes, prices and new trade relationships. The studies apply empirical economic methods, including quasi-natural experiment designs, to questions about supply chain resilience in aquaculture and wild-harvest seafood.

name: Ole Andreas Hegland Engen
summary: Ole Andreas Hegland Engen studies how risk, safety and security are governed in Norway, with a focus on the petroleum sector, critical infrastructure and emerging industries such as seabed minerals. His work uses qualitative methods including interviews, document analysis, case comparison and conceptual analysis, drawing on polycentric governance and securitization frameworks. It also covers climate change adaptation and flood risk policy at national and municipal levels, as well as the effects of geopolitical tensions, total defence and artificial intelligence on regulation and ethics.

name: Olena Mykolajivna Koval
summary: Olena Mykolajivna Koval studies risk communication and decision making, with a focus on how authorities communicate health risks during the COVID-19 pandemic. Her work uses social media content analysis, scoping reviews and country-level case reporting, and also includes behavioural experiments on how couples and random groups make complex decisions under time pressure. Application areas include public health communication to immigrants and other vulnerable groups, national pandemic response governance in Norway, and tourism safety planning.

name: Ove Njå
summary: Ove Njå studies safety and risk in complex socio-technical systems, with a main focus on road tunnel fire safety, including how road users behave during evacuation, how risk communication supports learning, and whether shelters can serve as evacuation measures. His work also covers emergency response learning and surge capacity testing, safety regimes and rule bending in heavy goods transport, asset management, and social risk assessment and public perception of hydrogen energy. Methods include randomized controlled trials in a virtual reality driving simulator, longitudinal interviews, surveys, structural equation modelling, document and literature analysis, workshops, and system-theoretic process analysis.

name: Paulo Thiago Bastos Rocha
summary: Paulo Thiago Bastos Rocha studies how culture shapes behavior and institutions, using cross-national quantitative analyses of personality traits and perceived honesty alongside surveys, interviews and case studies. His applied work centers on Norwegian criminal justice and education, including rehabilitation of older inmates, collaboration between justice and welfare agencies, intercultural competence training for customs officers, and blended learning for international students. He also has work on civil society and environmental governance in the context of climate change.

name: Petter Osmundsen
summary: Petter Osmundsen studies the economics of petroleum and offshore wind, covering project profitability, cost development, taxation and investment decisions. His work uses econometric methods, including multivariate and quantile regression, together with project cash-flow case analysis, applied to the Norwegian continental shelf, UK offshore wind farms and U.S. oil and gas firms. Topics include fiscal regime design, capital rationing, business cycles, development concept choice and recovery rates, oil company moves into renewables, and policy responses to industry downturns.

name: Reidar Staupe-Delgado
summary: Reidar Staupe-Delgado studies disasters, natural hazards and slow-moving or creeping crises, with attention to how time, seasonality, anticipation and uncertainty shape risk and everyday life. His work uses conceptual analysis, case studies of communities in New Zealand, Norway and Sweden, and literature reviews and interviews, and covers coastal hazards, planned relocation, antimicrobial resistance and cross-disciplinary smart city research. It also considers how global crises and development agendas influence disaster risk planning.

name: Riana Steen
summary: Riana Steen studies safety, resilience and organizational learning in complex socio-technical systems, with applications in emergency response, oil and gas, aviation, policing, military drone operations and disaster management. Her work combines qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups and thematic analysis with systems-based approaches including the Functional Resonance Analysis Method, the Viable System Model and Bayesian belief networks, and in some cases natural language processing. The publications address accident investigation, adaptive capacity, sensemaking, competence development, business continuity and interorganizational collaboration, mostly in Norwegian settings.

name: Roger Flage
summary: Roger Flage works on the foundations of risk science, including how risk, uncertainty, probability and knowledge are conceptualized, characterized and communicated in risk assessment and decision-making. His work is mainly conceptual and methodological, covering frameworks for strength of justification, evolving assumptions, unpredictable events and dynamic risk management, and it also includes applied studies using spatial statistics and dispersion modelling. Application areas include power systems, vaccines, artificial intelligence and digital twins, deep-sea mining and offshore oil and gas.

name: Roy Endre Holsvik Dahl
summary: Roy Endre Holsvik Dahl studies how feedback on exam performance affects student learning, with a focus on risk science education at the University of Stavanger. His work applies expected utility theory in a theoretical analysis, and it suggests that giving students justification for their exam results does not always improve learning and may reduce it. The discussion is framed around risk science programmes but is intended to apply more widely in higher education.

name: Ruth Beatriz Pincinato
summary: Ruth Beatriz Pincinato studies the economics and management of fisheries and aquaculture, using econometric methods such as difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, demand and cointegration analysis, and structural modelling. Her work covers rights-based fisheries management, sea lice control and regulation in salmon farming, seafood trade and markets, and global comparisons of sustainability, gender participation and food security in seafood systems. She has also applied GIS and multi-criteria analysis to river restoration and floodplain reconnection for urban flood resilience in Brazil.

name: Ruth Østgaard Skotnes
summary: Ruth Østgaard Skotnes studies risk communication, safety and security management, and organisational resilience, with a focus on municipalities and critical infrastructure. Her work uses qualitative methods such as interviews and focus groups, alongside theoretical analysis, to examine who owns risk communication in Norwegian and Swedish local governments, how safety and security are co-managed in smart cities and cyber-physical systems, and how culture and communities of practice shape cyber resilience in oil and gas. She has also examined stakeholder perception and acceptance of hydrogen in Norway, and communication and governance questions around AI and digital ethics.

name: Sasan Zarghooni-Hoffmann
summary: Sasan Zarghooni-Hoffmann studies customs and border security within the wider field of societal security, drawing on systems theory, risk science, intelligence studies and criminology. The work uses conceptual framework development, thematic and crime script analysis of Norwegian court verdicts, and case studies such as those on Svalbard to examine cross-sector cooperation, how smugglers protect their operations, and how to assess the quality of intelligence assessments. Other publications address customs education and risk competence, indicators for telling suicides from accidental deaths on railways, security clearance, and encyclopedia entries on Norwegian customs procedures.

name: Seth David Guikema
summary: Seth David Guikema studies the risk and resilience of infrastructure and communities facing natural hazards, using statistical modeling, machine learning, Monte Carlo simulation, spatial analysis and smartphone location data. His work covers power, water and cellular networks, household recovery, access to essential services, school closures and building habitability after hurricanes, including climate-change projections and equity impacts. He also writes on AI and digital twins in risk analysis, drinking water risk assessment, and the effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on online sex advertising as a proxy for trafficking.

name: Sigbjørn Landazuri Tveteraas
summary: Sigbjørn Landazuri Tveteraas studies the economics of tourism and hospitality in Norway, including competition between Airbnb and hotels, regional crisis adaptation in tourism destinations, and the efficiency of hotel staffing and management practices. He applies econometric methods such as cointegration, threshold autoregressive models and stochastic frontier analysis, alongside survey, interview and case-study approaches. He also contributes work on seafood by-product use for fishmeal, fish oil and fertiliser, and on business models and incentives for sustainable growth.

name: Sindre Lorentzen
summary: Sindre Lorentzen studies the economics and project performance of offshore wind, with a focus on UK wind farms. Using econometric analysis of capital cost and capacity factor data, project profitability modelling and descriptive statistics of project activity data, the work examines cost drivers, learning effects, production over a wind farm's life cycle, oil company investment returns and construction productivity including pandemic disruption. The findings relate to energy industry investors, policymakers and project managers.

name: Sissel Haugdal Jore
summary: Sissel Haugdal Jore studies how safety and security are governed together, especially for hybrid threats, terrorism and critical infrastructure. Her work uses qualitative interviews, document and discourse analysis, and conceptual analysis, drawing on cases such as the Norwegian petroleum sector, seabed minerals, security guard services and urban counterterrorism. It addresses regulation, private-sector roles in national security, resilience, organisational culture and ethical tensions in tripartite cooperation.

name: Tegg Westbrook
summary: Tegg Westbrook studies radiofrequency interference, mainly jamming and spoofing of satellite navigation (GNSS) systems, and its security and geopolitical consequences. The publications use literature review, conceptual analysis and secondary sources such as media reports to examine threats to ships, aircraft, autonomous vehicles and critical infrastructure, along with the motives of state and non-state actors and a tiered scheme for categorising interference in Finland. A further strand covers urban planning, smart and 15-minute cities, emergency response and teaching methods for sustainable cities.

name: Terje Aven
summary: Terje Aven works on the foundations of risk science, focusing on how risk is conceptualized, described and judged in terms of uncertainty, knowledge strength, probability and potential surprises. His publications use conceptual analysis, framework development, practitioner interviews, text analysis and case illustrations (such as the Boeing 737 Max, 9/11 and the Bovaer controversy) to examine risk study quality, ethics and systemic factors. Application areas include safety science, public guidance such as United Nations risk assessment documents, economics and decision analysis, and risk governance and regulation.

name: Todor Milkov Kesarovski
summary: Todor Milkov Kesarovski studies urban density, accessibility and air quality, mainly in Stavanger and other large Norwegian cities. His work combines GIS network analysis, isochrone-based '10-minute city' measures, regression models and air quality monitoring data to examine access to services and open spaces, and links between pollution, population density and electric vehicle adoption. He has also carried out qualitative questionnaire and interview studies on kindergarten staff's awareness of air quality and how it is communicated to children.

name: Tonja Knapstad
summary: Tonja Knapstad studies road tunnel safety, focusing on how risk communication shapes road users' learning and evacuation behaviour in tunnel fires. Her work combines a randomized controlled trial in a virtual reality driving simulator with longitudinal interviews to assess short- and long-term learning from a national information campaign. She also examines tunnel safety management, concepts of risk and the use of virtual reality in training from systems and social construction perspectives.

name: Tore Markeset
summary: Tore Markeset works on operational risk, safety and asset management for oil and gas operations and power distribution infrastructure. His publications develop risk assessment models and frameworks using evidence reasoning, multi-criteria decision analysis (TOPSIS, AHP), fuzzy inference, fault tree and failure mode analysis, and time series forecasting. They are applied to well control in onshore drilling, overhead power cables, country risk mapping, and digitalized lifecycle management and life cycle costing of equipment.

top_coauthors.name: Samarakoon Mudiyansele Samindi Manjula K Samarakoon

name: Una Aarsheim Milje
summary: Una Aarsheim Milje studies how young people perceive climate change and why those perceptions often do not lead to climate action. Her work is a literature review drawing on many disciplines, organised thematically around the roles of knowledge, emotions, and social and cultural factors such as self- and collective efficacy, proximity, collaboration, and social identity. The work sits in climate risk research and suggests holistic frameworks for understanding youth risk perception and behaviour.

name: Abit Hoxha
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Abit Hoxha works on democracy, media and digital society, with publications covering threats to democratic systems, dark tourism in Kosovo, and the role of AI assistants in how audiences find news. The listed work points to attention to indicators and mechanisms of democratic erosion, digital approaches to contested heritage, and the implications of AI-mediated news for trust and public knowledge. The work is relevant to journalism, media policy and cultural heritage contexts.

name: Anders Vassenden
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Anders Vassenden is a sociologist who studies face-to-face interaction using Goffman's interaction order, ritual and stigma, applying it to ethnoracial stigmatisation, cross-status encounters and the self-presentation of privileged groups. His work draws on ethnography, qualitative and photo-elicitation interviews, and institutional ethnography, in studies of Norwegian Somali parents' fears of child protective services, class and taste, and migrants' dealings with the welfare administration and labour market. He also contributes to methodological and theoretical debates on how interviews can capture situations beyond the interview itself.

name: Ane Lyngstad Oltedal
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ane Lyngstad Oltedal works on documentary filmmaking as an artistic practice, with a focus on how filmmakers try to create an experience of truth for audiences. The single publication, a 2022 Norwegian-language work, suggests a practice-based, reflective approach within artistic research on documentary film. Her work is relevant to film production, film studies and discussions of truthfulness in non-fiction storytelling.

name: Angela Subedi
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Angela Subedi works on inhabitant participation in urban planning and development, with a focus on the relational side of co-research. Her 2025 publication examines how researchers and residents work together as partners in shared inquiry. The work applies to participatory approaches in city planning and community-engaged research.

name: Ann-Karin Tennås Holmen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ann-Karin Tennås Holmen studies governance, innovation and digital transformation in the public sector, with a focus on Norwegian municipalities and regional institutions. Her work uses case studies and analytical models drawing on institutional theory, metagovernance and network governance to examine how new ideas, collaborative platforms and digital infrastructure meet and reshape existing institutions. She also addresses legitimacy in municipal governance networks, regulation of digital backbone infrastructure, public health partnerships and methods for co-research.

name: Benjamin Ronald Silvester
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Benjamin Ronald Silvester studies energy and sustainability transitions, with a focus on cross-border electricity interconnection and grid integration in the North Sea and Norway's role in European decarbonisation. His work draws on human geography and state theory, using conceptual frameworks and case analysis to examine the political, economic and technological conditions that shape transitions. Other publications address energy communities and the debates around carbon capture, utilisation and storage, including a case study of an industrial plant in Norway.

name: Bjørn-Tore Blindheim
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Bjørn-Tore Blindheim works on organisation and leadership in the context of the Anthropocene, developing a nature-oriented theory of organisation as a response to climate and nature challenges. His essays and public conversations draw on Norwegian social thought and on local examples, such as how households in Røldal used the landscape before hydropower development and how new hydropower plans change people's attachment to place. His work also engages grassroots movements and the green transition.

name: Büşra Yalçın öz-Uçan
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Büşra Yalçın öz-Uçan studies gender-based violence and intimate partner violence from a feminist and intersectional perspective, with particular attention to technology-facilitated violence, digital inequalities and online disclosure. Her work mainly uses qualitative interviews, thematic and grounded theory analysis, participatory visual methods, and scoping and rapid reviews. It covers survivors and service practitioners in Norway, Türkiye and Canada, including migrant and queer survivors, and addresses help-seeking, services, policy and research ethics.

name: Carlo Michael Knotz
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Carlo Michael Knotz studies public attitudes towards the welfare state, focusing on who is seen as deserving of benefits and services such as childcare, student finance and pandemic aid, and on how attitudes towards immigrants, psychological predispositions and technological change shape policy preferences and party support. His work relies mainly on original survey, vignette and conjoint experiments run across many countries in Europe, North America and the OECD, and he also compares welfare conditionality rules between OECD and Latin American countries. The findings relate to social policy design, immigration and integration, labour markets and the politics of the populist right.

name: Cato Wittusen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Cato Wittusen studies how professionals and expert organizations exercise agency when complying with institutional rules, working within organizational institutionalism and practice theory. His conceptual, philosophical approach draws on Wittgenstein's ideas about rule-following and on Kantian thought to distinguish routine compliance from more reflective compliance in difficult cases. The work applies to professional expertise in rule-governed organizations and regulatory settings.

name: Cecilie Larsen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Cecilie Larsen studies how wind-power development on Fosen/Fovsen in Norway has been framed in news media and public debate, focusing on conflict with Southern Sámi reindeer husbandry. Using discourse analysis and theories of settler colonialism, she examines news coverage from 2006 to 2023 to show how competing narratives justify or contest renewable energy infrastructure and shape the position of Sámi livelihoods in the green transition. She has also written on Sámi rights and human rights in the Fosen case in a public debate piece.

name: Dian Liu
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Dian Liu studies higher education and schooling, with work on gender and career advancement among female academics, internationalization and tuition policy in Norway, and workplace bullying among university staff. Other publications examine teacher burnout and school culture in China, digital parenting, and the concept of habitus in education, using surveys, interviews, case studies and systematic or umbrella reviews. Further work covers graduate and student entrepreneurship and sustainable campus development in China's Greater Bay Area.

name: Elin Merethe Oftedal
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Elin Merethe Oftedal studies how users, especially older adults, are included in innovation, with a focus on healthcare and digital health technologies. Her work uses interviews, focus groups, surveys and case studies to examine technology adoption, user motivation, living labs and responsible innovation in companies and public-private settings. She also researches sustainable innovation and carbon capture and utilisation, including the role of universities and industry in turning CO2 into a resource.

name: Elisabeth Lund Engebretsen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Elisabeth Lund Engebretsen studies gender, sexuality and queer politics, with a focus on anti-gender campaigns, online attacks on academics, and feminist and LGBTQ+ activism in the Nordic region and China. Her work uses case studies, discourse and content analysis of social media, and edited volumes, and draws on feminist, queer and postcolonial theory. It also covers Indigenous Sámi climate activism, settler colonialism, and practical guidance on gender and sexuality diversity in academia.

name: Ellen Jenny Torgersen Ravndal
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ellen Jenny Torgersen Ravndal studies the history and politics of international organisations, with a focus on the United Nations, its secretaries-general and the early years of the organisation under Trygve Lie. Her work also covers the 19th-century origins of intergovernmental organisations, including how empires, colonies and semi-sovereign states took part in them, using archival research and a new partial dataset on membership. She also contributes to public discussion of UN relevance and reform, the Cold War, and imperial legacies in the North Sea region.

name: Espen Mathiesen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Espen Mathiesen works on journalism, with publications covering both the foundations of journalistic practice across media platforms and the use of artificial intelligence in Norwegian newsrooms. His work appears to address how news production is carried out and how new technology is taken up in editorial settings. The application domain is the Norwegian news media and journalism education.

name: Ezgi Pehlivanli Kadayifci
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ezgi Pehlivanli Kadayifci is a sociologist who studies academic life and gender studies under neoliberal and illiberal conditions, including scholars' well-being, academic freedom, online harassment and what she terms academic sustainability. Her work also covers Turkish politics and populism, such as the Canal Istanbul dispute, and gender, the body and digital culture, including circumcision ceremonies on social media, caesarean birth preferences, anti-vaccine discourse and martial arts as leisure. She mainly uses qualitative methods, including in-depth interviews, content analysis of social media posts and critical literature review.

name: Feodosiya Pavlovna Ermakova
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Feodosiya Pavlovna Ermakova studies how quality in higher education can be understood as something created through educational practice rather than fixed by measurement. Her doctoral work draws on a qualitative study of work placement courses in social science programs, reading the empirical material alongside Dewey's and Bakhtin's ideas of experience, dialogue and inquiry, and critiques quality management traditions that treat education as a production process. The work is relevant to university quality systems, work-integrated learning and collaboration between students, staff and external organizations.

name: Fredrik Dahle Vedholm
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Geir Sverre Braut
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Geir Sverre Braut's publications cover patient safety and health-system preparedness, along with clinical and biomarker studies. He uses national surveys, interviews, focus groups, simulation-based surge capacity tests and registry and compensation-claim analyses to examine hospital and prehospital major-incident readiness, surgical checklists, nursing home leadership, informed consent, appendicitis training and malpractice claims, and safety regimes in road transport. He has also carried out controlled blood-marker studies of long-COVID fatigue and inflammation, as well as work on childbirth experience and Y chromosome variants in COVID-19 mortality.

name: Gunnar Thesen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Gunnar Thesen studies political communication and party competition, focusing on how news media cover parties, politicians and interest groups and how that coverage relates to electoral outcomes. His work uses large collections of newspaper articles, often analysed with computational text methods and combined with survey, polling and parliamentary speech data, across countries such as Denmark, the Netherlands, Norway and the United Kingdom. Topics include newspaper political leanings, the media costs of governing, gender bias in politicians' news visibility, and radical right and green party success.

name: Hallgeir Skretting
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Hallgeir Skretting works on documentary filmmaking, with publications on how to make a film about leprosy and on using archive footage as source material for new documentaries. He also writes about internationalisation and academic responsibility in higher education. The publications point to practice-based and reflective approaches to film production and to university collaboration across borders.

name: Hande Eslen Ziya
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Hande Eslen Ziya studies gender, populism and online extremism, using qualitative analysis of incel forums, manosphere humour and avatar images alongside discourse comparisons of right-wing populism in Turkey, Hungary and Sweden. She also researches academic freedom and online violence against scholars through interviews and a prototype-based method, and examines women's parliamentary careers and trust in universities using statistical models and survey data. Further work covers migrant teachers' access to the profession and migrant workers' skills and mobility in Norway, and the visual culture of protest.

name: Hans Eirik Voktor
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Hans Eirik Voktor studies documentary film, with a focus on the portrait genre and the relationship between the filmmaker, the person portrayed and the audience. His work uses an auto-ethnographic method, examining his own artistic practice as a director and analysing a film portrait of a painter as a case. It addresses dialogue as a working method in filmmaking and the ethical challenges that come with it.

name: Helle Sjøvaag
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Helle Sjøvaag studies the political economy of news and communication media, focusing on platform and AI dependency, market concentration and digital infrastructure in the Nordic countries and Europe. Her work combines conceptual and institutional theory with revenue and concentration data, discourse analysis, interviews, tracker analysis and survey data, and she has also developed a whiteboard method for interviewing media technologists. Application areas include local journalism, public service and commercial news media, backbone infrastructure governance, smart city and municipal data practices, and AI's implications for democratic elections.

name: Ingvil Førland Hellstrand
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ingvil Førland Hellstrand studies how technology, care and gender are imagined in science fiction, art, policy documents and everyday settings, using feminist theory, care ethics and interpretive reading of films, novels and government reports. Her empirical work includes interviews, a visual matrix method, a scoping review and a curated art exhibition, applied to care robots, welfare technology in nursing homes and conversational AI. She also writes on feminist pedagogy and posthuman thought in gender studies education.

name: Iryna Fyshchuk
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Iryna Fyshchuk studies digital transformation and cybersecurity in Ukrainian public administration, with a focus on local authorities in newly formed communities (hromadas) during the war with Russia. Her work relies mainly on semi-structured interviews with public officials, alongside policy analysis of EU-Ukraine cooperation programmes and decentralisation support. It covers the resource, staffing, skills and coordination challenges of managing cyberattacks and digitalisation, and the national and international measures that address them.

name: Janina Jasper
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Janina Jasper studies how the governance and institutional design of electricity markets shapes demand-side flexibility in energy transitions. Her work uses institutional theory and qualitative analysis of policy and regulatory frameworks in a multi-sited comparison of the Netherlands and Japan. It looks at who can participate in flexibility schemes and how costs and benefits are distributed, with relevance for energy policy and market design.

name: Janne Tjensvoll Stangeland
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Janne Tjensvoll Stangeland works on journalism and media communication, covering both the practical and theoretical sides of editorial work across platforms. Her publications also deal with credibility, trust, lying and rhetoric in language, and with the possible influence of social media influencers on audiences. The work appears to be oriented toward teaching and public-facing discussion in Norwegian.

name: Jens Kaae Fisker
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Jens Kaae Fisker studies participatory and inclusive urban and rural development, using futures-oriented workshops, participatory photography, utopian sketching, interviews and case studies, notably in Stavanger, Norway and the Danish countryside. His work draws on state and governance theory (including Jessop's strategic-relational approach) to examine the state's role in sustainability transitions and how marginalised local actors take part in governing rural places. He also researches rural quality of life and well-being, and applies this to planning, smart city and placemaking practice.

name: Kristian Skagen Ekeli
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Kristian Skagen Ekeli works in legal and political philosophy, with a focus on constitutional democracy, constitutional rights and how law can protect the interests of present and future generations. His publications use normative and conceptual argument to compare procedural and substantive constitutional environmental rights, weighing judicial enforcement against democratic and rule of law values. He also addresses the relationship between economic freedom and political freedom.

name: Kristiane Marie Fjær Lindland
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Kristiane Marie Fjær Lindland studies sustainable and smart urban development, with a focus on Stavanger as a Nordic case, using participatory and qualitative methods such as utopian future workshops, participatory photography and case studies. Her work draws on American Pragmatism and futures thinking to examine citizen participation, democracy, art, living labs and cross-case learning in urban transformation. She also applies related approaches to design processes, campus sustainability and social acceptance and energy justice in offshore wind.

name: Lene Myong
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Lene Myong researches race, coloniality and reproduction in the Nordic countries, with a focus on child removal, transnational adoption, surrogacy, marriage migration and anti-Black racism in Denmark and Norway. Her work is largely qualitative and theoretical, analysing legal, political and educational documents, literary texts and ethnographic material, and it develops concepts such as colonial care, severance, the biopolitics of parental access and reproductive hesitation. Application areas include family and migration policy, the Nordic welfare state, racism research and education, and climate-related reproductive politics.

name: Liv Sunnercrantz
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Liv Sunnercrantz studies populism and the radical right in Turkey, Hungary and the Nordic countries, with a focus on gender, anti-gender discourse, female party leadership and the role of experts. She uses discourse theory, rhetorical analysis and feminist perspectives, applied to political, media and social-media discourse and to biographical material. Her work also covers climate and fossil-fuel debates in Norway and just transitions, as well as the effects of the Russia-Ukraine war and elections on Nordic politics.

name: Martha Cecilia Chaves Villegas
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Martin Søyland
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Martin Søyland studies parliamentary politics, with a focus on the Norwegian Storting, including government–opposition conflict, party cohesion and discipline, and how MPs signal responsiveness to constituencies. His work applies computational text analysis such as word embeddings, sentiment analysis and named entity recognition to parliamentary questions. He also contributes to public discussion and edited publications on politics, democracy and human rights.

name: Mathias Klitgård
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Mathias Klitgård works in feminist and queer theory, bringing together queer theory, new materialism and historical materialism in an approach called queer materialism. Using theoretical and diffractive reading methods, the work examines topics such as queer and trans mental distress and social reproduction during COVID-19 lockdowns, the politics of nature in queer discourse, and oil, family abolition and climate transition. Further work covers sexualities and critiques of capital, and consent in sexual cultures such as queer nightlife.

name: Merete Hermansen Jonvik
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Merete Hermansen Jonvik studies how people encounter and take part in art, drawing on cultural sociology and ethnographic, interview and observation methods. Her work covers children's experiences of art encounters in schools through the Norwegian Cultural Rucksack programme, participation in art and urban development initiatives, and the role of art centres in the Norwegian art ecology. She also examines taste and moral boundaries using photo elicitation interviews, and has worked on performing arts projects for very young audiences.

name: Nadine Zoghbi
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Oluf Langhelle
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Oluf Langhelle studies the social and political dimensions of energy and sustainability transitions, with a strong focus on carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), including public acceptance in Poland and links to Norwegian maritime industries. His work also covers just transitions, energy communities, urban experimentation and the role of oil and gas in Norwegian climate and innovation policy. Methods shown include case studies, social research on community attitudes, and conceptual and critical analysis drawing on governance, geography and energy social science.

name: Ozan Félix Sousbois
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ozan Félix Sousbois studies masculinities, gender radicalisation and digital cultures, with a focus on incel and wider manosphere communities, including looksmaxxing, body modification, pain and loneliness. The work uses netnography, visual and digital ethnography, and qualitative analysis of forums, social media and avatar images, and also covers methodological and ethical issues for queer researchers in hostile fields. A second strand uses discourse analysis and interviews to examine political masculinity, populism and public Islam in Turkey, as well as manospheric nationalism in Norway.

name: Peter Mathias Lindkvist
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Peter Mathias Lindkvist studies energy communities and just energy transitions, drawing on human geography and energy social science. His work combines qualitative interview and grounded theory studies of leadership and stakeholder collaboration in Swedish and Greek energy communities with reports on social engagement campaigns and pilot deployments in EU projects. Application areas include community energy, urban sustainability projects, and policy and regulation for local energy initiatives.

name: Ragnhild Sofie Selstø
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ragnhild Sofie Selstø works on journalism, covering news writing, journalistic language, photography and editorial practice across media platforms. Her publications include a foundational textbook on journalism, a study of how media take part in the public debate on trans issues, and work on journalism in relation to Chinese domestic politics. She also addresses newsletter writing as a way of reaching readers, with applications in journalism education and newsroom practice.

name: Raul Ferrer Conill
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Raul Ferrer Conill studies media and communication, focusing on digital infrastructures, datafication and the position of journalism and public media within platform and data-driven systems. His work uses qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, co-creation whiteboard sessions and policy and legal analysis, alongside large-scale quantitative analysis of tracker and social media engagement data, with cases mainly from Scandinavia, plus China and Portugal. He also examines news engagement among young audiences, newsgames, journalistic norms, and science and health communication, including systematic and scoping reviews.

name: Renée Margaritha Scharnigg
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Renée Margaritha Scharnigg studies solar energy and energy community transitions in Portugal, drawing on sociotechnical and transition studies, policy analysis and justice perspectives. Her work uses interviews, fieldwork, media and document analysis, and scenario-based quantitative comparison of energy-sharing and metering rules. Topics include accountability of intermediaries and policymakers, gender and masculinities in energy imaginaries, the geopolitics of solar power and green hydrogen, and the trade-offs between fairness and efficiency in energy community design.

name: Siddharth Sareen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Siddharth Sareen studies the politics and governance of energy transitions, with a focus on solar power, energy communities and net-zero policy. His work uses qualitative methods such as fieldwork, interviews, visual ethnography, participatory ethnography and living labs, together with discourse and policy analysis. It covers case settings in India, Uganda, Norway and southern Europe and addresses justice, accountability, social inclusion and digitalisation in energy and mobility systems.

name: Sigmund Trageton
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Sigmund Trageton works on teaching methods in higher education, particularly media studies, and on artistic research in film. His publications describe a discussion-based teaching approach called Diskutek, using podcast production as assessment to strengthen student engagement and learning in the face of video meetings and ChatGPT. He also writes on fictional strategies such as reconstruction and dramatization in documentary film, and contributes a concept proposal for a park project.

name: Sindre Skjøld
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Stanislav Stedronsky
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Stanislav Stedronsky studies how higher education can support sustainability, focusing on the competencies students need to act as change agents in line with the Sustainable Development Goals. His work links Education for Sustainable Development with theories of sustainability transitions and uses an exploratory case study of Norwegian universities to identify obstacles to competence-based teaching. It also examines a novel simulation game as a practice-oriented teaching tool.

name: Terje Hillesund
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Terje Hillesund studies how people read, write and think with texts and digital technologies, using observational interviews and theories of embodied and distributed cognition, with a focus on scholarly reading and publishing habits among academics. He also writes on evolutionary and biological perspectives for sociology, covering gene-culture coevolution, non-genetic inheritance and debates over genomic methods in social science, along with commentary on Joseph Henrich's cultural theories. Much of his work also reaches the public through newspaper articles and commentary on reading, artificial intelligence and cognition.

name: Tevfik Murat Yildirim
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Tevfik Murat Yildirim is a political scientist who studies legislative behaviour, political communication, public opinion and gender in politics, with a strong focus on Turkey, the UK and the US. His work combines large-scale datasets, including parliamentary speeches, news coverage and decades of survey responses, with text coding, panel and regression models, causal designs such as difference-in-differences, and survey experiments. Application areas include voter turnout, women's political careers, media attention to politicians, emotive rhetoric, policy priorities, and partisan reactions to misinformation and elite cues.

name: Thomas Michael Sattich
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Thomas Michael Sattich studies the politics and geopolitics of the energy transition, including renewable energy competition, energy security in the Baltic Sea Region, and the social acceptance of carbon capture and storage. He also examines maritime and ocean affairs, covering shipping, maritime clusters, canals, digitalization and automation, using case studies and literature reviews. In education research, he develops and evaluates simulation games and competence-based teaching on climate negotiation and sustainability in universities.

name: Torvald Øgaard
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Torvald Øgaard studies tourist and visitor behaviour, including how perceived crowding and emotions shape satisfaction and loyalty at a ski resort, and how tourists judge risk, compare themselves with others and relate to tourist groups. His work uses survey-based studies as well as meta-analysis, such as a review linking workplace incivility to employees' turnover intentions. He also addresses the sustainability of cruise tourism as a route for destination development.

name: Turid Borgen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Turid Borgen researches documentary film and television, focusing on portrait documentaries, the relationship between filmmaker and subject, and the growing personal or intimate style in journalism and documentary storytelling. Her methods include auto-ethnographic study of her own filmmaking practice, film analysis, and analysis of personal TV documentaries, with attention to ethical questions. She also contributes to public debate on cultural policy, child welfare and media attention, and on internationalisation and academic responsibility in higher education.

name: Turid Rødne
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Ugo Corte
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ugo Corte is a sociologist who studies group life, culture and emotion, using ethnographic and other qualitative methods, with work on profanity in workplaces, cruelty as a form of group enjoyment, and the social worlds of big wave surfers. He also writes on theory-building and qualitative research practice, and on concepts such as anonymity, uncertainty and fateful moments. He has written essays engaging with the work of other sociologists, including Howard Becker, and has led workshops on qualitative methods and theorizing.

name: Xia Sun
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Xia Sun studies gender and career advancement in higher education, focusing on how female researchers in Norway navigate institutional policies, gender roles, relationships and personal goals. The work uses empowerment as an analytical framework and draws on interview data to examine how structural and individual factors shape recognition and progression. It is relevant to institutional policy design aimed at supporting women's academic careers.

name: Yonas Tesema Amaya
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Yonas Tesema Amaya studies labour, land and industrial development in Ethiopia and, more recently, industrial and urban energy transitions in Norway. His work uses ethnographic fieldwork, interviews and firm- and stakeholder-level case studies to examine worker exploitation, rural women's migration, land and labour dispossession, and fieldwork access in Ethiopian industrial parks, as well as decarbonization strategies, positive energy districts and stakeholder collaboration in Stavanger. The findings are aimed at informing policy on just labour conditions, net-zero transitions and sustainability transformation.

name: Aksel Leknes
summary: Aksel Leknes works on automated analysis of infant brain MRI, focusing on volumetry from ultra-low-field scanners that are more accessible in low- and middle-income settings. His publication presents an open-source segmentation pipeline built on age-specific templates and priors, checked against high-field MRI references using correlation and percentage-error measures across infant cohorts in South Africa and Uganda. The pipeline is applied to regional brain growth, sex differences and the effects of low birthweight in early development.

name: Aleksander Hagen Erga
summary: Aleksander Hagen Erga studies substance use disorders, particularly polysubstance use, using prospective longitudinal cohort studies in Norwegian treatment populations. His work covers how cognitive impairment, personality traits, childhood trauma, PTSD symptoms and drug-free friendships relate to recovery, psychological distress and life satisfaction, using regression, growth curve and dynamic structural equation models, and he leads a randomised trial protocol on dextroamphetamine substitution for amphetamine dependence.
