The publications cover credit card delinquency prediction from combined credit and debit data, store location and sales forecasting for retail chains, consumer perception of packaging design, and how the speed of export entry relates to new venture survival.

name: Babusi Clint Ngwenya
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Babusi Clint Ngwenya's publications span energy and industrial policy as well as theoretical physics. The policy work uses interviews and cost and emissions comparisons to assess heat pump policies for decarbonising building heating in Switzerland, and contributes to stakeholder workshops on battery and green industry development in Norwegian regions. The physics work uses lattice simulations of SU(3) gauge theory to study the Casimir potential for different boundary geometries and temperatures.

name: Bjørn Terje Asheim
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Bjørn Terje Asheim studies regional economic development and innovation, with a focus on how human agency, institutions and policy shape industrial change, diversification and sustainability transitions in regions. His work combines conceptual frameworks with qualitative methods such as interviews, case studies, policy document review and qualitative comparative analysis, drawing on Nordic regions, Norwegian oil and gas and maritime industries, and global production networks such as electric vehicle batteries. It addresses topics including green and just regional path development, transformative innovation policy, clusters, industrial districts and the changing geography of globalisation.

name: Carina Antonia Hallin
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Carina Antonia Hallin studies collective intelligence and its use in democratic governance and public policymaking, including how citizen knowledge can be gathered through digital deliberation platforms combined with artificial intelligence and natural language processing. Her work includes edited handbook volumes, conceptual and commentary pieces on digital disruption and democratic values, and case studies such as a Danish municipality and a UN global platform. She has also published an automated machine learning method that uses k-means clustering to assign new observations to data clusters for recommendation and decision support.

name: Carolin Nast
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Carolin Nast studies how science and innovation work, combining meta-research on whether findings in the social and behavioural sciences can be reproduced with research on science and innovation policy. Her methods include large-scale replication projects, structured elicitation of expert predictions, bibliometric analysis, survey data and time-series modelling of patent records. Application areas include research assessment during crises such as COVID-19, links between scientists and non-academic partners, and the effect of government R&D support on technological complexity.

name: Christine Lundberg
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Christine Lundberg studies popular culture tourism and fan travel, including destinations linked to films and books, and how these places develop and last over time. She also examines how retail chains and city centers adapt to crises, and how destination organisations collaborate digitally. Her work draws on interviews, fieldwork, scoping reviews and eye-tracking, in settings such as high streets, events and Nordic outdoor recreation.

name: Dahl Fitjar
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing

name: Espen Olsen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Espen Olsen studies organisational psychology, leadership and change management, with a focus on hospitals and other Norwegian workplaces. His work uses systematic reviews, large-scale surveys analysed with structural equation modelling, scale validation, longitudinal panel data and qualitative interviews to examine patient safety culture, organisational climate, job demands and resources, employee outcomes and compliance. Application areas include healthcare, schools, small businesses and offshore oil and gas, along with teaching texts on health, safety and environment management and decision-making in organisational change.

name: Farheen Naz
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Farheen Naz studies how digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data analytics and Industry 4.0 support smart manufacturing, resilient supply chains and sustainability. Her work combines systematic literature reviews, bibliometric analysis, structural topic modelling and meta-analysis with survey-based methods such as PLS-SEM, factor analysis, AHP and machine learning clustering. Application areas include preventive maintenance, green and carbon-neutral supply chains, circular economy, net zero, healthcare and fashion supply chains, sustainable agriculture, green consumer behaviour and renewable energy trends.

name: Fifi Tjan Kvalsvik
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Fifi Tjan Kvalsvik studies the health, frailty and everyday living conditions of older adults who live at home, with a focus on municipal health and care services in Norway. Her work combines interprofessional health needs assessment, pre-post study design, interviews (including dyadic interviews), conjoint experiments and thematic analysis. Application areas include early detection of frailty, nutrition and dietary behavior, online grocery shopping, loneliness and depression, and implementation of assessment practices in community care.

name: Gro Ellen Mathisen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Gro Ellen Mathisen studies how psychosocial work conditions relate to safety, well-being and performance, with a strong focus on high-risk industries such as Norway's offshore petroleum sector. Her work uses large national survey data, psychometric validation, systematic and narrative reviews, and interview and focus-group studies, often framed by the Job Demands-Resources model. Other application areas include digitalization of offshore work, older workers' occupational health, hospitality and software work environments, and frontline leadership in implementing clinical guidelines in mental health services.

name: Hilde Ness Sandvold
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing

name: Hong Li
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Hong Li studies participatory and service design, with applications in digital health, sustainable tourism and higher education. Her work uses case studies, mixed methods, journey mapping, workshops and art-based methods to engage stakeholders in designing and adopting services, including digital remote care for postoperative patients in China and Norway and tourism development in Finnish Sámi communities. She also examines challenge-based learning and student motivation and engagement in sustainability education.

name: Hongyan Shi
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Hongyan Shi studies pricing, product strategy and information decisions for firms and online platforms using game-theoretic analytical models. The publications examine whether a crowdsourcing platform should share style popularity information with artists who co-create products, and how technology for on-demand quality adjustments changes a firm's pricing and product-line choices under time-varying consumer needs. Outcomes analyzed include profit, consumer welfare and social welfare in digital and platform markets.

name: Huiwen Gong
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Huiwen Gong studies economic geography, focusing on regional development, global production networks and technological innovation systems, with particular attention to the electric vehicle battery industry in China and Europe. The work combines conceptual framework building with case studies, interviews and patent data analysis, covering topics such as geoeconomics, regional resilience, innovation policy, place leadership, interregional inequality and imaginaries of the future. Application areas include green and just industrial transitions, net-zero technology diffusion, development of peripheral regions, emerging industries such as blockchain, and regional policy in China, Switzerland and the US.

name: Huseyin Arasli
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Huseyin Arasli studies leadership, employee behavior and service quality in the hospitality and tourism sector, along with related areas such as corporate governance, marketing and airports. His work uses surveys analysed with structural and multilevel modelling, scale and index development, qualitative interviews, bibliometric reviews, and text and machine-learning analysis of online reviews and financial data. Applications include hotel workforce issues such as sabotage, incivility, job insecurity and fair work, responsible and spiritual leadership, service robots, green and Muslim-friendly hotels, Nordic airports and influencer marketing.

name: Jinghua Xie
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Jinghua Xie studies the economics of tourism and hospitality, with a focus on competition between Airbnb and hotels, hotel firm survival and financing, and the effects of seasonality and external shocks such as COVID-19. Using econometric methods including cointegration, threshold autoregressive, proportional hazards, panel data and logit models, along with survey and case study data, the work covers mainly Norway as well as whale watching destinations in Australia and Canada. Related publications examine tourist knowledge, interest and satisfaction, pro-environmental behaviour, consumer preferences for live fish in an emerging market, and the social costs of electricity use by time of day.

name: Kai Victor Myrnes-Hansen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Kai Victor Myrnes-Hansen researches smell disorders, telehealth and food and hospitality. He develops and validates questionnaires for parosmia, phantosmia and anosmia, and for practitioners' self-efficacy in video consultations, using expert interviews, Delphi methods, factor analysis and systematic reviews. He also studies meals and loneliness among older people, ageing consumers' expectations of institutional food, restaurant service and tipping, and working conditions in the Norwegian hospitality sector, using surveys, cluster analysis and focus groups.

name: Kjersti Berge Evensen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Kjersti Berge Evensen studies oral health and dental care for vulnerable groups, including people with dental anxiety or a history of abuse or torture, and prisoners. Her work uses questionnaires with regression and psychometric analysis, qualitative interviews with thematic and realist evaluation approaches, and literature reviews. She also examines health literacy, information sharing between health and kitchen personnel in hospitals and nursing homes, and how dental services are organised and delivered.

name: Kristina Nilsson Lindström
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Kristina Nilsson Lindström studies tourism development and governance, with a focus on popular culture tourism as a form of niche tourism in regional settings. Her work uses literature-based conceptual analysis to build a meta-governance framework for examining stakeholders, governance structures and strategies in the context of sustainability transition. She also writes on how people experience tourism in everyday life during periods of ongoing crisis.

name: Lukasz Andrzej Derdowski
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Lukasz Andrzej Derdowski studies workplace and consumer psychology, including how followers infer leaders' intentions and how psychosocial work factors relate to safety in high-risk industries. His work uses survey-based structural equation modeling, scale and index development, topic modeling of interviews, and systematic literature review. Application areas include responsible leadership, sustainable consumption, occupational safety, and organizational digitalization and school food programs in Norway.

name: Marte Cecilie Wilhelmsen Solheim
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Marte Cecilie Wilhelmsen Solheim studies innovation and entrepreneurship in Norway, with a focus on eco-innovation, digital innovation, business model change in oil and gas, and regional policy such as smart specialisation. Her work uses firm surveys, structural equation modelling, fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, interviews, case studies and literature reviews. She also examines gender, immigration and inclusion in venture capital, multinational careers, social entrepreneurship and higher education.

name: Matthew Mark Coffay
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Matthew Mark Coffay studies circular economy and sustainable business model innovation, including how circular business models emerge and how policy in the EU and California shapes company strategies in the United States. His work draws on interviews, workshops, case studies, literature review and design science to build frameworks and practitioner tools for organizational design, dynamic capabilities and circular experimentation. Further application areas include Norwegian aquaculture, CRISPR salmon innovation and responsible innovation for sustainability impact assessment.

name: Muzamil Farooq
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Muzamil Farooq studies how regional development can be examined through a future-oriented lens, moving beyond explanations based on path dependence and structural analysis. His work compares eight methodological approaches, grouped into three clusters and assessed by purpose, techniques, data needs and user suitability, to form a varied toolbox for regional futures research. The focus is on participatory and inclusive methods that bring out power dynamics and agency, with relevance to regional challenges such as inequality, climate change and social fragmentation.

name: Olga Gjerald
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Olga Gjerald studies organizational change and leadership, including how employees come to be ready for, resist or engage with change, and she contributes literature reviews and research agendas on these topics. She also researches hospitality and tourism work, covering fair work, trade unions, psychosocial risks, employment paradoxes and future work scenarios, using surveys, focus groups, comparative analysis and literature review. Further work uses survey-based and cluster analysis methods to examine consumer and visitor experience, such as crowding at ski resorts and ageing consumers' expectations of institutional food.

name: Ragnar Tveterås
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Ragnar Tveterås studies the economics of seafood and natural resource industries, with a strong focus on Norwegian salmon aquaculture. His work uses demand system models, hedonic price models, cost and profit-persistence models, panel data, and sustainability indicator datasets to examine consumer preferences, industry clusters and agglomeration, disease and environmental regulation, farm productivity, and offshore production economics. He also applies similar economic methods to global fisheries and aquaculture performance, petroleum resource rent taxation, and the financial effects of corporate carbon emission reductions.

name: Raj Kharel
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Raj Kharel studies fiscal devolution and the economic resilience of subnational governments, with a focus on Nepal's local municipalities during and after the Covid-19 pandemic. His work analyses how local government spending, internally raised revenue, and conditional and unconditional intergovernmental transfers relate to local resilience in rural and semi-urban areas. The findings are relevant to public finance design and decentralisation policy in developing countries with limited local administrative capacity.

name: Reidar Johan Mykletun
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Reidar Johan Mykletun studies how organizations can support older workers and extend working lives, using cross-national survey data, scale development and necessary condition analysis to examine human resource practices and cultural context. He also conducts research on hospital organisational climate and patient experience through systematic review, on the motivations of volunteer tourists on organic farms through large-scale surveys, and on responsible and sustainable approaches in business schools.

name: Robert Kreuzbauer
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Robert Kreuzbauer studies how generative AI can be built into business education to strengthen strategic decision-making. His work proposes a two-phase hybrid teaching approach, first training students in economic modeling such as profit optimization and incentive analysis without AI, then using GenAI to refine and test those models. It draws on student surveys and qualitative feedback from undergraduate, graduate and executive courses, and extends the ideas to AI-augmented learning in organizations.

name: Ronald Adalbert Boschma
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Ronald Boschma studies how regional economies evolve, diversify into new industries, technologies and occupations, and why some regions become stuck in development traps while others upgrade. His work applies evolutionary economic geography concepts of relatedness, economic complexity and institutional complementarities, using patent, industry, occupation and value-chain data on European regions plus studies of Brazil and the Netherlands. It informs regional innovation and Smart Specialisation policy, regional inequality and the role of interregional linkages and global value chains.

name: Rune Dahl Fitjar
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Rune Dahl Fitjar studies regional economic development and innovation, with a focus on university-industry collaboration, the regional role of universities, and how innovation and R&D funding contribute to spatial inequality. His work uses surveys of firms and academics, linked employer-employee and regional statistics, systematic literature reviews, structural equation models and qualitative comparative analysis. It covers Norway, the Nordic countries, Europe and Brazil, and addresses regional diversification, the role of agency and trust, and innovation and regional policy such as Smart Specialisation.

name: Rune Todnem By
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Rune Todnem By studies organizational change, leadership and ethics, with a focus on challenging conventional leadership thinking and on how people respond to change at work. His publications are mainly conceptual and edited-volume contributions that examine purpose-driven and collective leadership, stakeholder capitalism, design thinking, and hierarchy and bureaucracy. Application areas include sustainability-oriented organizations, business schools and higher education, and management practice.

name: Sigbjørn Barlaup Pedersen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing

name: Silje Haus-Reve
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Silje Haus-Reve studies regional economic development and industrial transition, with a focus on how regions and firms diversify into new activities, including the shift of Norway's oil and gas sector toward offshore wind, aquaculture and other green industries. Her work uses interviews, qualitative comparative analysis, document review and linked employer-employee and survey data to examine relatedness of industries and occupations, agency and opportunity spaces in Nordic regions, and firm-level learning and knowledge transfer. It also addresses regional innovation policy, clusters and societal challenges, and she has contributed Norwegian-language commentary and regional reports on transition and place-based policy.

name: Tatiana Aleksandrovna Iakovleva
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Tatiana Aleksandrovna Iakovleva studies responsible and user-inclusive innovation, with a strong focus on digital healthcare and welfare services, startups and living labs. Her work uses qualitative case studies, interviews, participatory dialogues and registry-based matching, with surveys and structural equation modelling in some studies, to examine stakeholder engagement, accelerators, and adoption of eHealth by elderly consumers. She also researches higher education topics such as challenge-based learning, university-industry collaboration and sustainability teaching, as well as creativity in small firms and governance of generative AI.

name: Thomas Laudal
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Thomas Laudal studies circular economy adoption in the construction industry, using surveys of professionals and qualitative case evidence to examine stakeholder views on costs, benefits, barriers and regulation. His work also covers servitization and economies of scale in 'everything as a service' business models, and responsible innovation in regulated public-private markets such as home care equipment. Further publications address sustainability teaching in business schools and a qualitative interview study of simulation-based pandemic preparation in a Norwegian hospital.

name: Thomas William Galliver
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Thomas William Galliver works on regional industrial development and the growth of battery value chains in Norway, with a focus on the Trøndelag region. The publication describes a stakeholder workshop, run within the PowerPlay project, that brought together companies, public bodies and researchers to discuss opportunities and barriers for green industry in the face of global competition and geopolitical uncertainty. His work is relevant to regional economic diversification and the green industrial transition.

name: Tom Broekel
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Tom Broekel studies the geography of innovation and regional economic development, with a focus on technological complexity, relatedness, knowledge networks and regional innovation systems. His work combines patent, employer-employee, geolocated turbine and large-scale text data with spatial regression, survival models, vector autoregressions and wavelet analysis. Application areas include innovation and Smart Specialisation policy, local acceptance of wind energy in Germany, regional news sentiment and how universities communicate the Sustainable Development Goals.

name: Tone Therese Linge
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Tone Therese Linge studies leadership and employment conditions in the hospitality industry, with a focus on fair work, trade unions, workplace abuse and harassment, and the future of hospitality work. Her work uses surveys, qualitative interviews, topic modeling, literature reviews and scenario development, including Nordic leadership values, internal crisis communication during Covid-19, and a new survey-based index of followers' inferred responsible leadership intentions. The findings are relevant to hospitality employers, unions and policymakers in Norway and the other Nordic countries.

name: Tord Ludvigsen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Tord Ludvigsen works on offshore salmon aquaculture, combining engineering models of dissolved oxygen in sea cages with economic analysis of production strategies. His publications use computational fluid dynamics simulations in OpenFOAM, a faster theoretical model checked against CFD-level accuracy, and measured metocean data from an offshore site to estimate hypoxia risk, stocking density limits and maximum biomass for cages of different sizes. A further study compares offshore production strategies in terms of capital cost, capacity utilization and profitability.

name: Trude Furunes
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Trude Furunes studies work and aging, occupational health and safety, and workplace conditions, with a focus on older workers, sustainable employability and age discrimination. Her work uses qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups and narratives, as well as surveys, two-wave panel studies with structural equation modelling, and participatory action research, and draws on systems-based theory to evaluate complex workplace interventions. Application areas include healthcare and home nursing, the hospitality industry, retirement transitions and bridge employment, and work ability and employability in the Norwegian labour market.

name: Truls Eric Johan Engström
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Truls Eric Johan Engström studies tourism and outdoor recreation, including visitor motivations and segmentation in a heavily visited Norwegian coastal protected area, using survey data, factor analysis and cluster analysis to inform spatially differentiated management. His work also covers people and organisations in tourism, such as the work preferences of Generation Z tourism students and the role of personality in mentoring relationships. In addition, he has carried out a systematic literature review on human-centered approaches to digital technology in tourism and has commented on Norwegian tourism policy.

name: Veera Emilia Haavisto
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Veera Emilia Haavisto studies leadership and internal communication in the hospitality sector, with a focus on how "Nordic leadership" shows up in hotels and restaurants. She uses qualitative methods, including interviews and multiple case studies with managers and employees in the Nordic countries, to examine leadership values, work-life balance and crisis communication during COVID-19. Her work also appears in Norwegian-language outlets aimed at industry readers.

name: Veronica Isabel Blumenthal
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Veronica Isabel Blumenthal studies tourism and visitor experiences, including how immersion works in virtual and real-world attractions, why people choose not to take part in sharing economy exchanges, and what industry partners gain from student innovation camps. She also examines how universal design is covered in sustainable tourism labeling schemes and standards. Her work relies mainly on semi-structured interviews with thematic analysis, plus document coding, with a focus on Norwegian tourism contexts.

name: Xiangyu Quan
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Xiangyu Quan studies inter-organizational collaboration and innovation under uncertainty, with a focus on how geography and local embeddedness shape eco-innovation and firm resilience. The work uses survey data from Norwegian service firms and integrative literature reviews with content analysis, and covers green transition, smart city public-private partnerships and responses to COVID-19. Further publications include monitoring and evaluation reports for the Re-Value project and a study of participant behavior in online communities.

name: Åsa Helen Grahn
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Åsa Helen Grahn studies responsible and sustainable tourism, with a focus on practices in the Nordic countries and on how it can strengthen regional competitiveness. Her work also covers accessible tourism, including the quality of travel experiences for people with disabilities and a review of the research field. She additionally addresses social sustainability and human rights in the tourism industry, including the implications of Norway's Transparency Act for tourism businesses.

name: Åse Helene Bakkevig Dagsland
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Åse Helene Bakkevig Dagsland studies working conditions and staff retention in the Norwegian hospitality and wider service sectors, including occupational socialisation of apprentice chefs, workplace abuse, bullying and sexual harassment, and employee turnover. Her work uses interviews, surveys, cluster analysis and structural equation modelling, and includes cross-national comparisons with Australia and the Fair Work framework. She has also examined the supervisor role and training in customs officer education, and harassment prevention approaches used by industry and working life partners.

name: Øystein Jensen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Øystein Jensen studies tourism experiences and visitor attractions, with attention to how audiences and visitors perceive authenticity, local traditions and cultural content. His work uses qualitative case studies based on interviews and observation, alongside conceptual frameworks that describe the product components of managed visitor attractions from the supply side. Application settings include cultural performance centers in Uganda, wildlife camps in Kenya and the Arctic, and mountain tourism on Kilimanjaro.

name: Heidi Victoria Skeiseid
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: UiS School of Business and Law (department not stated)
summary: Heidi Victoria Skeiseid studies consumer behaviour and marketing, with work on how individuals reduce consumption for environmental sustainability, how sports are used to offset negative publicity, and how customers give feedback in food service. Her methods include literature reviews that build typologies and research propositions, survey-based structural equation modelling with an extended theory of planned behavior, and qualitative focus groups using cartoon prompts. Application areas include sustainable consumption policy, social marketing, hospitality and tourism, and hospitality education, including students' career aspirations.

name: Ron Boschma
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: UiS School of Business and Law (department not stated)
summary: Ron Boschma studies how regions develop, diversify and sometimes become stuck, using an evolutionary economic geography perspective centred on relatedness, economic complexity and institutions. His work combines econometric analysis of industry, patent and occupational data for European regions with conceptual frameworks and case-based mixed-methods studies. Application areas include regional development traps, regional inequality, Smart Specialisation and place-based innovation policy, global value chains, and circular economy transitions.

name: Åse Lea
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: UiS School of Business and Law (department not stated)
